===Denver Broncos===
====2014====
The [[Denver Broncos]] selected Roby in the first round (31st overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref name="c654">{{cite web | last=Gantt | first=Darin | title=Broncos take cornerback Bradley Roby | website=NBC Sports | date=2014-05-08 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/broncos-take-cornerback-bradley-roby | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref> He was the fifth cornerback selected in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Although the Bengals allegedly told Roby they would select him 24th overall during their pre-draft visit, they instead selected Darqueze Dennard who unexpectedly fell in the first round.<ref name="Bengals">{{Cite web |last=Marcum |first=Jason |date=June 28, 2017 |title=Bengals told Bradley Roby they were taking him in 2014 NFL Draft |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2017/6/28/15881996/bengals-bradley-roby-2014-nfl-draft |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=cincyjungle.com}}</ref> The [[San Diego Chargers]] also showed serious interest in Roby, but both teams chose to select different cornerbacks following his arrest, with the Chargers selecting [[Jason Verrett]] (25th overall) and the Bengals selecting [[Darqueze Dennard]] (24th overall).<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 5, 2014 |title=Ex-Ohio State CB Roby: I would love to play for the Chargers |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bradley-roby-to-chargers-it-s-time-for-them-to-get-a-great-corn-0ap2000000339609 |access-date=February 3, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Head coach [[John Fox (American football)|John Fox]] stated Roby likely fell due to character concerns.

On June 10, 2014, the Broncos signed Roby to a four–year, $6.95 million contract that included $5.58 million guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] of $3.37 million.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Bradley Roby contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/denver-broncos/bradley-roby-14440/ |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], he competed against [[Chris Harris Jr.]], [[Tony Carter (cornerback)|Tony Carter]], and [[Kayvon Webster]] for the starting cornerback role.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 3, 2014 |title=Denver Broncos 2014 Training Camp Profile: Bradley Roby |url=http://www.rantsports.com/nfl/2014/06/03/denver-broncos-2014-training-camp-profile-bradley-roby/ |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=rantsports.com}}</ref> Fox named Roby the third cornerback on the depth chart to start the 2014 season, behind veterans [[Aqib Talib]] and Chris Harris Jr.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2014 |title=Broncos roster cuts: A final Denver Broncos depth chart projection |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/broncos-roster-cuts-final-denver-163003470.html |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=yahoo.com |archive-date=February 2, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202072256/https://www.yahoo.com/amphtml/sports/news/broncos-roster-cuts-final-denver-163003470.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Broncos' season-opener against the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and recorded a season-high seven solo tackles and three pass deflections during their 31–24 victory. Roby also made a key deflection while covering [[Reggie Wayne]] in the fourth quarter to seal the victory for the Broncos. In Week 6, Roby made three combined tackles, two pass deflections, and had his first career sack on [[New York Jets]] quarterback [[Geno Smith]] in the Broncos' 31–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 6-2014: Denver Broncos @ New York Jets |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014101206/2014/REG6/broncos@jets |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On November 2, 2014, Roby recorded two combined tackles, two pass deflections, a forced fumble, and had his first career interception off a pass attempt by [[New England Patriots]] quarterback [[Tom Brady]] in the Broncos' 43–21 loss. The following week, he collected four combined tackles, defended two passes, and intercepted [[Derek Carr]] during a 41–17 win against the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 20-2015: Denver Broncos @ Oakland Raiders |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014110907/2014/REG10/broncos@raiders |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On November 23, 2014, Roby earned his first career start and had four solo tackles and a pass deflection during a 39–36 victory against the [[Miami Dolphins]]. Roby finished his rookie season in {{NFL Year|2014}} with a career-high 65 combined tackles (63 solo), 13 pass deflections, two interceptions, one sack, and a forced fumble in 16 games and two starts.<ref name="stats14">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley Roby (2014) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleyroby/2543505/gamelogs?season=2014 |access-date=February 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Broncos finished first in the [[AFC West]] with a 12–4 record, clinching a playoff berth. On January 11, 2015, Roby appeared in his first career playoff game and recorded two solo tackles, a pass deflection, and intercepted [[Andrew Luck]] during a 24–13 loss to the Colts in the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] Divisional round.<ref name="stats14" /> The Broncos and head coach John Fox agreed to part ways during the offseason.

====2015====
[[File:Chris harris bradley roby autographs.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Roby along with [[Chris Harris Jr.]] signing autographs in 2015]]
Newly appointed head coach [[Gary Kubiak]] named Roby the starting nickelback and the third cornerback on the team behind Aqib Talib and Chris Harris Jr to begin the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Broncos Depth Chart |url=http://gridironorange.com/broncos-depth-chart/ |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=gridironorange.com}}</ref>

In Week 2, Roby returned a fumble by [[Jamaal Charles]] for a touchdown in the final seconds of the fourth quarter to give the Broncos a 31–24 victory over the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. The following week, he made two solo tackles, deflected a pass, and intercepted [[Matthew Stafford]] during the Broncos' 24–12 victory at the [[Detroit Lions]]. On December 20, 2015, Roby tied his season-high with five solo tackles in a 34–27 loss at the Steelers. He finished the {{NFL Year|2015}} season with 40 combined tackles (34 solo), ten pass deflections, an interception, and a fumble recovery in 16 games and four starts.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley Roby (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleyroby/2543505/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=NFL.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202190838/http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleyroby/2543505/gamelogs?season=2015|archive-date=February 2, 2018}}</ref> The Broncos' secondary ranked first in overall grade by Pro Football Focus and was named the "No Fly Zone". Roby received an overall grade of 81.0 by PFF in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stockwell |first=Ben |date=September 1, 2016 |title=2016 Cheat sheet: Denver Broncos |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/pro-2016-cheat-sheet-denver-broncos |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

The Broncos finished first in their division with a 12–4 record and received a first round bye. On January 17, 2016, he made three solo tackles and forced a key fumble by Steelers' running back [[Fitzgerald Toussaint]] to set up a go-ahead touchdown drive by the Broncos and defeat the Steelers. The following week, he intercepted a tipped pass by teammate [[Aqib Talib]] on a two-point conversion to preserve a fourth-quarter 20–18 victory over the Patriots.<ref>{{cite web | title=Denver Broncos Hang On, Defeat New England Patriots 20-18 In AFC Title Game | website=CBS News - Philadelphia |agency=Associated Press| date=2016-01-24 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/denver-broncos-hang-on-defeat-new-england-patriots-20-18-in-afc-title-game/ | access-date=2026-03-14}}</ref> On February 7, 2016, Roby appeared in [[Super Bowl 50]] and recorded two solo tackles and three pass deflections in the Broncos' 24–10 victory over the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl 50 - Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers - February 7th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201602070den.htm |access-date=August 31, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl 50 - National Football League Game Summary |url=http://www.nfl.com/liveupdate/gamecenter/56834/DEN_Gamebook.pdf |access-date=August 7, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2016====
Roby remained the third cornerback under defensive coordinator [[Wade Phillips]] for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelberman |first=Zach |date=September 3, 2016 |title=Updated Broncos depth chart after final cuts |url=https://www.247sports.com/nfl/denver-broncos/Bolt/Updated-Denver-Broncos-depth-chart-after-final-cuts-47182752/Amp |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}{{dead link|date=January 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On October 30, 2016, Roby recorded a season-high seven combined tackles, deflected two passes, and returned an interception off [[Philip Rivers]] for a 49-yard touchdown during a 27–19 victory over the Chargers. It marked the first time Roby returned an interception for a touchdown. In Week 13, he collected three solo tackle, defended two passes, and returned an interception by [[Blake Bortles]] for a 51-yard touchdown in Denver's 20–10 win at the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. Roby finished the season with 39 combined tackles (34 solo), eight pass deflections, two interceptions, two touchdowns, and a sack in 16 games and four starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley Roby (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleyroby/2543505/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Without quarterback [[Peyton Manning]] leading the offense, the Broncos finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season third in the AFC West with a 9–7 record and did not qualify for the playoffs. Kubiak retired after the season, citing issues with his health. The Broncos' secondary was ranked fourth by [[Pro Football Focus]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 18, 2017 |title=Ranking all 32 NFL teams' secondaries heading into the 2017 season |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/pro-ranking-all-32-nfl-teams-secondaries-heading-into-the-2017-season |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref> Pro Football Focus gave Roby an overall grade of 58.9, ranking him 83rd among cornerbacks in 2016.<ref name="Bengals" />

====2017====
[[File:Bradley Roby 2017.jpg|thumb|Roby with the Denver Broncos in 2017]]
On April 18, 2017, the Broncos announced they exercised the fifth-year, $8.52 million option on Roby's rookie contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jhabvala, Nicki |date=April 18, 2017 |title=Broncos expected to pick up Bradley Roby's fifth-year contract option |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2017/04/18/broncos-bradley-roby-fifth-year-contract-option/ |website=DenverPost.com}}</ref> Roby remained the third cornerback behind Talib and Harris under new head coach [[Vance Joseph]] to start the 2017 regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Tim |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Broncos release first depth chart of regular season |url=https://www.milehighreport.com/2017/9/3/16249298/broncos-first-depth-chart-of-regular-season |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=milehighreport.com}}</ref>

He played in the Broncos' season-opener against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' and recorded five combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass attempt by quarterback [[Philip Rivers]] to set up a touchdown drive by the Broncos in their 24–21 comeback victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers at Denver Broncos - September 11th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709110den.htm |access-date=October 7, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> On November 5, 2017, Roby recorded a season-high five solo tackles and deflected a pass during a 51–23 loss at the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He finished the {{NFL Year|2017}} season with 42 combined tackles (35 solo), a career-high 17 pass deflections, an interception, and one sack in 16 games and four starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley Roby (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleyroby/2543505/gamelogs |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Roby played in 64 consecutive games and did not miss a game over the course of four seasons. The Broncos finished last in the AFC West with a 5–11 record and did not qualify for the playoffs for the second season in a row. [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Roby an overall grade of 84.0 in 2017 and his grade ranked 25th among all cornerbacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: Bradley Roby |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/bradley-roby/8666 |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2018====

With Roby having impressed in his years as a backup, the general consensus heading into the 2018 season was that he was a high-quality defensive back deserving of a full-time starting role.<ref name=MHS>{{cite web|last=Segars|first=Zach|title=2018 Season Review: Should Denver Broncos retain Bradley Roby or let him go?|work=Mile High Sports|url=https://milehighsports.com/2018-season-review-should-the-broncos-retain-bradley-roby-or-let-him-go/|date=February 20, 2019|access-date=November 25, 2021}}</ref> This consensus convinced Broncos president of football operations [[John Elway]] to move on from Talib, trading him to the [[Los Angeles Rams|Rams]], and to promote Roby to one of Denver's two starting cornerbacks.<ref name=MHS/> However, Roby had a disappointing 2018 season, as his Pro Football Focus player grade plummeted to just 59.9.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: Bradley Roby 2018 Season Stats|url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/bradley-roby/8666?season=2018 |access-date=November 25, 2021 |work=Pro Football Focus}}</ref> His head coach publicly called him "inconsistent," and low point came when he was called out on national television in a December 24 ''Monday Night Football'' broadcast by commentator [[Jason Witten]] for perceived lack of effort.<ref>{{cite web|last=Legwold|first=Jeff|title=Former first-round pick Bradley Roby's future in Denver in question|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/denver-broncos/post/_/id/32747/former-first-round-pick-bradley-robys-future-in-denver-in-question|date=December 29, 2018|access-date=November 25, 2021}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On March 14, 2019, Roby signed a one-year, $10 million contract with the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Texans sign free agent CB Bradley Roby |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-free-agent-cb-bradley-roby |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>
Roby made his debut with the Texans in week 1 against the [[New Orleans Saints]].  In the game, Roby made 9 tackles in the 30–28 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2019 |title=Lutz's 58-yard field goal lifts Saints over Texans, 30-28 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128021 |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>
In week 13 against the [[New England Patriots]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'', Roby recorded his first interception of the season off a pass thrown by [[Tom Brady]] and returned it for 22 yards during the 28–22 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Watson throws 3 TDs, catches another; Texans top Pats 28-22 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127967 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>
In week 16 against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Roby intercepted a pass thrown by [[Jameis Winston]] and returned it for a 27-yard touchdown during the 23–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 21, 2019 |title=Texans win AFC South title with victory over Bucs |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127901 |access-date=December 21, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On April 3, 2020, Roby signed a three-year, $36 million contract with the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weston |first=Matt |date=March 15, 2020 |title=Houston Texans Re-Sign Bradley Roby To Three-Year Contract |url=https://www.battleredblog.com/2020/3/15/21180932/2020-nfl-free-agency-houston-texans-re-sign-bradley-roby-to-three-year-contract |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=Battle Red Blog |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>
In Week 6 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], Roby recorded his first interception of the season off a pass thrown by [[Ryan Tannehill]] during the 42–36 overtime loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Tennessee Titans - October 18th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010180oti.htm |access-date=October 20, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On November 30, 2020, Roby was suspended six games for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing drug policy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=November 30, 2020 |title=Texans' Fuller, Roby banned six games for PEDs |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30423848/houston-texans-wr-fuller-suspended-six-games-ped-policy |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On September 8, 2021, Roby was traded to the Saints in exchange for a 2022 third round selection and a conditional 2023 sixth round selection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=September 8, 2021 |title=Texans trading CB Bradley Roby to Saints |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/texans-trading-cb-bradley-roby-to-saints |access-date=September 9, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On November 25, he recorded his first interception as a Saint and of the season against Josh Allen and the Bills in a 31–6 loss on Thanksgiving.<ref>{{cite web | last=Sigler | first=John | title=Watch: Bradley Roby picks off Bills QB Josh Allen for his first INT as a Saint | website=Saints Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2021-11-26 | url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/saints/2021/11/25/saints-vs-bills-highlights-bradley-roby-intercepts-josh-allen/80385027007/ | access-date=2026-03-14}}</ref>

Roby entered the 2022 season as a starting cornerback opposite [[Marshon Lattimore]]. He suffered an ankle injury in Week 7 and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 25, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sigler |first=John |date=October 25, 2022 |title=Saints send Bradley Roby to injured reserve, re-sign Keith Kirkwood |url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2022/10/25/saints-lose-bradley-roby-injured-reserve-nfl-keith-kirkwood/ |access-date=August 30, 2023 |website=Saints Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was activated on November 26.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Hendrix |first=John |date=November 26, 2022 |title=Saints Activate Penning and Roby from IR, Elevate Isaac Yiadom |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/saints-saturday-transactions-penning-roby-activated |access-date=August 30, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

On August 29, 2023, Roby was released by the Saints.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 29, 2023 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-53-reductions-2023-nfl-season |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia Eagles ===
On October 3, 2023, Roby signed with the [[practice squad]] of the Eagles after fielding interest from multiple teams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=October 3, 2023 |title=Report: Eagles agree to terms with Bradley Roby |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/report-eagles-agree-to-terms-with-bradley-roby |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=October 4, 2023 |title=Eagles sign Bradley Roby to the practice squad |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-bradley-roby-to-the-practice-squad |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on October 13, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 13, 2023 |title=Eagles sign Bradley Roby to the active roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-bradley-roby-to-the-active-roster |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Roby was raised by his mother, Betty Roby, in [[Suwanee, Georgia]], and admires her for raising him as a single mother. His father, James Roby, was not around during his childhood.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Axelrod |first=Ben |date=October 10, 2012 |title=Roby making his dreams a reality |url=https://ohiostate.rivals.com/news/roby-making-his-dreams-a-reality |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20250623070203/https://ohiostate.rivals.com/news/roby-making-his-dreams-a-reality |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref> He has a dog named Young Nino, and is good friends with [[Steve Atwater]] after growing up being friends with his son, Steve Atwater Jr.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bagelstein |first=Eddie |date=December 14, 2014 |title=Steve Atwater Has a Nickname for Bradley Roby's Mom |url=http://dailyupperdecker.com/2014/12/steve-atwater-has-a-nickname-for-bradley-robys-mom/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191130125548/http://dailyupperdecker.com/2014/12/steve-atwater-has-a-nickname-for-bradley-robys-mom/ |archive-date=November 30, 2019 |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=Daily Upper Decker}}</ref>

===Legal issues===
On July 24, 2013, Roby was arrested and charged with misdemeanor battery. The police report states that the [[Bloomington, Ohio|Bloomington Police]] responded to a call at 2:40AM at Dunkirk Bar. When they arrived, Roby was being detained by private security after an incident where he was removed from the establishment after he attempted to start a fight with another patron. Roby re-entered the establishment to try to find his friends and was stopped by security. While being confronted, he allegedly struck the security guard in the chest and was immediately taken down by force until police arrived.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lesmerises |first=Doug  |date=July 22, 2013 |title=Details emerge on arrest of Ohio State Buckeyes cornerback Bradley Roby |url=http://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2013/07/details_emerge_on_arrest_of_oh.html |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=Cleveland.com}}</ref> On August 21, 2013, the case was conditionally dismissed after Roby pleaded guilty to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and agreed to complete a pre-trial diversion program. Under the terms of the agreement, Roby was required to stay out of legal trouble until August 16, 2014.<ref name="OVI">{{Cite web |last=Breech |first=John |date=April 24, 2014 |title=2014 NFL Draft prospect CB Bradley Roby charged with OVI in Ohio |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/2014-nfl-draft-prospect-cb-bradley-roby-charged-with-ovi-in-ohio/ |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=cbssports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fornelli |first=Tom |date=August 21, 2013 |title=Charge against Ohio State's Bradley Roby dismissed |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/charge-against-ohio-states-bradley-roby-dismissed/ |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=cbssports.com}}</ref>

On April 20, 2014, Roby was charged with physical control of a motor vehicle while under the influence of drugs or alcohol from an incident that occurred on April 20. The police report filed with Franklin County court states [[Columbus, Ohio|Columbus Police]] responded to a call about a drunk driver of a [[Dodge Charger]] that nearly hit kids walking on the sidewalk. The officers arrived to find Roby passed out in the driver seat of his vehicle. After Roby did not respond to officers, they opened the door to the vehicle and smelled an alcohol like odor. It appeared Roby was under the influence after another officer responded and conducted a field sobriety test, which he failed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2014 |title=Former Ohio State University Buckeye Bradley Roby Charged With OVI |url=https://www.10tv.com/article/former-ohio-state-university-buckeye-bradley-roby-charged-ovi |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=10TV.com}}</ref><ref name="OVI" /> On April 29, 2014, Roby pleaded guilty to physical control of a motor vehicle while under the influence of drugs or alcohol and was charged with a suspended sentence of 180 days in jail. Under the terms of the sentence, he was required to attend a three-day driver intervention program and pay a $375 fine plus court costs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huguenin |first=Mike |date=April 29, 2014 |title=Bradley Roby pleads guilty, gets suspended sentence |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bradley-roby-pleads-guilty-gets-suspended-sentence-0ap2000000345120 |access-date=February 2, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

'''Bradley Wilson Sorensen ''' (born March 13, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Southern Utah Thunderbirds football|Southern Utah Thunderbirds]] and was selected by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the seventh round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.utsandiego.com/news/2013/apr/27/chargers-draft-brad-sorensen-philip-rivers/|title=Chargers close draft with QB Sorensen|first=Michael|last=Gehlken|date=April 27, 2013|work=[[U-T San Diego]]|accessdate=December 19, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
Sorensen redshirted at [[Brigham Young University]], but transferred to [[Southern Utah Thunderbirds football|Southern Utah]] to gain playing time. He started quarterback for the Thunderbirds from 2010 until 2012. He has the school's all-time records in passing yards (9,445) and touchdown passes (61). He also became the school's first 3,000-yard passer in a season, which he did all three years he played at SUU.

The [[San Diego Chargers]] selected Sorensen in the seventh round (221st overall) of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He became Southern Utah's first player to be selected in the [[NFL draft]] in school history. He was released on August 29, 2014.

Sorensen had a brief spell with the [[Tennessee Titans]] in September 2014, reuniting him with former Chargers Coach [[Ken Whisenhunt]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2014/09/24/titans-add-qb-brad-sorensen-to-practice-squad/16153697/|title=Titans add QB Brad Sorensen to practice squad|agency=Associated Press|date=Sep 24, 2014|accessdate=December 17, 2014}}</ref>

Following his release in Tennessee, he was re-signed to the Chargers practice squad in December 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2014/12/15/7398989/san-diego-chargers-place-ilb-donald-butler-on-ir-sign-qb-brad-sorensen|title=San Diego Chargers place ILB Donald Butler on IR, sign QB Brad Sorensen|first=John|last=Gennaro|date=Dec 15, 2014|accessdate=December 17, 2014}}</ref> He was released again from the Chargers on October 1, 2015. San Diego re-signed Sorensen to their practice squad on October 24. On December 12, 2015, he was promoted to the active roster. On December 14, Sorensen was waived. On December 16 he was re-signed by the Chargers. On December 17, he was once again waived. He was later re-signed on December 18 to the practice squad.<ref>Levine, Ben, [http://www.profootballrumors.com/minor-nfl-transactions-121915/ "Minor NFL Transactions: 12/19/15"], "profootballrumors.com", December 19, 2015</ref>

On August 20, 2016, Sorensen signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-Free-Agent-QB-Release-RB/b9191270-505e-4ccd-b7c2-a1b76f3f9689|title=Vikings Sign Free Agent QB Release RB|access-date=2016-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821173402/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-Free-Agent-QB-Release-RB/b9191270-505e-4ccd-b7c2-a1b76f3f9689|archive-date=2016-08-21|url-status=dead}}</ref>  He was released by the team on August 29, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://min.247sports.com/Bolt/JUST-IN-Vikings-make-first-wave-of-cuts-47043934|title=JUST IN: Vikings make first wave of cuts}}</ref>  After starting quarterback [[Teddy Bridgewater]] was injured during practice, the Vikings re-signed Sorensen. On September 3, 2016, he was released again by the Vikings when the team traded for [[Philadelphia Eagles]] quarterback [[Sam Bradford]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set 53-Man Roster|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Announce-Roster-Moves-Set-Roster/b567f012-ae55-4c9f-86c9-539cfb9231c6|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028041835/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Announce-Roster-Moves-Set-Roster/b567f012-ae55-4c9f-86c9-539cfb9231c6|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 28, 2016|website=Vikings.com|date=September 3, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sorensen was raised by his parents Corey and Roxanne in the city of Grand Terrace, California. Sorensen has four brothers named Trevan, Bryan, Cody, Daniel, and one sister named Emily. The youngest brother, [[Daniel Sorensen]], played [[college football]] for the [[2013 BYU Cougars football|2013 BYU Cougars]] and currently plays safety for the [[2022 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].

'''Bradley McDougald''' (born November 15, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas Jayhawks]] and was signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] as [[undrafted free agent]] in 2013. He has also played for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[New York Jets]], [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].

==College career==
McDougald originally committed to [[Ohio State University]] out of [[Dublin Scioto High School]] as a [[wide receiver]], but changed his commitment to the [[University of Kansas]]. Following his sophomore year, McDougald switched permanently to safety.
[[File:Bradley McDougald (121113-F-GY869-172) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|McDougald with [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]] in 2012]]

==Professional career==
McDougald attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] and completed all of the combine and positional drills. His overall combine performance was underwhelming and described as rough.<ref name="agency">{{Cite web |last=Culley |first=Stephen |date=February 10, 2017 |title=Could S Bradley McDougald be a 2017 NFL free agent target for the Bills? |url=https://www.billswire.usatoday.com/2017/02/10/could-s-bradley-mcdougald-be-a-2017-nfl-free-agent-target-for-the-bills/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211220206/http://billswire.usatoday.com/2017/02/10/could-s-bradley-mcdougald-be-a-2017-nfl-free-agent-target-for-the-bills/ |archive-date=February 11, 2017 |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=Bills Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On March 15, 2013, McDougald participated at Illinois' pro day and attempted to improve his 40-yard dash (4.51s), 20-yard dash (2.62s), 10-yard dash (1.63s), vertical jump (33"), and short shuttle (4.33s). At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, McDougald was projected to be a seventh round pick or priority undrafted free agent. He was ranked as the 12th best free safety in the draft by DraftScout.com.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bradley McDougald, DS #12 FS, Illinois |url=https://www.draftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=89693&draftyear=2013&genpos=FS |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=DraftScout.com |archive-date=July 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180729230544/https://www.draftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=89693&draftyear=2013&genpos=FS |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
====2013: Rookie year====
On April 29, 2013, the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] signed McDougald to a three-year, $1.48 million contract after he went undrafted in the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Agree to Terms with 13 Rookie Free Agents|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Agree-to-Terms-with-13-Rookie-Free-Agents/894184a2-8925-4158-90ef-f6d9fb072b9d|author=Ferrin, Reid|website=Chiefs.com|date=May 1, 2013|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107014322/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Agree-to-Terms-with-13-Rookie-Free-Agents/894184a2-8925-4158-90ef-f6d9fb072b9d|archive-date=November 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="overthecap">{{cite web |title=Overthecap.com: Bradley McDougald contract |url=https://overthecap.com/player/bradley-mcdougald/2516 |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=overthecap.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, McDougald competed for a roster spot as a backup safety against [[Quintin Demps]], [[Husain Abdullah]], [[Otha Foster]], [[Tysyn Hartman]], Greg Castillo, and Malcolm Bronson.<ref>{{cite web |title=Did the Kansas City Chiefs improve? S edition |url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2013/7/16/4527668/did-the-kansas-city-chiefs-improve-s-edition |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=arrowheadpride.com |author=Thorman, Joel |date=July 16, 2013}}</ref> McDougald had an impressive performance throughout the preseason and made 13 combined tackles (11 solo) and a pass deflection. On September 1, 2013, McDougald was released by the Kansas City Chiefs, but was re-signed two days later. Head coach [[Andy Reid]] named McDougald the fifth safety on the Chiefs' depth chart, behind [[Eric Berry]], [[Kendrick Lewis]], Husain Abdullah, and Quintin Demps.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/KC |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On September 16, 2013, the Kansas City Chiefs waived McDougald and re-signed him to the practice squad two days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Release S Bradley McDougald|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Release-S-Bradley-McDougald/3a52fd21-9101-4c2a-8caf-a7236db35bf0|author=Ferrin, Reid|website=Chiefs.com|date=September 16, 2013|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225131907/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Release-S-Bradley-McDougald/3a52fd21-9101-4c2a-8caf-a7236db35bf0|archive-date=February 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Makes Change to Practice Squad Roster|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Makes-Change-to-Practice-Squad-Roster/01cb7470-698f-4f43-afae-157e49ea004d|author=Ferrin, Reid|website=Chiefs.com|date=September 13, 2013|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225131913/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Makes-Change-to-Practice-Squad-Roster/01cb7470-698f-4f43-afae-157e49ea004d|archive-date=February 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 12, 2013, he was promoted to the Chiefs' active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Elevate McDougald, Place Kelce on IR|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Elevate-McDougald-Place-Kelce-on-IR/66b4ea50-35e7-48ca-893f-4a7354311c4e|author=Ferrin, Reid|website=Chiefs.com|date=October 12, 2013|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225131910/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Elevate-McDougald-Place-Kelce-on-IR/66b4ea50-35e7-48ca-893f-4a7354311c4e|archive-date=February 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following day, McDougald made his professional regular season debut in the [[2013 Kansas City Chiefs|Chiefs']] Week 3 victory against the [[2013 Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]]. On November 5, 2013, McDougald was waived by the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Activate Commings from IR, Waive McDougald|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Activate-Commings-from-IR-Waive-McDougald/265754b0-9080-4393-8ff0-a61344ef8b90|author=Ferrin, Reid|website=Chiefs.com|date=November 5, 2013|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107020417/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Activate-Commings-from-IR-Waive-McDougald/265754b0-9080-4393-8ff0-a61344ef8b90|archive-date=November 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> McDougald was inactive as a healthy scratch for five games and only appeared in one game during his stint with the Kansas City Chiefs.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On November 7, 2013, the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] claimed McDougald off of waivers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=November 6, 2013 |title=Bucs place Jeff Demps on IR, claim Bradley McDougald off waivers |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bucs-place-jeff-demps-on-ir-claim-bradley-mcdougald-off-waivers |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> The Buccaneers claimed him after starting free safety [[Dashon Goldson]] sustained a knee injury and was inactive for two games (Weeks 8–9).<ref>{{cite web |title=Dashon Goldson injury: Buccaneers safety out vs. Seahawks |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2013/11/2/5059622/dashon-goldson-out-buccaneers-seahawks |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=sbnation.com |author=Brady, James |date=November 2, 2013}}</ref> Head coach [[Greg Schiano]] named McDougald the backup free safety behind [[Kelcie McCray]] upon joining the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart: 12/01/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/153/TB |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> McDougald appeared in three games with the Buccaneers and appeared primarily on special teams. He was inactive as a healthy scratch for five of the seven regular season games.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley McDougald (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleymcdougald/2539243/gamelogs?season=2013 |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 30, 2013, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers fired head coach Greg Schiano and general manager [[Mark Dominik]] after they finished with a 4–12 record in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=Greg Schiano, GM Mark Dominik fired by Buccaneers |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/greg-schiano-gm-mark-dominik-fired-by-buccaneers-0ap2000000307039 |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=NFL.com |author=Rosenthal, Greg |date=December 30, 2013}}</ref>

====2014====
During training camp, McDougald competed for a roster spot as a backup safety against Kelcie McCray and [[Keith Tandy]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Buccaneers trade for guard Rishaw Johnson, send Kelcie McCray to the Chiefs |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2014/8/21/6053801/buccaneers-trade-for-guard-rishaw-johnson-send-kelcie-mccray-to-the |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=bucsnation.com |author=Howell, Leo |date=August 21, 2014}}</ref> Head coach [[Lovie Smith]] named McDougald the backup strong safety to start the regular season, behind [[Mark Barron]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart: 10/01/2014 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/164/TB |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On September 18, 2014, McDougald made one solo tackle during a 56–14 loss at the [[2014 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] in Week 3. McDougald made his first career regular season tackle on running back [[Devonta Freeman]] after a three-yard gain in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 3-2014: Tampa Bay Buccaneers @ Atlanta Falcons |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014091800/2014/REG3/buccaneers@falcons |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 28, 2014, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers traded starting strong safety Mark Barron to the [[2014 St. Louis Rams|St. Louis Rams]] for a fourth and a sixth round pick in the [[2015 NFL draft]]. McDougald remained the backup strong safety behind [[Major Wright]] after the Buccaneers traded Mark Barron.<ref>{{cite web  |title=Buccaneers trade safety Mark Barron to Rams for picks |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000419401/article/buccaneers-trade-safety-mark-barron-to-rams-for-picks |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029034101/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000419401/article/buccaneers-trade-safety-mark-barron-to-rams-for-picks |url-status=live |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=NFL.com |author=Sessler, Marc |date=October 28, 2014}}</ref> On November 30, 2014, McDougald earned his first career start after Major Wright injured his ribs and was inactive.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buccaneers vs. Packers Injuries: Major Wright out, Clinton McDonald, Mason Foster questionable |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2014/12/19/7422805/buccaneers-vs-packers-injuries-major-wright-out-clinton-mcdonald |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=bucsnation.com |author=Philipse, Sanders |date=December 19, 2014}}</ref> He made four solo tackles during the Buccaneers' 14–13 loss to the [[2014 Cincinnati Bengals|Cincinnati Bengals]] in Week 13. In Week 15, he collected a season-high 15 combined tackles (11 solo) during a 19–17 loss at the [[2014 Carolina Panthers|Carolina Panthers]]. On December 28, 2014, McDougald recorded four combined tackles, a season-high three pass deflections, and made his first career interception in a 23–20 loss to the [[2014 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]] in Week 17. McDougald intercepted a pass by Saints' quarterback [[Drew Brees]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 17-2014: New Orleans Saints @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014122810/2014/REG17/saints@buccaneers |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the [[2014 NFL season|2014 season]] with 50 combined tackles (40 solo), seven pass deflections, and an interception in 15 games and five starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley McDougald (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleymcdougald/2539243/careerstats |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2015====
[[File:Bradley McDougald.jpg|thumb|McDougald with the Buccaneers in 2015]]
On March 5, 2015, the Buccaneers extended a restricted free agent tender offers to McDougald.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jenkins, Lansanah, McDougald Re-Signed |url=http://knockoutradio.com/jenkins-lansanah-mcdougald-re-signed/ |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=knockoutradio.com |date=March 6, 2015 |archive-date=July 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730050617/http://knockoutradio.com/jenkins-lansanah-mcdougald-re-signed/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Buccaneers signed McDougald to a one-year, $585,000 contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Buccaneers re-sign Bradley McDougald, Danny Lansanah and Mike Jenkins|url=http://www.bucsnation.com/2015/3/5/8158067/buccaneers-re-sign-bradley-mcdougald-danny-lansanah-and-mike-jenkins|author=Philipse, Sander|website=BucsNation.com|date=March 5, 2015|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref>

During training camp, McDougald competed to be the starting free safety against [[Chris Conte]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=March 11, 2015 |title=Bucs set to release Dashon Goldson, sign Chris Conte |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bucs-set-to-release-dashon-goldson-sign-chris-conte-0ap3000000478355 |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Head coach Lovie Smith named McDougald the starting free safety to begin the 2015 regular season, alongside strong safety Major Wright.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart: 10/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/175/TB |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On October 11, 2015, McDougald recorded three combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made an interception during a 38–31 victory against the [[2015 Jacksonville Jaguars|Jacksonville Jaguars]]. McDougald intercepted a pass by Jaguars' quarterback [[Blake Bortles]], that was originally intended for tight end [[Marcedes Lewis]], during the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 5-2015: Jacksonville Jaguars @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015101104/2015/REG5/jaguars@buccaneers |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 16, he collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (ten solo) in the Buccaneers' 26–21 loss to the [[2015 Chicago Bears|Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley McDougald (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleymcdougald/2539243/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the [[2015 NFL season|2015 season]] with 87 combined tackles (67 solo), four pass deflections, and two interceptions in 16 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2016====
On January 6, 2016, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers fired head coach Lovie Smith after they finished with a 6–10 record in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=January 6, 2016 |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers fire Lovie Smith |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tampa-bay-buccaneers-fire-lovie-smith-0ap3000000618589 |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On March 9, 2016, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers assigned a second round tender to McDougald as a [[restricted free agent]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Buccaneers tender Bradley McDougald, Jacquies Smith, three others |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2016/3/9/11185890/buccaneers-tender-bradley-mcdougald-jacquies-smith-three-others |access-date=July 30, 2018 |author=Philipse, Sanders |date=March 9, 2016}}</ref> On April 5, 2016, McDougald accepted his one-year, $2.55 million restricted free agent tender.<ref>{{cite web|title=McDougald, DePaola Sign Tenders|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/McDougald-DePaola-Sign-Tenders/e09f81b4-0b4c-4257-ba22-51b526d0a460|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107031606/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/McDougald-DePaola-Sign-Tenders/e09f81b4-0b4c-4257-ba22-51b526d0a460|archive-date=November 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The Buccaneers promoted offensive coordinator [[Dirk Koetter]] to head coach and hired former [[2015 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons']] head coach [[Mike Smith (American football coach)|Mike Smith]] as their defensive coordinator. McDougald entered training camp slated as the starting free safety. Head coach Dirk Koetter officially named McDougald the starting free safety to start the season, alongside strong safety Chris Conte.<ref>{{cite web |title=Buccaneers'2016 depth chart: Vernon Hargreaves shares starting job |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2016/9/6/12814072/buccaneers-2016-depth-chart-vernon-hargreaves-shares-starting-job |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=bucsnation.com |author=Philipse, Sanders |date=September 6, 2016}}</ref>

In Week 4, he collected a season-high eight solo tackles during a 27–7 loss to the [[2016 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]]. On October 23, 2016, McDougald recorded seven combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made an interception in the Buccaneers' 34–17 victory at the [[2016 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]]. The following week, he tied his season-high of eight solo tackles and broke up a pass during a 30–24 loss to the [[2016 Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]] in Week 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Bradley McDougald (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradleymcdougald/2539243/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He started in all 16 games in [[2016 NFL season|2016]] and made a career-high 91 combined tackles (79 solo), ten pass deflections, and two interceptions.<ref name="career"/> Defensive coordinator Mike Smith installed a multiple coverage defense that required McDougald to play both strong safety and free safety.<ref name="agency" /> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave McDougald an overall grade of 79.0 in 2016.<ref name="s331">{{cite web | last=Kosko | first=John | title=Top 10 under-the-radar players about to hit free agency | website=PFF | date=2017-01-18 | url=https://www.pff.com/news/pro-top-10-under-the-radar-players-about-to-hit-free-agency | access-date=2024-12-29}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
====2017====
On March 22, 2017, the [[Seattle Seahawks]] signed McDougald to a one-year, $2 million contract with $750,000 guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=2017-03-22 |title=Bradley McDougald chooses a one-year deal with Seahawks |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bradley-mcdougald-chooses-a-one-year-deal-with-seahawks |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Seahawks agree to one-year deal with safety Bradley McDougald |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/18976613/seattle-seahawks-agree-one-year-deal-safety-bradley-mcdougald |access-date=July 29, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Kapadeia, Shia |date=March 22, 2017}}</ref>

Head coach [[Pete Carroll]] named McDougald the backup free safety, behind [[Earl Thomas (defensive back)|Earl Thomas]], to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Seattle Seahawks Depth Chart: 10/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/SEA |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 9, McDougald started at free safety in place of Earl Thomas after Thomas sustained a hamstring injury that sidelined him for two games. He became the starting strong safety for the remainder of the season in Week 11 after [[Kam Chancellor]] sustained a neck injury and was subsequently placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Why doctors say Chancellor and Avril's neck injuries could be career-threatening|url=https://q13fox.com/2017/11/29/after-neck-injuries-its-very-possible-avril-and-chancellor-will-never-play-football-again/ |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=q13fox.com}}</ref> On December 3, 2017, McDougald collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (seven solo) and two pass deflections during a 24–10 victory against the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 13.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Seattle Seahawks - December 3rd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712030sea.htm |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with 75 combined tackles (51 solo) and four pass deflections in 16 games and nine starts.<ref name="career"/> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave McDougald an overall grade of 77.3, which ranked 47th among all safeties in 2017.<ref name="Pff">{{cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: Bradley McDougald |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/bradley-mcdougald/8220 |access-date=July 30, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2018====
[[File:Bradley McDougald 2018.JPG|thumb|McDougald with the Seahawks in 2018]]
On March 12, 2018, the Seahawks re-signed McDougald to a three-year, $13.95 million contract with $6.50 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $4 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 12, 2018 |title=Seahawks extend safety Bradley McDougald |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/seahawks-extend-safety-bradley-mcdougald |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{cite web|title=Bradley McDougald contract|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/bradley-mcdougald-12835/|website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> In the Seahawks' 27–24 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]] in the season opener, he recorded his first career game with two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Richard |first=Dean E. S.  |last2=Mathews |first2=Liz |date=September 10, 2018 |title=Seahawks Player of the Game: Safety Bradley McDougald |url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/10/seahawks-player-of-the-game-safety-bradley-mcdougald/ |access-date=October 1, 2018 |website=Seahawks Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 74.7 from Pro a Football Focus, which ranked 22nd among all qualified safeties in 2018.<ref name="Pff"/>

====2019====
In week 2 against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], McDougald recorded his first interception of the season off [[Mason Rudolph (American football)|Mason Rudolph]] as the Seahawks won 28–26.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2019 |title=Wilson, Seahawks edge Steelers 28-26 as Roethlisberger exits |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128110 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>
In the NFC Wild Card game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], McDougald recorded a team high 11 tackles and sacked [[Carson Wentz]] once during the 17–9 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2020 |title=Wilson leads Seahawks past Eagles 17-9 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131039 |access-date=January 5, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

=== New York Jets ===
On July 25, 2020, McDougald, along with first- and third-round picks in the [[2021 NFL draft]] and a first-round selection in the [[2022 NFL draft]], was traded to the [[New York Jets]] in exchange for safety [[Jamal Adams]] and a fourth-round selection in the 2022 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=July 25, 2020 |title=Seahawks Acquire All-Pro Safety Jamal Adams In Trade With Jets |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-acquire-all-pro-safety-jamal-adams-in-trade-with-jets |access-date=July 27, 2020 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

McDougald made his debut with the Jets in Week 1 against the [[2020 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. During the game, McDougald recorded 8 tackles and recovered a fumble in the 27–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bills 27-17 Jets (Sep 13, 2020) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore/_/gameId/401220116 |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He suffered a shoulder injury in Week 7 and was placed on injured reserve on October 31, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=October 31, 2020 |title=Jets Place S Bradley McDougald on Injured Reserve; Activate CB Arthur Maulet |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-s-bradley-mcdougald-on-injured-reserve-activate-cb-arthur-maulet |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On August 16, 2021, McDougald signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|work=TennesseeTitans.com|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-add-veteran-safeties-clayton-geathers-and-bradley-mcdougald-part-ways-wit|title=Titans Add Veteran Safeties Clayton Geathers and Bradley McDougald, Part Ways With Four Others, in a Flurry of Roster Moves|date=August 16, 2021|accessdate=August 16, 2021|first=Jim|last=Wyatt}}</ref> He was released on September 7, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=September 7, 2021 |title=Titans Make Several Roster Moves On Roster, and Practice Squad |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-make-several-roster-moves-on-roster-and-practice-squad |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 13, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=September 13, 2021 |title=Titans Make a Number of Roster Moves, Including Adding TE MyCole Pruitt and DB Bradley McDougald to the Active Roster |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-make-a-number-of-roster-moves-including-adding-te-mycole-pruitt-and-db-br |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> He was released on September 21, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=September 21, 2021 |title=Titans Release Safety Bradley McDougald, DL Anthony Rush |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-safety-bradley-mcdougald-dl-anthony-rush |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On December 31, 2021, McDougald was signed to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2021 |title=Roster Moves: 2 coaches currently unavailable; 1 placed on COVID-19 list; 2 players signed |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-2-coaches-currently-unavailable-1-placed-on-covid-19-list-2-players |access-date=December 29, 2023 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on January 1, 2022 and returned to the practice squad on January 3, 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/bradley-mcdougald-mcdoubr01/transactions | title=Bradley McDougald | publisher=Footballdb.com | accessdate=May 30, 2024}}</ref>

'''Bradley Jerrill Marquez''' (born December 14, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]]. He is also a member of the [[New York Mets]] organization where he played minor league baseball from 2012 to 2013 and again in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbs7.com/content/sports/OHS-alum-Marquez-trading-in-his-NFL-pads-for-a-swing-at-the-MLB-508387591.html|title=OHS alum Marquez trading in his NFL pads for a swing at the MLB|date=April 10, 2019 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Marquez played high school football, ran [[Track and field|track]], and played [[baseball]] at [[Odessa High School (Texas)|Odessa High School]] in [[Odessa, Texas]]. He played football at the [[running back]] position, and baseball at the [[shortstop]] position. Marquez was ranked as a 4-star prospect by [[Scout.com]] and an All-American prospect by [[PrepStar College Recruiting]].  His father, Brad Givens, also played for Odessa High. As a sophomore, Marquez rushed 203 times for 1,743 yards and 21 touchdowns, earning ''[[Associated Press]]'' All-State 2nd Team honors.<ref name=LAJ>{{cite news|last=Williams|first=Don|title=Odessa standout pledges to Tech|access-date=May 12, 2014|newspaper=Lubbock Avalanche-Journal|date=May 7, 2010|url=http://www.redraiders.com/2010/05/07/odessa-standout-pledges-to-tech/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100510025902/http://www.redraiders.com/2010/05/07/odessa-standout-pledges-to-tech/|archive-date=May 10, 2010}}</ref> As a junior, Marquez rushed 77 times for 492 yards before being sidelined by an elbow tendon [[tearing|tear]]. During his senior year, Marquez accrued 2,210 rushing yards and 29 touchdowns, becoming the school's new all-time leading rusher.<ref name=TTU>{{cite web|title=Bradley Marquez Bio |url=http://www.texastech.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bradley_marquez_763543.html |publisher=Texas Tech University |access-date=May 12, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140513024029/http://www.texastech.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bradley_marquez_763543.html |archive-date=May 13, 2014 }}</ref>

Marquez accepted a scholarship to play football collegiately for [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech]] over several schools including the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]]. Additionally, Marquez was selected by the [[New York Mets]] in the 16th round of the [[2011 Major League Baseball draft]].<ref name=MetsMinors>{{cite web|last=Hyde|first=Toby|title=Brad Marquez Returns to Football; Leaves Money on the Table|url=http://metsminorleagueblog.com/uncategorized/brad-marquez-returns-to-football-leaves-money-on-the-table/|publisher=MetsMinors|access-date=May 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512213854/http://metsminorleagueblog.com/uncategorized/brad-marquez-returns-to-football-leaves-money-on-the-table/|archive-date=May 12, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Marquez's first season in the minors was cut short by a [[quadriceps]] injury.<ref name=MRT>{{cite news|last=Hull|first=Jonathan|title=TECH AT GRANDE: OHS grad Marquez working way back from knee injury|url=http://www.mrt.com/sports/article_687fe5c2-5755-5a7d-98a9-3d9ac7c80aed.html|access-date=May 12, 2014|newspaper=Midland Reporter-Telegram|date=April 6, 2013}}</ref>

==College football and baseball==

Selected in the 16th round of the 2011 Major League Draft, Marquez arranged a two-sport deal which allowed him to attend Texas Tech to play football while playing baseball for the [[Kingsport Mets]] in the spring. Marquez forfeited $250,000 of his $325,000 signing bonus by not choosing to play baseball full-time by September 15, 2013.<ref name=MetsMinors />

Marquez earned playing time in all 12 games, with 4 starts. In the season opening September 9, 2011 game against [[2011 Texas State Bobcats football team|Texas State]], Marquez caught his first receiving touchdown on a diving catch, becoming the first true freshman wide receiver to do so in a season opener for the school in 17 years.<ref name=TTU /> Marquez would finish the season contributing on special teams and at the receiver position, accruing 25 receptions for 240 yards with 1 receiving touchdown.

Marquez would play in 6 games during the [[2012 Texas Tech Red Raiders football team|2012 season]], before suffering a season ending knee injury in the October 13, 2012 upset against #5 [[2012 West Virginia Mountaineers football team|West Virginia]].<ref name=CollegeInjury>{{cite news|title=Texas Tech WR Bradley Marquez out for season after suffering knee injury vs. West Virginia|url=http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2012/10/texas-tech-wr-bradley-marquez-out-for-season-after-suffering-knee-injury-vs-west-virginia.html/|access-date=May 12, 2014|newspaper=Lubbock Avalanche-Journal|date=October 14, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512214842/http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2012/10/texas-tech-wr-bradley-marquez-out-for-season-after-suffering-knee-injury-vs-west-virginia.html/|archive-date=May 12, 2014}}</ref> Marquez earned Academic All-[[Big 12 Conference]] 1st Team honors following the season.

In 2013, Marquez started in all 13 games in his junior season. During the October 12, 2013 game against Iowa State, Marquez earned his first career 100-yard receiving game. Marquez would contribute in every game and ended the season with 49 receptions, 633 receiving yards, and six touchdowns. Marquez again earned Academic All-Big 12 Conference 1st Team honors, in addition to All-Big 12 honorable mention honors.<ref name=TTU />

Prior to the start of the 2014 season during spring football practices, Marquez announced that he would forgo playing minor league baseball in the summer to concentrate on football for his senior season.<ref name=SAEN>{{cite news|last=Griffin|first=Tim|title=Tech's Bradley Marquez will skip the minors to concentrate on football|url=http://blog.mysanantonio.com/big12/2014/03/techs-bradley-marquez-will-skip-the-minors-to-concentrate-on-football/|access-date=May 12, 2014|newspaper=San Antonio Express-News|date=March 31, 2014|archive-date=May 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512230038/http://blog.mysanantonio.com/big12/2014/03/techs-bradley-marquez-will-skip-the-minors-to-concentrate-on-football/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In March 2019, Marquez returned to the Mets at their minor league spring training camp.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://metsmerizedonline.com/2019/03/bradley-marquez-in-mets-minor-league-camp.html/|title = Bradley Marquez in Mets Minor League Camp | Metsmerized Online|date = March 15, 2019}}</ref> He was assigned to the [[Columbia Fireflies]] of the [[Class A (baseball)|Class A]] [[South Atlantic League]] on April 8<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1115347582073626624|user=Jacob_Resnick|title=Former NFL WR Bradley Marquez has been promoted to the Low-A Columbia Fireflies and will start in left field tonight. #Mets<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |date=April 8, 2019}}</ref> and made his first appearance since July 28, 2013 that night.

==Professional career==
===St. Louis / Los Angeles Rams===
Marquez signed with the [[St. Louis Rams]] after going undrafted in the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He played in all 16 games as a rookie with one start recording 13 receptions for 88 yards as well as contributing on special teams with 11 tackles.

In 2016, Marquez played in 14 games recording 3 receptions for 37 yards before being placed on injured reserve on December 23, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Place WR Bradley Marquez On I.R. & Promote Two|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/rams-place-wr-bradley-marquez-r-promote-two/|website=NFLTradeRumors.com|date=December 23, 2016}}</ref>

On August 7, 2017, Marquez was waived/injured by the Rams and placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thomas Passes Physical, Marquez Waived|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Thomas-Passes-Physical-Marquez-Waived/e7e38dc0-e689-4e67-8b80-c7986b436eda|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171119021625/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Thomas-Passes-Physical-Marquez-Waived/e7e38dc0-e689-4e67-8b80-c7986b436eda|archive-date=2017-11-19|author=Simmons, Myles|website=TheRams.com|date=August 7, 2017}}</ref> He was released by the Rams on November 6, 2017.

===Detroit Lions===
On November 10, 2017, Marquez was signed to the [[Detroit Lions]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions waive-injured T Greg Robinson|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-waive-injured-T-Greg-Robinson/afe2da5c-7570-4b2b-b538-252da010f30b|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180215085509/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-waive-injured-T-Greg-Robinson/afe2da5c-7570-4b2b-b538-252da010f30b|archive-date=2018-02-15|website=DetroitLions.com|date=November 10, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 27, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign WR Bradley Marquez and S Rolan Milligan to active roster|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-WR-Bradley-Marquez-and-S-Rolan-Milligan-to-active-roster/dc689f18-e158-43d1-9cd1-2f33d4d5ce12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201055645/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-WR-Bradley-Marquez-and-S-Rolan-Milligan-to-active-roster/dc689f18-e158-43d1-9cd1-2f33d4d5ce12|archive-date=2018-02-01|website=DetroitLions.com|date=November 27, 2017}}</ref>

On September 11, 2018, Marquez was waived by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions awarded OL Jamil Demby via waivers from Los Angeles Rams|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-awarded-ol-jamil-demby-via-waivers-from-los-angeles-rams|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 11, 2018}}</ref>

Marquez was born to Veronica Marquez and Brad Givens. He is an exercise and sports science major.<ref name=LAJ />

===Minnesota Vikings===
On April 28, 2013, Randle signed with the NFL's [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref>{{cite web | title=Former UNLV RB Bradley Randle signs with the Vikings| work= lasvegassun.com | date= April 28, 2013 | url=http://www.lasvegassun.com/news/2013/apr/28/former-rebel-john-lotulele-picked-seattle-non-draf/#axzz2XgFTYeyE|access-date=April 28, 2013}}</ref>  Randle was released by the Vikings on August 26, 2013 (along with 12 others) to get to a 75-man roster.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Craig |title=Vikings release 13 players |url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/vikings/221240701.html |work=StarTribune.com |publisher=Star Tribune |date=August 26, 2013 |access-date=August 26, 2013 }}</ref> On September 4, he was signed to the [[practice squad]], and then released on September 10. Finally, Randle was re-signed to the Vikings practice squad on December 11, where he remained.<ref>[https://twitter.com/Vikings/status/410806533660766208 Twitter / Vikings: Practice Squad Transaction: The #Vikings have signed RB Bradley Randle to the practice squad.]</ref> Randle was released on May 13, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Officially Sign 15 College Free Agents, Waive 4 Veterans|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Officially-Sign-15-College-Free-Agents-Waive-4-Veterans/c7c85501-1e72-4fee-8051-51917f516ce7?campaign=social_20140513_23835174|publisher=Vikings.com|access-date=May 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140515154206/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Officially-Sign-15-College-Free-Agents-Waive-4-Veterans/c7c85501-1e72-4fee-8051-51917f516ce7?campaign=social_20140513_23835174|archive-date=May 15, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===BC Lions===
Randle was signed by the [[BC Lions]] of the CFL on September 30, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bclions.com/roster/show/id/7513 |title=Bradley Randle |publisher=bclions.com |access-date=September 30, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006081644/http://www.bclions.com/roster/show/id/7513 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 }}</ref> He had only 2 carries during the 2014 regular season but he managed to gain 35 yards (19 and 16 yards each). He also returned 3 punts for a total of 9 yards (only 3 yards per return).

=== Winnipeg Blue Bombers ===
On March 9, 2015, Randle and the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] agreed to a contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.bluebombers.com/article/Blue-Bombers-Add-Running-Back|title = Blue Bombers Add Running Back|date = |website = Blue Bombers|publisher = |last = |first = |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150402185445/http://www.bluebombers.com/article/Blue-Bombers-Add-Running-Back|archive-date = April 2, 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref>

'''Brandin Tawan Cooks''' (born September 25, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors before being selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the first round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. Cooks has also played for the [[New England Patriots]], [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Houston Texans]], and [[Dallas Cowboys]].

==Early life==
Cooks was born in [[Stockton, California]], to Worth Cooks Sr. and Andrea (Glasper) Cooks on September 25, 1993. Worth Sr. died of a heart attack when Brandin was six years old and Cooks and his three brothers, Fred, Worth Jr., and Andre, were thereafter raised by their mother.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mays |first=Robert |date=May 7, 2014 |title=The Big Promise of Brandin Cooks |url=http://grantland.com/features/brandin-cooks-nfl-draft-oregon-state-wide-receiver/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508062436/http://grantland.com/features/brandin-cooks-nfl-draft-oregon-state-wide-receiver/ |archive-date=May 8, 2014 |access-date=November 2, 2017 |website=Grantland |language=en-US}}</ref> He attended [[Lincoln High School (Stockton, California)|Lincoln High School]] in Stockton, where he played [[high school football]] for the Trojans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2014 |title=Lincoln High School alum Brandin Cooks earning praise at New Orleans Saints camp |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2014/lincoln-high-school-alum-brandin-cooks-earning-praise-at-new-orleans-saints-camp |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406230348/http://usatodayhss.com/2014/lincoln-high-school-alum-brandin-cooks-earning-praise-at-new-orleans-saints-camp |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McBride |first=Jim |date=May 20, 2017 |title=How a few key decisions turned Brandin Cooks into a choice player |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/patriots/2017/05/20/how-few-key-decisions-turned-brandin-cooks-into-choice-player/zmeRWgsPW5aeiVtzNEl1tM/story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002181217/https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/patriots/2017/05/20/how-few-key-decisions-turned-brandin-cooks-into-choice-player/zmeRWgsPW5aeiVtzNEl1tM/story.html |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=BostonGlobe.com}}</ref> As a sophomore, Cooks recorded 29 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 600 yards and seven As a junior, he had 46 receptions for 783 yards and 10 touchdowns, while also collecting three [[interceptions]] on the defensive side of the ball. As a senior, Cooks had 66 receptions for 1,125 yards and 11 touchdowns. He was ranked by the [[Rivals.com]] recruiting network as the 26th-best wide receiver and the 240th overall prospect in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks – Yahoo! Sports |url=http://sports.yahoo.com/oregonstate/football/recruiting/player-Brandin-Cooks-113489 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150409102409/http://sports.yahoo.com/oregonstate/football/recruiting/player-Brandin-Cooks-113489 |archive-date=April 9, 2015 |access-date=April 2, 2017 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref> Cooks originally committed to play [[college football]] at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] but changed to [[Oregon State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Biggins |first=Greg |date=November 29, 2010 |title=WR Cooks flips from UCLA to Oregon State |url=http://insider.espn.go.com/college-football/blog/_/name/biggins_greg/id/5862353/brandin-cooks-flips-ucla-oregon-state |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002181214/http://insider.espn.com/college-football/blog/_/name/biggins_greg/id/5862353/brandin-cooks-flips-ucla-oregon-state |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=April 2, 2017 |website=ESPN.go.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Buker |first=Paul |date=September 23, 2011 |title=Beavers Insider: Brandin Cooks prepares to face UCLA, team he snubbed for Oregon State |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2011/09/beavers_insider_brandin_cooks.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427131758/https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2011/09/beavers_insider_brandin_cooks.html |archive-date=April 27, 2020 |access-date=April 2, 2017 |website=OregonLive.com}}</ref> In addition to football, he also played [[high school basketball|basketball]] and ran track in high school.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks |url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=883171 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312231514/http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=883171 |archive-date=March 12, 2017 |access-date=November 15, 2020 |website=Athletic.net |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Cooks played at Oregon State from 2011 to 2013 under head coach [[Mike Riley (American football)|Mike Riley]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oregon State Beavers Football Record By Year |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418032557/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/ |archive-date=April 18, 2018 |access-date=April 17, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2011 season===
Cooks made an immediate impact for Oregon State in their 3–9 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 Oregon State Beavers Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/2011.html |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=October 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007235113/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/2011.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Cooks recorded three receptions for 26 yards in the 29–28 loss in his collegiate debut against [[2011 Sacramento State Hornets football team|Sacramento State]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sacramento State at Oregon State Box Score, September 3, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-09-03-oregon-state.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829091601/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-09-03-oregon-state.html |archive-date=August 29, 2017 |access-date=April 23, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On October 15, against [[2011 BYU Cougars football team|BYU]], he had three receptions for 90 yards and his first collegiate receiving touchdown, which came on a 59-yard reception from quarterback [[Sean Mannion (American football)|Sean Mannion]], in the 38–28 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BYU at Oregon State Box Score, October 15, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-10-15-oregon-state.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002181237/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-10-15-oregon-state.html |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=April 23, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He played in all 12 games with three starts and recorded 31 receptions for 391 yards and three touchdowns. In addition, he returned [[Kickoff (gridiron football)|kickoffs]], averaging 22.4 yards per return on eight attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandin-cooks-1/gamelog/2011/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406231349/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandin-cooks-1/gamelog/2011/ |archive-date=April 6, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
