===New Orleans Saints===
====2014 season====
Cooks was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] as the 20th overall pick of the first round of the 2014 NFL draft; the Saints traded up from the 27th spot, giving their first and third-round picks to the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in return for Arizona's first-round pick, in order to get Cooks.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Farrar |first=Doug |date=May 8, 2014 |title=New Orleans Saints select Brandin Cooks No. 20 overall in the 2014 NFL draft |work=NFL.SI.com |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=http://nfl.si.com/2014/05/08/new-orleans-saints-select-brandin-cooks-2014-nfl-draft/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140511014842/http://nfl.si.com/2014/05/08/new-orleans-saints-select-brandin-cooks-2014-nfl-draft/ |archive-date=May 11, 2014}}</ref> Cooks was the highest drafted player out of Oregon State since [[Ken Carpenter (gridiron football)|Ken Carpenter]] went 13th overall in the first round of the [[1950 NFL draft]]. He was also the highest drafted wide receiver in school history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oregon St. Drafted Players/Alumni |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/oregonst/drafted.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190105043537/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/oregonst/drafted.htm |archive-date=January 5, 2019 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 18, 2014, the Saints signed Cooks to a four-year contract worth $8.3 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vargas |first=Ramon Antonio |date=May 30, 2014 |title=Saints sign No. 1 pick Brandin Cooks |url=http://theadvocate.com/sports/9209505-128/saints-sign-no-1-pick |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140518223753/http://theadvocate.com/sports/9209505-128/saints-sign-no-1-pick |archive-date=May 18, 2014 |access-date=April 14, 2020 |website=The Advocate}}</ref>

In his first NFL game, Cooks had seven receptions for 77 yards and a touchdown and had an 18-yard rush during a 37–34 overtime road loss to the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints wide receiver Brandin Cooks impresses in NFL debut |url=http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-game-highlights/0ap3000000376139/Brandin-Cooks-impresses-in-NFL-debut |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180926014621/http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-game-highlights/0ap3000000376139/Brandin-Cooks-impresses-in-NFL-debut |archive-date=September 26, 2018 ====2016 season====
Before the 2016 season, Cooks was pegged as a breakout candidate by [[ESPN]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoegler |first=Alex |date=August 24, 2016 |title=ESPN believes Brandin Cooks will break out |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/espn-believes-brandin-cooks-break-112928538.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224041856/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/espn-believes-brandin-cooks-break-112928538.html |archive-date=December 24, 2016 |access-date=April 2, 2017 |website=Yahoo.com}}</ref> He lived up to the pre-season hype when he recorded six receptions for 143 yards and two touchdowns and an 11-yard rush during the narrow season-opening 35–34 loss to the [[Oakland Raiders]]. Cooks caught a 98-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter to set the Saints' franchise record for the longest play from scrimmage.<ref name="98Yard">{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2016 |title=Drew Brees-to-Brandin Cooks 98-yard TD sets franchise marks |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/drew-brees-to-brandin-cooks-98-yard-td-sets-franchise-marks-17659429?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306042817/https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/drew-brees-to-brandin-cooks-98-yard-td-sets-franchise-marks-17659429?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=New Orleans Saints |language=en-US}}</ref> He, [[Willie Snead IV]], and rookie [[Michael Thomas (wide receiver, born 1993)|Michael Thomas]], finished the day with 373 receiving yards combined, the most ever by a New Orleans trio in a loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=September 12, 2016 |title=Saints' speedy receivers shred Raiders defenders in loss |url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2016/09/saints_wr_corps_use_speed_to_o.html#incart_river_mobile_index |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916183358/https://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2016/09/saints_wr_corps_use_speed_to_o.html |archive-date=September 16, 2016 |website=NOLA.com}}</ref> During a Week 6 41–38 victory against the Panthers, Cooks had seven receptions for 173 yards and an 87-yard touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints – October 16th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610160nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611132703/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610160nor.htm |archive-date=June 11, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

After a Week 12 49–21 victory over the [[Los Angeles Rams]], in which Cooks was not targeted for a single pass,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at New Orleans Saints – November 27th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611270nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200609041602/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611270nor.htm |archive-date=June 9, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> he voiced his frustration by saying, "Closed mouths don't get fed."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=December 2, 2016 |title=Brandin Cooks: 'Closed mouths don't get fed' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brandin-cooks-closed-mouths-don-t-get-fed-0ap3000000749802 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403042309/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000749802/article/brandin-cooks-closed-mouths-dont-get-fed |archive-date=April 3, 2017 |access-date=April 2, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Three weeks later against the Cardinals, Cooks caught seven passes for a career-high 186 yards and two touchdowns, one for 65 yards and one for 45 yards, in the 48–41 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 15, 2020 |title=New Orleans Saints at Arizona Cardinals – December 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180crd.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200310003055/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180crd.htm |archive-date=March 10, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/2016.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200420144141/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/2016.htm |archive-date=April 20, 2020 |access-date=April 26, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Cooks finished the 2016 season with 78 receptions for a then career-high in receiving yards with 1,173 and eight touchdowns in 16 games and 12 starts. He finished seventh in the NFL in receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Leaders and Leaderboards |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/leaders.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108041718/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/leaders.htm |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=January 18, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Although Cooks' targets dropped from 129 in 2015 to 117 in 2016, his 10.0 yards per target ranked sixth among NFL wide receivers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks Advanced Stats and Metrics Profile: Yards Per Target |url=http://www.playerprofiler.com/nfl/brandin-cooks |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170401060414/https://www.playerprofiler.com/nfl/brandin-cooks/ |archive-date=April 1, 2017 |access-date=April 9, 2017 |website=PlayerProfiler.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407053328/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2016/ |archive-date=April 7, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===

====2018 season====
On April 3, 2018, the Patriots traded Cooks and a fourth-round draft pick to the Rams for a first-round pick (used on [[Isaiah Wynn]]) and a sixth-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=April 3, 2018 |title=Rams acquire Brandin Cooks in trade with Patriots |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-acquire-brandin-cooks-in-trade-with-patriots-0ap3000000924657 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230041136/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000924657/article/rams-send-firstround-pick-to-patriots-for-brandin-cooks |archive-date=December 30, 2019 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108042100/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=November 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On July 17, Cooks signed a five-year, $81 million extension with the Rams with $50.5 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=July 17, 2018 |title=Rams' Brandin Cooks signs five-year, $81M extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-brandin-cooks-signs-five-year-81m-extension-0ap3000000940666 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416094644/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000940666/article/rams-brandin-cooks-signs-fiveyear-81m-extension |archive-date=April 16, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

In Week 2 against the Cardinals, Cooks had seven receptions for a season-high 159 yards in the 34–0 shutout victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reedy |first=Joe |date=September 16, 2018 |title=Rams 2–0 for first time since 2001 after blanking Cardinals |url=https://www.apnews.com/2784ac19e1c54c3799ea8f3185228e63 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004225944/https://www.apnews.com/2784ac19e1c54c3799ea8f3185228e63 |archive-date=October 4, 2018 |access-date=October 4, 2018 |website=AP News |language=en-US}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Cooks had seven receptions for 116 yards and a touchdown along with a 10-yard rush in the 38–31 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=September 28, 2018 |title=Rams' WRs show off against Thielen, Diggs as best unit in the NFL |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/28/nfl-los-angeles-rams-vikings-cooks-woods-kupp/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002181335/https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/28/nfl-los-angeles-rams-vikings-cooks-woods-kupp/ |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=October 11, 2018 |website=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 9, Cooks was set to face off against his former team in the Saints. Following his trade to the Rams, Saints' starting receiver [[Michael Thomas (wide receiver, born 1993)|Michael Thomas]] instigated an online feud with Cooks out of anger for his departure from New Orleans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newport |first=Kyle |date=March 6, 2017 |title=Saints WRs Mike Thomas, Brandin Cooks Appear to Be Involved in Twitter Mixup |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2696386-saints-wrs-mike-thomas-brandin-cooks-appear-to-be-involved-in-twitter-mixup |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gonzales |first=Maximo |date=April 4, 2018 |title=Saints news: Michael Thomas appears to throw shade at Brandin Cooks |url=https://clutchpoints.com/saints-news-michael-thomas-appears-throw-shade-former-teammate-brandin-cooks-rams-trade |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=ClutchPoints |language=en}}</ref> Cooks caught six receptions for 114 yards and a touchdown during the 45–35 road loss as Thomas in an effort to taunt Cooks and the Rams; would re enact [[Joe Horn]]'s cellphone celebration upon scoring his final touchdown of the game to secure the Saints the lead.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 10, 2018 |title=NFL fines Michael Thomas $30,000 for cell phone celebration |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/nfl-fines-michael-thomas-30000-for-cell-phone-celebration |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at New Orleans Saints – November 4th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811040nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200723191643/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811040nor.htm |archive-date=July 23, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], he had another great outing, catching ten passes for 100 yards and rushing for a nine-yard touchdown during the 36–31 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scurlock |first=Amanda |date=November 15, 2018 |title=The Rams Beat the Seahawks to Commit Season Sweep |url=https://lasentinel.net/the-rams-beat-the-seahawks-to-commit-season-sweep.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190701160025/https://lasentinel.net/the-rams-beat-the-seahawks-to-commit-season-sweep.html |archive-date=July 1, 2019 |access-date=July 1, 2019 |website=Los Angeles Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> The following week against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Cooks caught eight passes for 107 yards in the narrow 54–51 victory. In one of the [[2018 Kansas City Chiefs–Los Angeles Rams game|highest-scoring back-and-forth games in NFL history]], he helped convert a key first down on a 22-yard reception on the drive that put the Rams up for good.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Los Angeles Rams – November 19th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811190ram.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416153439/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811190ram.htm |archive-date=April 16, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Following a Week 12 bye, the Rams went on the road to face the Lions. During the 30–16 road victory, Cooks eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards on the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Detroit Lions – December 2nd, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812020det.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200723191747/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812020det.htm |archive-date=July 23, 2020 |access-date=April 15, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the process, he became the first player in NFL history with 1,000 receiving yards in three consecutive seasons with three different teams.<ref name="simmons" />

===Houston Texans===
On April 10, 2020, Cooks and a [[2022 NFL draft|2022]] fourth-round draft pick were traded to the Texans in exchange for the Texans second-round draft pick, which was later used on [[Van Jefferson]], in the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=April 10, 2020 |title=Rams agree to trade WR Brandin Cooks to Texans |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-agree-to-trade-wr-brandin-cooks-to-texans |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200410210613/https://www.therams.com/news/rams-agree-to-trade-wr-brandin-cooks-to-texans |archive-date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=April 14, 2020 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref>

====2020 season====
During Week 5 against the Jaguars, Cooks caught eight passes for 161 yards and his first touchdown as a Texan during the 30–14 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Houston Texans – October 11th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110htx.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115121337/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110htx.htm |archive-date=November 15, 2020 |access-date=October 11, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During Week 16 against the Bengals, Cooks recorded seven receptions for 141 yards and a touchdown in the 37–31 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans – December 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012270htx.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111155403/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012270htx.htm |archive-date=January 11, 2021 |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the regular-season finale against the Titans, he had 11 receptions for 166 yards and two touchdowns during the 41–38 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Houston Texans – January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030htx.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112052547/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030htx.htm |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |access-date=January 8, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Cooks finished the 2020 season with 81 receptions for 1,150 yards and six touchdowns in 15 games and starts as the Texans finished with a 4–12 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2020/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205153720/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2020/ |archive-date=February 5, 2021 |access-date=January 8, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 Houston Texans Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/htx/2020.htm |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 30, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221230110740/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/htx/2020.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> He joined [[Brandon Marshall]] as the only players in NFL history to record a 1,000-yard receiving season with four different teams.<ref name="werner">{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |date=January 3, 2021 |title=Brandin Cooks joins Brandon Marshall with 1,000-yard seasons for 4 teams |url=https://touchdownwire.usatoday.com/2021/01/03/brandin-cooks-joins-brandon-marshal-with-1000-yard-seasons-for-4-teams/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110102835/https://touchdownwire.usatoday.com/2021/01/03/brandin-cooks-joins-brandon-marshal-with-1000-yard-seasons-for-4-teams/ |archive-date=January 10, 2021 |access-date=January 8, 2021 |website=Touchdown Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===

==== 2023 season ====
On March 19, 2023, the Texans traded Cooks to the Cowboys in exchange for a fifth-round pick in 2023 (#161-[[Nick Hampton (American football)|Nick Hampton]]) and a sixth-round pick in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Walker|first=Patrik|title=Brandin Cooks Acquired by Cowboys in Trade Deal|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/brandin-cooks-acquired-by-cowboys-in-trade-deal|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=March 19, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2023|archive-date=March 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319163555/https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/brandin-cooks-acquired-by-cowboys-in-trade-deal|url-status=live}}</ref> This trade made Cooks tie the NFL all-time record for most traded player held by retired running back, [[Eric Dickerson]].<ref>{{cite news|work=USAToday.com|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2023/03/brandin-cooks-dallas-cowboys-texans-trade-nfl|title=New Cowboys WR Brandin Cooks has tied the record for NFL's most-traded player ever|first=Cory|last=Woodroof|date=March 19, 2023|accessdate=March 20, 2023|archive-date=March 20, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320223322/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2023/03/brandin-cooks-dallas-cowboys-texans-trade-nfl|url-status=live}}</ref>

During the season opener, Cooks suffered a slight MCL sprain in the 40–0 shutout victory over the [[New York Giants]]. He did not play the following week against the [[New York Jets]] due to his injury. Cooks had a slow start to the season, tallying 17 catches for 165 yards and two touchdowns in the first eight games. In a Week 10 victory over the Giants, he had nine receptions for 173 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Dallas Cowboys – November 12th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311120dal.htm |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Cooks appeared in 16 games with 15 starts, making 54 receptions for 657 yards and eight touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2024 season ====
Prior to Week 5, Cooks was placed on injured reserve with a knee issue.<ref name="c170">{{cite web | last=Dajani | first=Jordan | title=Brandin Cooks injury update: Cowboys placing veteran WR on injured reserve with knee issue, per report | website=CBSSports.com | date=2024-10-05 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/brandin-cooks-injury-update-cowboys-placing-veteran-wr-on-injured-reserve-with-knee-issue-per-report/ | access-date=2025-01-13}}</ref> He missed seven games. In the 2024 season, Cooks had 26 receptions for 259 yards and three touchdowns in 10 games and nine starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints (second stint)===
On March 21, 2025, Cooks signed a two-year, $13 million contract with the New Orleans Saints, the team that drafted him in the first round in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|date=March 21, 2025|title=New Orleans Saints agree to terms with WR Brandin Cooks|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/brandin-cooks-new-orleans-saints-wide-receiver-signs-contract-2025-nfl-free-agency|website=New Orleans Saints|access-date=March 21, 2025}}</ref> Cooks was released on November 19.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terrell |first=Katherine |date=2025-11-19 |title=Saints move on from veteran receiver Cooks |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47024142/saints-releasing-veteran-wr-brandin-cooks-source-says |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Buffalo Bills ===
On November 25, 2025, Cooks signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Buffalo Bills sign WR Brandin Cooks to active roster|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/buffalo-bills-sign-wr-brandin-cooks-to-active-roster|author=White, Alec|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=November 25, 2025}}</ref> During Week 17 against the Eagles, he had four receptions for 101 yards in the narrow 13–12 loss.<ref>{{cite web | title=Bills' Brandin Cooks: Breaks out for 101 yards in Week 17 | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-12-29 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bills-brandin-cooks-breaks-out-for-101-yards-in-week-17/ | access-date=2026-01-09}}</ref> In the 2025 season, Cooks had 24 receptions for 279 yards in 15 games and five starts with both the Saints and the Bills.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Cooks 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CookBr00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-01-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2025–26 NFL playoffs#Divisional playoffs|Divisional Round]] against the [[2025 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]], Cooks was involved a pivotal and controversial ruling where a deep pass was intercepted by cornerback [[Ja'Quan McMillian]] in overtime. Both players jumped for the ball with Cooks landing on the field and McMillian landing on top of him and pulling the ball out of Cooks' hands in the end.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/columnist/bell/2026/01/18/jaquan-mcmillian-brandon-cooks-bills-broncos-interception-controversy/88247072007/|work=USAToday.com|title=Sorry, Bills. It's not the NFL without officiating controversy {{!}} Opinion|first=Jarrett|last=Bell|date=January 18, 2026|accessdate=January 20, 2026}}</ref> The officials ruled it an interception and confirmed the call after video review.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/nfl-former-vp-of-officiating-brandin-cooks-int|work=SI.com|title=NFL’s Former VP of Officiating Explains Why Brandin Cooks Play Wasn’t a Catch|first=Liam|last=McKeone|date=January 18, 2026|accessdate=January 20, 2026}}</ref> Following the interception, the Broncos went on to win 33–30 by driving down the field and kicking the game-winning field goal. In a postgame interview, head coach [[Sean McDermott]] criticized the officials' ruling of an interception and believed it should have been ruled a valid catch by Cooks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McKessy |first=Jack |date=January 17, 2026 |title='I'm standing up for Buffalo': Bills HC Sean McDermott vents on interception ruling |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/bills/2026/01/17/sean-mcdermott-interception-bills-broncos/88238939007/ |access-date=2026-01-19 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Cooks is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elizabeth |first=Lindsay |date=October 24, 2018 |title='Jesus Is the Light of the World': NFL WR Brandin Cooks Is on Fire for the Lord |url=http://www1.cbn.com/cbnnews/2018/october/lsquo-jesus-is-the-light-of-the-world-rsquo-nfl-wr-brandin-cooks-is-on-fire-for-the-lord |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190418132330/http://www1.cbn.com/cbnnews/2018/october/lsquo-jesus-is-the-light-of-the-world-rsquo-nfl-wr-brandin-cooks-is-on-fire-for-the-lord |archive-date=April 18, 2019 |access-date=April 14, 2020 |website=Christian Broadcasting Network}}</ref> He followed big plays in the 2016 season with a bow-and-arrow motion, referencing a Bible verse where a boy named [[Ishmael]] used his archery skills to survive in the desert after he nearly died there without water.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dabe |first=Christopher |date=November 5, 2015 |title=Brandin Cooks explains the reason for his bow-and-arrow celebration |url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2015/11/brandin_cooks_new_orleans_sain_3.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171217050338/http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2015/11/brandin_cooks_new_orleans_sain_3.html |archive-date=December 17, 2017 |access-date=April 2, 2017 |website=NOLA.com}}</ref> Cooks earned a nickname as "the Archer".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Mark |date=May 1, 2020 |title=Texans WR Brandin Cooks says his nickname comes a Bible verse |url=https://texanswire.usatoday.com/2020/05/01/texans-brandin-cooks-nickname-bible-verse/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929104621/https://texanswire.usatoday.com/2020/05/01/texans-brandin-cooks-nickname-bible-verse/ |archive-date=September 29, 2022 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=Texans Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

Cooks married Briannon Lepman on July 7, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Han |first=Jamie |date=July 9, 2018 |title=Rams Receivers Celebrate Big Week |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-receivers-celebrate-big-week |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190421022116/https://www.therams.com/news/rams-receivers-celebrate-big-week |archive-date=April 21, 2019 |access-date=July 9, 2018 |website=TheRams.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pompei |first=Dan |date=August 16, 2017 |title=Preparing to Be a Pat: Brandin Cooks Determined Not to Waste Shot at Greatness |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2727419-preparing-to-be-a-pat-brandin-cooks-determined-not-to-waste-shot-at-greatness |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002181257/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2727419-preparing-to-be-a-pat-brandin-cooks-determined-not-to-waste-shot-at-greatness |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, Cooks donated $50,000 to his hometown of Stockton, California. The donation helped establish the Stockton Children's Fund, which serves local children impacted by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williamson |first=Bill |date=March 23, 2020 |title=Brandin Cooks, Johnny Hekker donate to coronavirus relief efforts |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2020/3/23/21191907/brandin-cooks-johnny-hekker-coronavirus-nfl |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002181257/https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2020/3/23/21191907/brandin-cooks-johnny-hekker-coronavirus-nfl |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=April 27, 2020 |website=Turf Show Times|publisher=SB Nation |language=en}}</ref> In 2021, Cooks earned his [[Private pilot licence|Private Pilot License]] and [[Instrument rating|Instrument Rating]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=2024-06-19 |title='Got in the air, I fell in love': Inside Brandin Cooks' unique hobby of piloting his own plane |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/40333377/inside-cowboys-brandin-cooks-unique-hobby-piloting-planes |access-date=2026-01-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Bradley Alexander Pinion''' (born June 1, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Punter (football)|punter]] and [[kickoff specialist]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the fifth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. Pinion has also played for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
Pinion attended [[Northwest Cabarrus High School]] in [[Concord, North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hutton |first=Henry |date=May 15, 2017 |title=Living the Dream: Ex-Northwest Cabarrus star growing as player, person with San Francisco 49ers |url=http://www.independenttribune.com/sports/living-the-dream-ex-northwest-cabarrus-star-growing-as-player/article_dd924dce-39ab-11e7-9d55-bbb8664df1c7.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=The Independent Tribune |language=en}}</ref> He committed to [[Clemson University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion, Northwest Cabarrus, Kicker |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Bradley-Pinion-9160/high-school-12197/ |access-date=August 2, 2019 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Pinion played college football at [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]] from 2012 to 2014 under head coach [[Dabo Swinney]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bradley-pinion-1.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a freshman in 2012, Pinion only appeared in five games with teammate Spencer Benton doing a majority of the work that season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Clemson Tigers Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/clemson/2012.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On September 8, Pinion made his collegiate debut in the 52–27 win over [[Ball State Cardinals football|Ball State]]. In the game, he had three [[Punt (gridiron football)|punts]] for 117 yards (39.0 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ball State at Clemson Box Score, September 8, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-09-08-clemson.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, in the 2012 season, Pinion recorded nine punts for 355 yards (39.4 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bradley-pinion-1/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2013, Pinion became the main punter for the Tigers. That season, he handled the punting duties for all but three attempts, which went to Ammon Lakip and Andy Teasdall.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 Clemson Tigers Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/clemson/2013.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the season opener against the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], Pinion had a season-high seven punts for a season-high 287 yards (41.0 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Georgia at Clemson Box Score, August 31, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-08-31-clemson.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game, against [[South Carolina State Bulldogs football|South Carolina State]], he had four punts for 195 yards for a season-high 48.8 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Carolina State at Clemson Box Score, September 7, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-07-clemson.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, in the 2013 season, Pinion had 56 punts for 2,205 yards for a 39.4 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bradley-pinion-1/gamelog/2013 |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a junior in 2014, Pinion continued his role as the main punter for the Tigers. That season, he handled all but one punt, which went to Andy Teasdall. Pinion attempted and converted three [[extra point]]s on the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Clemson Tigers Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/clemson/2014.html |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During the season opener against the Georgia Bulldogs, Pinion had a season-high 10 punts for a season-high 451 yards ===San Francisco 49ers===
====2015 season====
Pinion was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the fifth round (165th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Emerick |first=Tyler |date=May 2, 2015 |title=San Francisco 49ers Draft Clemson P Bradley Pinion |url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/San-Francisco-49ers-Draft-Clemson-P-Bradley-Pinion/954fef68-a348-48f2-a89c-b2f459a6c20d |access-date=July 3, 2017 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was the only punter to be selected in the draft that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=June 18, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During the season-opening 20–3 over the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Pinion punted thrice for 140 yards (46.67 average) in his NFL debut.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers – September 14th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509140sfo.htm |access-date=September 26, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During Week 7 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', Pinion had a season-high nine punts for 390 yards (43.33 average) in the 20–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers - October 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510220sfo.htm |access-date=October 23, 2015 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He tied his season-high nine punts in the next game against the [[St. Louis Rams]], punting for 412 yards (45.78 average) during the 27–6 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at St. Louis Rams - November 1st, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511010ram.htm |access-date=November 3, 2015 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The following week the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Pinion recorded five punts for 241 net yards for a season-high 48.20 average in the narrow 17–16 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at San Francisco 49ers – November 8th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511080sfo.htm |access-date=November 11, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 13 26–20 overtime road victory over the [[Chicago Bears]], he had nine punts for a season-high 433 yards (48.11 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Chicago Bears – December 6th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512060chi.htm |access-date=December 18, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished his rookie season with 91 punts for 3,969 yards for a 43.62 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=January 8, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2016 season====
[[File:Bradley Pinion.JPG|thumb|right|Pinion  in 2016]]
Pinion began his second NFL season with very similar statistics in the first three games. During the season-opening 28–0 shutout victory over the [[Los Angeles Rams]], he recorded seven punts for 319 yards (45.57 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at San Francisco 49ers – September 12th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609120sfo.htm |access-date=September 17, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Pinion had seven punts for 318 yards (45.43 average) during the 46–27 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Carolina Panthers – September 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180car.htm |access-date=September 23, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], he punted seven times for 319 yards in the 37–18 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks – September 25th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250sea.htm |access-date=October 1, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 5 against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on ''Thursday Night Football'', Pinion had seven punts for 349 yards for a season-high 49.86 average in the 33–21 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers – October 6th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610060sfo.htm |access-date=October 8, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During a narrow Week 16 22–21 road victory over the Rams, Pinion recorded a season-high nine punts for a season-high 372 net yards (41.33 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams – December 24th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612240ram.htm |access-date=January 1, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished his second professional season with 100 punts for 4,402 yards and a 44.02 average in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2016 |access-date=January 4, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> His 100 punts led the league in attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Leaders and Leaderboards |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/leaders.htm |access-date=February 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2017 season====
[[File:Robbie Gould, Bradley Pinion (23871714198).jpg|thumb|Pinion (#5) with [[Robbie Gould]] in 2017|left]]Pinion remained as the 49ers' punter going into his third professional season. During a Week 4 18–15 overtime road loss to the Cardinals, he punted seven times for 351 yards for a season-high 50.14 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Arizona Cardinals – October 1st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710010crd.htm |access-date=October 2, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 8 33–10 road loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Pinion had eight punts for a season-high 364 yards (44.00 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Philadelphia Eagles – October 29th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710290phi.htm |access-date=October 30, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 12 24–13 loss to the Seahawks, he recorded a season-high nine punts for 342 yards (38.00 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers – November 26th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711260sfo.htm |access-date=November 27, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished the 2017 season with a then career-low 75 punts for 3,255 yards for a 43.4 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2017 |access-date=January 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2018 season ====
During the season-opening 24–16 road loss to the Vikings, Pinion recorded four punts for 174 yards (43.5 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Minnesota Vikings – September 9th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090min.htm |access-date=September 17, 2018 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During Week 8 against the Cardinals, he had a season-high seven punts for a season-high 285 yards (40.71 average) in the 18–15 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Arizona Cardinals - October 28th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201810280crd.htm |access-date=November 1, 2018 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Oakland Raiders]] on ''Thursday Night Football'', Pinion punted thrice for 164 yards for a season-high 54.7 average, including a season-long 64-yard punt, during the 34–3 blowout victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at San Francisco 49ers – November 1st, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811010sfo.htm |access-date=November 4, 2018 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance against the Raiders.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 7, 2018 |title=Kareem Hunt, Michael Thomas among Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/kareem-hunt-michael-thomas-among-players-of-the-week-0ap3000000985405 |access-date=August 2, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Pinion finished the 2018 season with a then career-low 68 punts for 2,973 yards for a 43.7 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=August 2, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===

==== 2019 season ====
On March 13, 2019, Pinion signed a four-year contract with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 13, 2019 |title=Bucs Boot Up Free Agency with Punter Bradley Pinion |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-boot-up-free-agency-with-punter-bradley-pinion |access-date=August 2, 2019 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

Pinion made his Buccaneers debut during the season-opening 31–17 loss to his former team, the [[San Francisco 49ers]], punting twice for 42 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - September 8th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909080tam.htm |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Carolina Panthers]] on ''Thursday Night Football'', Pinion recorded a season-high six punts for a season-high 295 yards and a season-high 49.17 average during the 20–14 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Carolina Panthers - September 12th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909120car.htm |access-date=September 14, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he had six punts for 263 yards (43.83 average) in the 31–24 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at New Orleans Saints - October 6th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201910060nor.htm |access-date=October 11, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the Panthers in London, Pinion recorded similar statistics, tying his season-high of six punts for 267 yards (44.5 average) during the 37–26 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - October 13th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201910130tam.htm |access-date=2019-10-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished the 2019 season with a then career-low 57 punts for 2,464 yards for a 43.23 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 1, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at New Orleans Saints - January 17th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101170nor.htm |access-date=2021-01-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During the NFC Championship Game against the Packers, Pinion punted twice for 80 yards in the 31–26 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship - ==== 2021 season ====

===Atlanta Falcons===
==== 2022 season ====
On June 30, 2022, Pinion signed a one-year contract with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McElhaney |first=Tori |date=June 30, 2022 |title=Falcons sign veteran punter to special teams unit |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-veteran-punter-to-special-teams-unit |access-date=July 1, 2022 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref>

During a Week 3 27–23 road victory over the Seahawks, Pinion recorded a career-long 73-yard punt.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Seattle Seahawks – September 25th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209250sea.htm |access-date=September 30, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against his former team, the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Pinion had a season-high six punts for a season-high 290 yards (48.33 average) in the 21–15 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - October 9th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210090tam.htm |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He put up similar statistics during a Week 7 35–17 road loss to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], punting six times for 282 yards (47.0 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Cincinnati Bengals - October 23rd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210230cin.htm |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished the 2022 season with 62 punts for 2,845 yards for a 42.46 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=January 1, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2023 season ====
On March 13, 2023, Pinion signed a three-year, $8.65 million contract extension with the Falcons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McElhaney |first=Tori |date=March 13, 2023 |title=Falcons sign punter, kickoff specialist Bradley Pinion to three-year deal |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-punter-kickoff-specialist-bradley-pinion-to-three-year-deal |access-date=2024-02-18 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref>

During the season-opening 24–10 victory over the Panthers, Pinion punted seven times for 337 yards (48.14 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons - September 10th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309100atl.htm |access-date=September 14, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Detroit Lions]], he recorded six punts for 295 yards (49.17 average) in the 20–6 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Detroit Lions - September 24th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309240det.htm |access-date=September 30, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Pinion had five punts for 271 yards and a season-high 54.2 average during the 23–7 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Jacksonville Jaguars - October 1st, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310010jax.htm |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 8 27–23 road loss to the [[Tennessee Titans]], Pinion punted six times for 305 yards (50.83 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Tennessee Titans - October 29th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310290oti.htm |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 13 13–8 road victory over the [[New York Jets]], he recorded a season-high nine punts for a season-high 433 yards (48.11 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New York Jets - December 3rd, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202312030nyj.htm |access-date=2023-12-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the regular season finale against the Saints, Pinion had five punts for 254 yards (50.8 average) and a season-long 66-yard punt during the 48–17 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints - January 7th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401070nor.htm |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished the 2023 season with 75 punts for 3,523 yards for a 46.97 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-02-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He was named first team All-Pro by Pro Football Focus.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/allpro.htm |access-date=2025-01-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2024 season ====
During the season-opening 18–10 loss to the Steelers, Pinion had four punts for 210 yards (52.5 average).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Atlanta Falcons - September 8th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202409080atl.htm |access-date=September 9, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Chiefs on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football]]'', he punted thrice for 162 yards and a season-long 65-yard punt in the 22–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons - September 22nd, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202409220atl.htm |access-date=September 28, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 15 15–9 road victory over the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], Pinion recorded a season-high six punts for a season-high 265 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Las Vegas Raiders - December 16th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202412160rai.htm |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Pinion finished the 2024 season with a career-low 47 punts for 2,209 yards for a career-high 47.00 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 8, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2025 season====
Pinion finished the 2025 season with 64 punts for 2,889 yards for a 45.1 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Pinion 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PiniBr00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On March 20, 2026, Pinion signed a one-year, $1.48 million contract with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins sign Pinion |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-pinion |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=21 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Bralon Addison''' (born October 12, 1993) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He most recently played for the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]]. Addison has also been a member of the [[Denver Broncos]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[Toronto Argonauts]], [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]], and [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Addison attended [[Hightower High School]] in [[Missouri City, Texas]]. He played predominately  [[quarterback]] his senior and junior years and wide receiver his sophomore year. He had thrown for 2,158 passing yards, 22 passing [[touchdowns]], had 1,625 rushing yards and 20 rushing touchdowns as a senior. As a junior, he passed for 1,858 yards with 28 touchdowns and rushed for 1,068 yards and 15 touchdowns. Addison was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a four-star recruit and committed to the [[University of Oregon]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bralon Addison, 2012 Wide Receiver, Oregon |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/bralon-addison-14399?view=pv |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2012 |title=Recruiting notes: Hightower's Addison switches from A&M to... |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/highschool/article/recruiting-notes-hightower-s-addison-switches-2935269.php |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=Chron |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
As a [[true freshman]] at Oregon in 2012, Addison played in all 13 games and had 22 receptions for 243 yards. As a sophomore in 2013, Addison started 11 of 13 games, recording 61 receptions for 890 yards and seven touchdowns. He also returned two [[punt return]]s for touchdowns. Addison missed 2014 due to a [[torn ACL]] suffered during spring practice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greif  |first=Andrew |date=April 11, 2014 |title=Oregon wide receiver Bralon Addison tears ACL in knee and could miss 2014 season |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2014/04/oregon_wide_receiver_bralon_ad.html |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=OregonLive |language=en}}</ref> He came close to playing in the [[2015 College Football Playoff National Championship]], but was not completely healed in time for the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olson |first=Max |date=January 10, 2015 |title=Dontre Wilson, Bralon Addison struggle with whether to play |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/pac12/post/_/id/83040/dontre-wilson-bralon-addison-struggle-with-whether-to-play |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>[http://www.csnnw.com/ducks/oregon-wr-bralon-addison-remains-out-national-title-game Oregon WR Bralon Addison remains out for national title game] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405061716/http://www.csnnw.com/ducks/oregon-wr-bralon-addison-remains-out-national-title-game |date=April 5, 2015 }}</ref> Addison returned from the injury to play in all 13 games in 2015. He finished with 63 receptions for 804 yards, 10 receiving touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and one punt return touchdown. After the season, he entered the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greif |first=Andrew |date=January 5, 2016 |title=Oregon Ducks receiver Bralon Addison declares for NFL draft |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2016/01/oregon_ducks_receiver_bralon_a_2.html |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=OregonLive |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Denver Broncos===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NFL draft]], Addison was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]]. On August 30, 2016, Addison was waived by the Broncos during roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mason |first=Andrew |date=August 30, 2016 |title=Broncos release Britton Colquitt, make three other moves to get down to 75 |url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-release-Britton-Colquitt-make-three-other-moves-to-get-down-to-75/506103de-172e-40eb-af2f-ea17ee7076e3 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160831145744/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-release-Britton-Colquitt-make-three-other-moves-to-get-down-to-75/506103de-172e-40eb-af2f-ea17ee7076e3 |archive-date=August 31, 2016 |access-date=September 1, 2016 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On December 5, 2016, Addison was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears add veteran Banks to secondary|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-rostermoves/Bears-add-veteran-Banks-to-secondary/5183b4e6-ce2d-4bd8-befc-765f74550a2c|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212031110/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-rostermoves/Bears-add-veteran-Banks-to-secondary/5183b4e6-ce2d-4bd8-befc-765f74550a2c|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 12, 2017|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 20, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears add Bralon Addison to active roster|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/bears-add-bralon-addison-to-active-roster/|author=Eurich, Matt|website=CBSSports.com|date=December 20, 2016}}</ref> On May 1, 2017, Addison was waived by the Bears.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears ink Boggs, waive six players|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-ink-boggs-waive-six-players-18813260|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=May 1, 2017}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On April 18, 2018, Addison signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref name="l485">{{cite web | title=Argos sign WR Bralon Addison and LB Durell Eskridge | website=Toronto Argonauts | date=2018-04-18 | url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2018/04/18/argos-sign-wr-bralon-addison-lb-durell-eskridge/ | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref> Addison did not play a game for the Argos before he was released by the team on August 25, 2018.

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats (first stint)===
[[File:86, Bralon Addison, June 22, 2019.jpg|thumb|left|Addison with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats in 2019|200px]]
On September 1, 2018, Addison signed with the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ticats.ca/tiger-cats-add-five-players-to-practice-roster-2/|title=Ticats add five players to practice roster – Hamilton Tiger-Cats|date=September 1, 2018|publisher=[[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]]}}</ref> Addison played 4 regular season games for Hamilton. In the final game of the year, Addison had 7 catches for 103 yards and a touchdown; Addison had only one catch for 10 yards the rest of the year. To explain Addison's playing time at the expense of CFL veteran [[Terrell Sinkfield]], head coach [[June Jones]] jokingly replied about Addison, "He's better."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ferguson |first=Marshall |date=November 11, 2018 |title=Ferguson: Addison fills the void as unsung hero shines |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/11/11/ferguson-bralon-addison-answer-ticats/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=CFL.ca}}</ref> While Sinkfield was inactive for both playoff games, Addison caught 5 passes for 124 yards in Hamilton's 48–8 victory over the [[BC Lions]], and had 12 catches for 129 yards in the CFL East final, a loss to Ottawa. Addison continued his strong play into the [[2019 CFL season|2019 season]] and was named a CFL Top Performer for the month of September.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/hamilton-tiger-cats-bralon-addison-dane-evans-lead-top-performers-for-september-1.1375160|title=Hamilton Tiger-Cats' Bralon Addison, Dane Evans lead Top Performers for September - TSN.ca|author=TSN ca Staff|date=October 2, 2019|website=TSN|language=en|access-date=October 2, 2019}}</ref> He finished the season with 95 receptions for 1,236 yards with seven touchdowns: He also carried the ball 36 times for 218 yards with one rushing touchdown and was named a CFL All-Star.<ref>{{Cite web|date=November 27, 2019|title=Stars Aligned: 2019 CFL All-Stars unveiled|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2019/11/27/stars-aligned-2019-cfl-stars-unveiled/|access-date=September 28, 2021|website=CFL.ca|language=en}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On January 21, 2020, Addison signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the NFL.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings sign former CFL receiver Bralon Addison|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/01/21/vikings-sign-former-cfl-receiver-bralon-addison/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=January 21, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on August 6, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Alper, Josh |title=Vikings activate Armon Watts, waive Bralon Addison |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/08/06/vikings-activate-armon-watts-waive-bralon-addison/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=August 6, 2020 |accessdate=August 10, 2020}}</ref>

===Hamilton Tiger-Cats (second stint)===
On December 25, 2020, Addison re-signed with the Tiger-Cats to a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2020/12/25/bralon-back-two-year-deal-tiger-cats/|title=Bralon back on two-year deal with Tiger-Cats|date=December 25, 2020|publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]}}</ref> Addison missed the first half of the [[2021 CFL season]] while recovering from a knee injury; he was added to the active roster on September 28, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|author=TSN ca Staff|date=September 28, 2021|title=Bralon Addison knee injury active roster Hamilton Tiger-Cats - TSN.ca|url=https://www.tsn.ca/bralon-addison-knee-injury-active-roster-hamilton-tiger-cats-1.1699383|access-date=September 28, 2021|website=TSN|language=en}}</ref> On October 24 Addison was placed on the six-game injured reserve list with a hamstring issue.<ref name="k871">{{cite web | title=Ticats’ receiver Bralon Addison ruled out with hamstring injury | website=3DownNation | date=2021-10-23 | url=https://3downnation.com/2021/10/23/ticats-receiver-bralon-addison-ruled-out-with-hamstring-injury/ | access-date=2025-01-19}}</ref> Due to the multiple injuries Addison was limited to just three regular season games, catching 18 passes for 231 yards. He was re-added to the active roster on November 24, 2021, four days before the Ti-Cats Eastern semifinal match against the [[Montreal Alouettes]].<ref>{{Cite web|author=TSN ca Staff|date=November 24, 2021|title=Ticats activate WR Addison ahead of Eastern semifinal - TSN.ca|url=https://www.tsn.ca/hamilton-tiger-cats-bralon-addison-1.1725678|access-date=November 24, 2021|website=TSN|language=en}}</ref> Addison did not catch a pass in either playoff game, and the Tiger-Cats were defeated in the [[108th Grey Cup]] match. After playing in the first eight games of the [[2022 CFL season|2022 season]] Addison was carted off the field with what was initially reported as a knee injury in the team's Week 9 loss against the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref>{{Cite web |author=TSN ca Staff |date=August 6, 2022 |title=Ticats WR Addison carted off; Argos DB Richardson leaves with lower-body injury - TSN.ca |url=https://www.tsn.ca/bralon-addison-shaq-richardson-hamilton-tiger-cats-toronto-argonauts-injury-1.1833708 |access-date=August 8, 2022 |website=TSN |language=en}}</ref> A couple days later he reveled on Twitter that he had suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|torn Achilles]] and would miss the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 10, 2022 |title=Ticats' Addison confirms Achilles injury |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2022/08/10/ticats-addison-confirms-achilles-injury/ |access-date=August 11, 2022 |website=CFL.ca |language=en}}</ref> At the time of the injury Addison was leading the team in receptions, with 43, and was second to [[Steven Dunbar]] in receiving yards with 433 (Dunbar had 559 receiving yards). Addison was released by Hamilton on May 10, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |author=3Down Staff |date=May 10, 2023 |title=Hamilton Tiger-Cats release veteran receiver Bralon Addison |url=https://3downnation.com/2023/05/10/hamilton-tiger-cats-receiver-bralon-addison-announces-retirement-from-cfl/ |access-date=May 10, 2023 |website=3DownNation |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
On May 13, 2023, it was announced that Addison had signed a one-year contract with the [[Ottawa Redblacks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2023/05/13/redblacks-sign-bralon-addison-to-one-year-deal/|title=Redblacks sign Bralon Addison to one-year deal|date=May 13, 2023|publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]}}</ref> In January 2024, he signed a one-year extension.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Staff |first1=CFL ca |title=Redblacks, Addison agree to one-year extension |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2024/01/18/redblacks-addison-agree-to-one-year-extension/ |website=CFL.ca |access-date=3 October 2025 |language=en |date=18 January 2024}}</ref> On January 22, 2025, he signed a one-year extension with the Redblacks.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://ottawacitizen.com/ottawa-redblacks/redblacks-reach-deal-bralon-addison|title=Ottawa Redblacks extend Braylon Addison through 2025 season|date= January 22, 2025 |publisher=[[Ottawa Citizen]]}}</ref> In [[2025 Ottawa Redblacks season|2025]], Addison recorded 72 receptions for 825 yards and three touchdowns along with 17 carries for 58 rushing yards. He became a [[free agent]] upon the expiry of his contract on February 10, 2026.<ref name=2026T>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2026/ |title=Transactions – Football Player Trades and Signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 14, 2026}}</ref> 

==Personal life==
Addison is the son of Julias Addison and Sonya Swindell. He has one brother and one sister.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bralon Addison - Football |url=https://goducks.com/sports/football/roster/bralon-addison/5042 |website=University of Oregon Athletics |access-date=3 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
