'''Braedon Dean Bowman''' (born January 30, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Alabama Jaguars football|South Alabama Jaguars]] and was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] as an undrafted free agent in 2016.

==Early life==
Bowman was born in 1994 in Mesa, Arizona as the second eldest of four children to parents Laura Becker and Warren Bowman.<ref name="South Alabama Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman">[https://usajaguars.com/sports/football/roster/braedon-bowman/6307 "South Alabama Jaguars"] Profile. Retrieved November 22, 2024.</ref> He attended Skyline High School in his hometown where he played [[wide receiver]] with the Coyotes football team.<ref name="Skyline WR Braedon Bowman">[https://www.maxpreps.com/az/mesa/skyline-coyotes/athletes/braedon-bowman/bio/?careerid=2rq1gst18t066 "MaxPreps"] Recruitment Profile. Retrieved November 22, 2024.</ref> During two years of football, Bowman earned two letters.<ref name="South Alabama Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman"/>

Bowman also earned a letter in [[baseball]] while in high school.<ref name="South Alabama Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman"/> Standing {{Height|ft=6|in=4}} and weighing {{convert|190|lbs|kg|0}}, Bowman played [[Center (basketball)|center]] in [[basketball]],<ref name="Skyline WR Braedon Bowman"/> earning a letter that made him a three-sport standout. He graduated in 2012.

==College career==
Bowman played [[junior college]] football as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] with the Scottsdale Fighting Artichokes while attending [[Scottsdale Community College]].<ref name="USA Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman"/> Between the 2012 and 2013 semesters, Bowman earned first-team junior college and conference honors. While at Scottsdale CC, Bowman was rated a two-star recruit, receiving offers from [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming]], [[Northern Colorado Bears football|Northern Colorado]], [[Jacksonville State Gamecocks football|Jacksonville State]], [[Georgia State Panthers football|Georgia State]], [[Georgia Southern Eagles football|Georgia Southern]] and South Alabama.<ref name="TE Braedon Bowman">[https://247sports.com/recruitment/braedon-bowman-38891/recruitinterests/ "247Sports"] Recruitment Profile. Retrieved November 22, 2024.</ref>

Bowman began his junior season at the [[University of South Alabama]] in 2014. He joined the South Alabama Jaguars as a tight end, starting 5 of 11 games before sustaining a [[Bone fracture|broken]] [[foot]] during his fourth start.<ref name="USA Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman">O'Halloran, Ryan. [https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/2016/06/25/jaguars-insider-undrafted-bowman-has-chance-earn-roster/15714996007/ "Jaguars Insider: Undrafted Bowman has a chance to earn roster spot"]. The Florida Times-Union. Retrieved November 22, 2024.</ref> He caught 18 passes and made 15 receptions.<ref name="South Alabama Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman"/> As a senior during the 2016 season, Bowman finished with 11 catches. For the two seasons played at South Alabama, Bowman ranked as the second best tight end on the team in receptions and receiving yards.<ref name="South Alabama TE B. Bowman">South Alabama Jaguars Sports Article: [https://usajaguars.com/news/2016/5/1/football-usas-bowman-signs-free-agent-contract-with-nfls-jaguars "Bowman Signs Free Agent Contract With Nfls Jaguars"]. Retrieved November 22, 2024.</ref> While attending South Alabama, Bowman majored in [[criminal justice]], preparing for a possible career in [[Law enforcement in the United States|law enforcement]].<ref name="South Alabama Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman"/>

==Professional career==
===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On May 1, 2016, Bowman signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref name="al.com">{{cite web | title=South Alabama's Braedon Bowman headed to Jacksonville Jaguars as undrafted free agent | work= al.com | url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2016/04/south_alabamas_braedon_bowman_1.html |access-date=April 30, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars agree to terms with nine undrafted rookie free agents|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-agree-to-terms-with-nine-undrafted-rookie-free-agents/4a645a28-b29a-4d57-875e-a96e7a860c91|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813013120/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-agree-to-terms-with-nine-undrafted-rookie-free-agents/4a645a28-b29a-4d57-875e-a96e7a860c91|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 13, 2017|website=Jaguars.com|date=May 1, 2016|access-date=May 26, 2017}}</ref> On September 3, he was released by the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Down to 53: LB Davis, OG Bernadeau released|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Down-to-53-LB-Davis-OG-Bernadeau-released/d39aa0b3-fc8a-47df-9a6d-c71d01ffa980|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813013636/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Down-to-53-LB-Davis-OG-Bernadeau-released/d39aa0b3-fc8a-47df-9a6d-c71d01ffa980|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 13, 2017|last=Oehser|first=John|website=Jaguars.com|date=September 3, 2016}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On September 4, 2016, Bowman was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Jets]].<ref name="al.com"/> On September 13, he was waived by the Jets but was re-signed on September 23.<ref>{{cite web | title=Jets waive TE Braedon Bowman to make room for Sheldon Richardson | work= nj.com |url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2016/09/jets_waive_te_braedon_bowman_to_make_room_for_shel.html |access-date=September 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Jets sign tight end Braedon Bowman to 53-man roster | work= nj.com | url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2016/09/jets_sign_tight_end_braedon_bowman_to_53-man_roste.html |access-date=September 23, 2016}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on October 22, with a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Promote LBs Ochi & Stanford to Roster|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Promote-LBs-Ochi--Stanford-to-Roster/1376b5db-4465-44f6-950a-2b2394e234b8|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822095126/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Promote-LBs-Ochi--Stanford-to-Roster/1376b5db-4465-44f6-950a-2b2394e234b8|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 22, 2017|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=October 22, 2016}}</ref>

On May 30, 2017, Bowman was waived by the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign WR Chris Harper|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Sign-WR-Chris-Harper/47f687dc-8afe-4bdf-94b0-22ab6e2af3f7|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=May 30, 2017|access-date=May 31, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904200514/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Sign-WR-Chris-Harper/47f687dc-8afe-4bdf-94b0-22ab6e2af3f7|archive-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On August 12, 2017, Bowman was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-announce-roster-moves/5be5e8c8-c7eb-457f-a4a5-3cceb7221dfd|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914201736/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-announce-roster-moves/5be5e8c8-c7eb-457f-a4a5-3cceb7221dfd|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 14, 2017|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=August 12, 2017}}</ref> On September 2, Bowman was waived by the Saints.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints make 37 roster moves|url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-make-37-roster-moves/772dc16b-7962-4363-b7a8-85db4dd37f90|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007170254/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/New-Orleans-Saints-make-37-roster-moves/772dc16b-7962-4363-b7a8-85db4dd37f90|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 7, 2017|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=September 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On September 6, 2017, Bowman was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Sign TE Braedon Bowman & LB Nick Dzubar To Practice Squad|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/chargers-sign-te-braedon-bowman-lb-nick-dzubar-practice-squad/|website=NFLTradeRumors.com|date=September 6, 2017}}</ref> He was released on November 15, but was re-signed two days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Sign OT Jake Rodgers To Practice Squad, Release TE Braedon Bowman|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/chargers-sign-ot-jake-rodgers-practice-squad-release-te-braedon-bowman/|website=NFLTradeRumors.co|date=November 15, 2017}}</ref> Bowman signed a reserve/future contract with the Chargers on January 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Sign Six to Reserve/Future Contracts|url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2018/01/01/chargers-sign-six-reservefuture-contracts|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407180219/http://www.chargers.com/news/2018/01/01/chargers-sign-six-reservefuture-contracts|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 7, 2018|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=January 1, 2018}}</ref> On September 1, Bowman was waived by the Chargers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Cut Roster Down to 53|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-cut-roster-down-to-53|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Birmingham Iron===
For the 2019 campaign, Bowman joined the [[Birmingham Iron]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Inabinett|first=Mark|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2019/01/birmingham-iron-sets-roster-for-inaugural-season.html|title=Birmingham Iron sets roster for inaugural season|newspaper=[[The Birmingham News]]|date=January 30, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}}</ref>  He was placed on injured reserve on February 14, 2019. Bowman was activated from injured reserve on March 19. The league ceased operations in April of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===New Jersey Generals===
Bowman was selected by the [[New Jersey Generals (2022)|New Jersey Generals]] in the 34th round of the [[2022 USFL draft]].<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLGenerals |title=March On! The Generals have selected Braedon Bowman #USFLDraft #InTheTrenches |number=1496581810259918848 |date=February 23, 2022 |access-date=May 14, 2022}}</ref> He was transferred to the team's inactive roster on May 12 with a [[quadriceps]] injury.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLGenerals |title=Roster Updates |number=1524952321964113921 |date=May 12, 2022 |access-date=May 14, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLGenerals |title=Braedon Bowman, TE: Out (Quad) |number=1524955340885725184 |date=May 12, 2022 |access-date=May 14, 2022}}</ref>

Bowman re-signed with the Generals on July 14, 2023.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLGenerals |title=Free Agent Signings |number=1679941287481430023 |date=July 14, 2023 |access-date=July 16, 2023}}</ref> The Generals folded when the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] and USFL merged to create the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=January 1, 2024 |title=Newly formed United Football League sets 8 markets, tabs coaches |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/39222541/newly-formed-united-football-league-sets-8-markets-tabs-coaches |access-date=January 15, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

=== Houston Roughnecks ===
On January 5, 2024, Bowman was selected by the [[Houston Roughnecks (2024)|Houston Roughnecks]] during the [[2024 UFL dispersal draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-06 |title=UFL Dispersal Draft Results for Former XFL, USFL Teams |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/ufl/news/ufl-notebook-ufl-dispersal-draft-results-xfl-usfl-players |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He signed with the team on February 27.<ref>{{cite news |title=UFL Player Transactions, Tuesday February 27, 2024 |url=https://uflboard.com/news/ufl-player-transactions-tuesday-february-27-2024/ |website=UFLBoard.com |date=February 27, 2024 |access-date=February 28, 2024}}</ref> Bowman was released by Houston on July 23.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UFL Transactions |url=https://uflboard.com/ufl-transactions/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=UFLBoard.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bowman's favorite movie is [[Happy Gilmore]]. As a sports fan, his favorite football team is the [[Arizona Cardinals]] and his favorite [[basketball]] team is the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. His hobbies include hunting, fishing and music. In football, Bowman listed [[Eric Decker]] and [[Larry Fitzgerald]] as his favorite players.<ref name="South Alabama Jaguars TE Braedon Bowman"/>

'''Branden Jackson''' (born November 11, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]].

==College career==
Jackson played four years at Texas Tech, appearing in 51 games with 38 starts, totalling 138 tackles, 11 sacks, three forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and one pass defensed.

Hayden to Reserve/Injured List|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-DL-Branden-Jackson-to-Active-Roster-Hayden-to-ReserveInjured-List/9536c240-707c-4f5f-8ed1-d0fe262e4222?sf44742851=1|website=Raiders.com|date=December 3, 2016|access-date=December 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220224319/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-DL-Branden-Jackson-to-Active-Roster-Hayden-to-ReserveInjured-List/9536c240-707c-4f5f-8ed1-d0fe262e4222?sf44742851=1|archive-date=December 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Jackson was waived by the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|website=Raiders.com|date=September 2, 2017|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209084351/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|archivedate=December 9, 2017|url-status=dead|access-date=September 8, 2017}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On September 26, 2017, Jackson was signed to the [[Seattle Seahawks]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks cut Tyvis Powell, Gabe Jackson; sign Branden Jackson|url=https://247sports.com/article/seahawks-cut-tyvis-powell-gabe-jackson-sign-branden-jackson-108035228/|website=247sports.com|date=September 26, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 7, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign DE Branden Jackson; Waive LB Justin March-Lillard|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-de-branden-jackson-waive-lb-justin-march-lillard-195731|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=October 7, 2017}}</ref>

On September 2, 2018, Jackson was waived by the Seahawks and was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Claim G Jordan Simmons And DB Simeon Thomas On Waivers|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-claim-g-jordan-simmons-and-db-simeon-thomas-on-waivers|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 2, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks re-sign Branden Jackson, release Antwione Williams|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/Article/Branden-Jackson-re-sign-Antwione-Williams-released-121466299/|website=247sports.com|date=September 5, 2018}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 25, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Defensive End Branden Jackson Off Practice Squad, Waive Tight End Darrell Daniels|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-defensive-end-branden-jackson-off-practice-squad-waive-tight-end-d|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 25, 2018}}</ref>

Jackson re-signed with the Seahawks on April 23, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Boyle, John |title=Seahawks Sign Linebacker Bruce Irvin; Re-Sign Joey Hunt, Branden Jackson & Bryan Mone |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-linebacker-bruce-irvin-re-sign-joey-hunt-branden-jackson-bryan-mon |website=Seahawks.com |date=April 23, 2020 |accessdate=April 23, 2020}}</ref> He was released on July 26, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |author=Rauschenberg, Nathan |title=Seahawks Waive Seven, Terminate Two, Including Center Joey Hunt |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-waive-seven-terminate-two-including-center-joey-hunt |website=Seahawks.com |date=July 26, 2020 |accessdate=July 27, 2020}}</ref> but was re-signed on August 6.<ref>{{cite news |author=Boyle, John |title=Seahawks Re-Sign DE Branden Jackson |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-re-sign-de-branden-jackson |website=Seahawks.com |date=August 6, 2020 |accessdate=August 10, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] due to a career ending neck injury on August 30, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign DE Pita Taumoepenu; Place Branden Jackson On IR|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-de-pita-taumoepenu-place-branden-jackson-on-ir|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=August 30, 2020}}</ref>

'''Brandin Bryant''' (born September 16, 1993)<ref name="fausports.com">{{Cite web |title=fausports.com Brandin Bryant Bio – Florida Atlantic Official Athletic Site |url=http://www.fausports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandin_bryant_810926.html |access-date=March 6, 2017 |archive-date=December 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223201110/http://www.fausports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/brandin_bryant_810926.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> is an American children’s book author and professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic]] and was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as an undrafted free agent in 2016. Brandin published his debut children’s book “So, You Want To Be an Athlete?” in January 2024.

==College career==
Bryant first went to college at [[Fort Scott Community College]] as a redshirt freshman. He transferred to [[Florida Atlantic University]], where he would be a starter for the following four seasons. He majored in communication and political science. During his junior season, he returned to Nebraska, where his grandfather had played in the mid-1950s. Over his four-year collegiate career, he totaled 130 total tackles (27.0 for a loss), 13.5 sacks, 2 passes defended and a forced fumble. He earned FAU's comeback player of the year award during the 2015 season.<ref name="fausports.com" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Bryant College Stats - College Football at Sports-Reference.com |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/brandin-bryant-1.html |access-date=March 6, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Seattle Seahawks===
Bryant was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as an undrafted free agent on May 6, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle, John |date=May 6, 2016 |title=Seahawks Sign 13 Undrafted Free Agents and 9 of 10 Draft Picks |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/05/06/seahawks-sign-13-undrafted-free-agents-and-9-10-draft-picks |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826153031/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/05/06/seahawks-sign-13-undrafted-free-agents-and-9-10-draft-picks |archive-date=August 26, 2017 |access-date=March 18, 2017 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He played in all four of their preseason games, compiling 3 total tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brandin Bryant: Game Logs at NFL.com |website=[[NFL.com]] |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/brandinbryant/2556486/gamelogs |access-date=March 6, 2017}}</ref> On September 3, 2016, Bryant was waived by the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arthur, Kenneth |date=September 3, 2016 |title=Seahawks final cuts 2016: Full list of players released as Seattle gets down to 53-man roster |url=http://www.fieldgulls.com/2016/9/3/12785274/seahawks-final-cuts-2016-53-man-roster-camp-battle-starters-depth-chart |access-date=March 18, 2017 |website=FieldGulls.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On October 24, 2016, Bryant was signed to the [[New York Jets]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen, Eric |date=October 24, 2016 |title=Jets Sign DL Brandin Bryant to Practice Squad |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Sign-DL-Brandin-Bryant-to-Practice-Squad/494d9bb9-7872-477f-afd1-bcfce40f6c45 |access-date=March 18, 2017 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 20, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg, Ethan |date=December 20, 2016 |title=Jets Place Winters and Catapano on IR |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Place-Winters-and-Catapano-on-IR/a0b73b0f-e286-4665-8add-bab05456673b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805015527/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Place-Winters-and-Catapano-on-IR/a0b73b0f-e286-4665-8add-bab05456673b |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |access-date=March 18, 2017 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

On August 4, 2017, Bryant was waived/injured by the Jets and placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen, Eric |date=August 4, 2017 |title=Jets Sign DL Still & Faulk |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Sign-DL-Still--Faulk/fa31d560-ff65-411a-8f1b-f97a681d8589 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904211817/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/Jets-Sign-DL-Still--Faulk/fa31d560-ff65-411a-8f1b-f97a681d8589 |archive-date=September 4, 2017 |access-date=August 5, 2017 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was waived from IR on August 9, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2017-08-09 |title=Jets Waive DL Brandin Bryant From I.R. With Settlement |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/jets-waive-dl-brandin-bryant-r-settlement/ |access-date=2025-01-13 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Bryant signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] on August 9, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 9, 2019 |title=Browns sign DT Brandin Bryant, T Travis Vornkahl |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-dt-brandin-bryant-t-travis-vornkahl}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2019 and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Browns cut roster to 53 players |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-cut-roster-to-53-players |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Browns announce nine additions to practice squad |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-announce-nine-additions-to-practice-squad |access-date=June 2, 2020 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |archive-date=September 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903181813/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-announce-nine-additions-to-practice-squad |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Browns elevated Bryant to their active roster on November 22, 2019. He was waived on December 21, 2019 and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 21, 2019 |title=Browns elevate DE Robert McCray to active roster |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-elevate-lb-robert-mccray-from-practice-squad |access-date=June 2, 2020 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> The Browns signed Bryant to their reserve/futures list on December 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2019 |title=Browns sign 8 players |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-8-players |access-date=June 2, 2020 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> Bryant was waived by the Browns on May 8, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=May 8, 2020 |title=Browns re-sign WR Rashard Higgins |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-re-sign-wr-rashard-higgins}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
Bryant was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] on August 12, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolphins Sign Brandin Bryant|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-brandin-bryant|access-date=2020-08-12|website=www.miamidolphins.com|language=en-US|date=August 12, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on August 15, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Dolphins Awarded Jeremiah Dinson |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-awarded-jeremiah-dinson |website=MiamiDolphins.com |date=August 15, 2020 |accessdate=August 16, 2020}}</ref> and activated the next day.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dolphins Waive Two, Activate Brandin Bryant |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-waive-two-activate-brandin-bryant |website=MiamiDolphins.com |date=August 16, 2020 |accessdate=August 17, 2020 |archive-date=August 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200824052037/https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-waive-two-activate-brandin-bryant |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived on September 5, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Acquire Lynn Bowden, Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-acquire-lynn-bowden-make-roster-moves|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills (first stint)===
On September 17, 2020, Bryant was signed to the [[Buffalo Bills]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills elevate CB Cam Lewis to active roster, add two to practice squad|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-elevate-cb-cam-lewis-to-active-roster-add-two-to-practice-squad|author=Brown, Chris|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=September 17, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on October 31 for the team's week 8 game against the [[New England Patriots]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bills activate CB Levi Wallace; elevate CB Dane Jackson |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-activate-cb-levi-wallace-elevate-cb-dane-jackson |website=BuffaloBills.com |date=October 31, 2020 |accessdate=November 13, 2020}}</ref> On January 26, 2021, Bryant signed a reserves/futures contract with the Bills.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=January 26, 2021|title=Bills signed these 13 players to reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-signed-these-13-players-to-reserve-future-contracts|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126220319/https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-signed-these-13-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |archive-date=January 26, 2021 |access-date=2021-01-27|website=www.buffalobills.com|language=en-US}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2021 and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills release 23 players to set the initial 2021 53-man roster|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-release-23-players-to-set-the-initial-2021-53-man-roster|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bills sign 15 players to the 2021 practice squad|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-15-players-to-the-2021-practice-squad|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

After the Bills were eliminated in the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs|Divisional Round]] of the 2021 playoffs, Bryant signed a reserve/future contract on January 24, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-10-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-for-2022|work=BuffaloBills.com|title=Bills sign 10 players to reserve/future contracts for 2022|date=January 24, 2022|accessdate=January 24, 2022|first=Chris|last=Jenkins}}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, Bryant was waived by the Bills and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster moves: Bills set initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/roster-moves-bills-set-initial-53-man-roster|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bills sign 13 players to practice squad|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-13-players-to-practice-squad|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 24.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills place Micah Hyde on IR; sign Brandin Bryant, Prince Emili to active roster|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/09/24/bills-place-micah-hyde-on-ir-sign-brandin-bryant-prince-emili-to-active-roster/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=September 24, 2022}}</ref> He was released on November 1.

===Houston Texans===
On November 7, 2022, Bryant was signed to the [[Houston Texans]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (11-7-2022)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-11-7-2022|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=November 7, 2022}}</ref> He was released on December 12.

===Buffalo Bills (second stint)===
On December 13, 2022, the Buffalo Bills signed Bryant to the 53-man roster.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=BuffaloBillsPR |number=1602684814175477762 |title=Bills roster moves: -Signed DT Brandin Bryant to the 53-man roster -Signed WR Cole Beasley to the practice squad -Released DT C.J. Brewer -Released WR Marquez Stevenson from the practice squad}}</ref> On December 19 he was released.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=BuffaloBills |number=1604940886080528384 |title=We’ve activated OL @IkeBoettger from Reserve/PUP and released DT Brandin Bryant.}}</ref> On December 21, he was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=BuffaloBillsPR |number=1605586401965199362 |title=Bills practice squad transactions: Re-signed DT Brandin Bryant to the practice squad Released DT Kendal Vickers from the practice squad}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 23, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jenkins |first=Chris |date=January 23, 2023 |title=Bills signed these players to reserve/future contracts for 2023 |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-signed-these-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-for-2023 |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> He was released on June 1, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=2023-06-01 |title=Bills release Brandin Bryant |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/bills-release-brandin-bryant |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On July 24, 2023, the [[New York Giants]] signed Bryant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Citak |first=Matt |date=July 24, 2023 |title=Giants sign defensive tackle Brandin Bryant; 2 waived |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-defensive-tackle-brandin-bryant-buffalo-bills-florida-atlantic |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was released on August 27.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=August 27, 2023 |title=Giants make series of transactions ahead of NFL roster deadline |url=https://www.giants.com/news/roster-transactions-nfl-deadline-bryce-ford-wheaton-collin-johnson |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State Wolfpack]], and was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the first round of the [[2018 NFL draft]]. Chubb was traded to the [[Miami Dolphins]] in 2022, and played for them until he was released in 2026. == Early life == Chubb was a hybrid [[linebacker]]-[[defensive end]] at [[Hillgrove High School]], where he helped the Hawks advance to the [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] 6A quarterfinals as a senior.{{Cite web |last=Sager II |first=Craig |date=August 30, 2013 |title=College recruits dot rosters in Cobb double-header |url=http://www.scoreatl.com/stories/college-recruits-dot-rosters-in-cobb-double-header/ |access-date=May 9, 2017 |website=Score Atlanta}} He officially committed to [[North Carolina State University]] on June 24, 2013.{{Cite web |title=Bradley Chubb, Hillgrove HS DE – Photos |url=http://www.scout.com/player/177131-bradley-chubb/photos |access-date=May 9, 2017 |website=Scout.com |language=en}} Chubb also had offers from [[Duke University|Duke]], [[West Virginia University|West Virginia]], [[Wake Forest University|Wake Forest]], [[East Carolina University|East Carolina]], and others.{{Cite web |title=Bradley Chubb, N.C. State Wolfpack, Weak-Side Defensive End |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Bradley-Chubb-21847 |access-date=May 9, 2017 |website=247sports.com}} == College career == As a freshman, Chubb received marginal playing time, mostly on special teams. He switched from outside linebacker to defensive end before his sophomore season and broke the starting lineup by the beginning of the season.{{Cite web |title=Bradley Chubb – 2015 Football |url=http://gopack.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2814 |access-date=May 9, 2017 |website=NC State Wolfpack Athletics}} [[File:Bradley Chubb.png|thumb|left|Chubb with the NC State Wolfpack in 2017]] As a junior, he continued to start and became a team leader off the field. He finished third in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] in [[tackles for loss]].{{Cite web |title=Bradley Chubb College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bradley-chubb-1.html |access-date=July 4, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} During the [[2016 Independence Bowl]], Chubb sacked [[2015 Vanderbilt Commodores football team|Vanderbilt]] quarterback [[Kyle Shurmur]], which made a favorable impression on Kyle's father [[Pat Shurmur]], who scouted Chubb extensively in early 2018.{{Cite web |last=Rock |first=Tom |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Chubb's sacking ability hits close to home for Shurmur |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/giants/nfl-draft-bradley-chubb-pat-shurmur-1.17699575 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329120826/https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/giants/nfl-draft-bradley-chubb-pat-shurmur-1.17699575 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 29, 2018 |access-date=March 28, 2018 |website=Newsday |language=en}} In his senior season, Chubb, after winning a game against then-No. 12 [[2017 Florida State Seminoles football team|Florida State]], ran to midfield at FSU's [[Doak Campbell Stadium]] and spat on the Seminole logo in an apparent act of disrespect.{{Cite news |last=Adelson |first=Andrea |date=September 24, 2017 |title=NC State DE spits on FSU (0–2) logo, apologizes |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/20795257/north-carolina-state-de-bradley-chubb-spits-florida-state-seminoles-midfield-logo |access-date=March 29, 2018}} He later apologized for the incident. As for a cause, he alluded to a February 2017 [[Instagram]] post on which some Florida State players negatively commented.{{Cite news |last=Adelson |first=Andrea |date=September 25, 2017 |title=NC State DE regrets spitting, got 'caught up' |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/20809738/bradley-chubb-regrets-spitting-florida-state-midfield-logo-north-carolina-state-win |access-date=March 29, 2018}} On November 4, 2017, playing [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]], Chubb took opposing quarterback [[Kelly Bryant (American football)|Kelly Bryant's]] towel three times. After not eliciting a reaction after the first two, a Clemson offensive lineman held Chubb after the third time until he gave the towel back. Chubb met with officials after the incident but was not penalized.{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Jonathan |date=March 20, 2018 |title=Bradley Chubb Strikes a Balance Between Serious and Fun |language=en |work=SI.com |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/03/20/nfl-draft-2018-bradley-chubb-pro-day-nc-state |access-date=March 28, 2018}} A week later in a game against [[Boston College]], Chubb recorded two and a half sacks to pass [[Mario Williams]] as the all-time sack leader in [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State Wolfpack]] history. In the same game, he also passed Williams to become the Wolfpack leader in tackles for loss.{{Cite news |last=Giglio |first=Joe |date=November 11, 2017 |title=Bradley Chubb dances into NC State record '''Braden Smith''' (born March 25, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Olathe, Kansas]], Smith attended [[Olathe South High School]], where he was a two-way lineman on the [[High school football|football varsity]]. Smith was credited with 82 pancake blocks on offense, 59 tackles on defense in his senior season.

Regarded as a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]], Smith was ranked as the No. 9 offensive guard prospect in the class of 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 ESPN Top Offensive guards |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/playerrankings/_/position/offensive-guard/class/2014/view/position}}</ref> He had offers from Alabama, Texas A&M, Georgia and Notre Dame, and decided to commit to Auburn University on May 27, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Braden Smith commits to Auburn |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Braden-Smith-17692/?PlayerInstitution=28772}}</ref>

==College career==
Smith played as a freshman playing in 12 games. In his sophomore season at Auburn, he played right guard and was named Second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Smith Auburn Profile |url=http://www.auburntigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/braden_smith_907492.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616194038/http://www.auburntigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/braden_smith_907492.html |archive-date=June 16, 2018 |access-date=August 22, 2017}}</ref> Smith received [[2017 College Football All-America Team|All-America]] honors in both 2016 and 2017 as well as received the [[Jacobs Blocking Trophy]] for the best blocker in the SEC in 2017. He finished his collegiate career with 41 starts in four seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.colts.com/team/players-roster/braden-smith/|title = Braden Smith (OT): Bio, News, Stats & more}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts=== 
Smith was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the second round, 37th overall, of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref name="t556">{{cite web | last=Shepherd | first=Chris | title=Indianapolis Colts Select Braden Smith with Pick 37 in NFL Draft | website=Stampede Blue | date=2018-04-27 | url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2018/4/27/17290450/indianapolis-colts-select-braden-smith-with-pick-37-in-nfl-draft | access-date=2024-07-23}}</ref> He was named the starting right tackle in Week 5, and started the final 12 games, as well as both games in the playoffs. He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2018.htm |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Smith was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on December 25, 2020,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hickey, Kevin |date=December 25, 2020 |title=Colts place RT Braden Smith on COVID-19 list |work=USAToday.com |url=https://coltswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/25/indianapolis-colts-braden-smith-covid-19-list/ |access-date=February 8, 2021}}</ref> and activated on December 30.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hickey, Kevin |date=December 30, 2020 |title=Colts activate RT Braden Smith from COVID-19 list |work=USAToday.com |url=https://coltswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/30/indianapolis-colts-braden-smith-activate-covid-19-list/ |access-date=February 8, 2021}}</ref>

On July 28, 2021, Smith signed a four-year, $72.4 million contract extension with the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Mike |date=July 28, 2021 |title=Indianapolis Colts extend RT Braden Smith with $72.4 million contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31904760/indianapolis-colts-extend-rt-braden-smith-724-million-contract |access-date=May 17, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Smith started all 13 appearances for Indianapolis during the 2025 season. On December 13, 2025, Smith was placed on [[injured reserve list|injured reserve]] due to a concussion and neck injury suffered in Week 14 against the [[2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Colts' Braden Smith: Shifts to IR|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/colts-braden-smith-shifts-to-ir/|access-date=December 23, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===

On March 10, 2026, Smith signed with the division rival [[Houston Texans]] on a two-year, $25 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texans reach two-year deal with ex-Colts OT Braden Smith|date=March 10, 2026|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48164400/texans-reach-two-year-deal-ex-colts-ot-braden-smith|access-date= March 13, 2026|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=March 13, 2026|title=The Houston Texans made a roster move|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-13-2026|website=houstontexans.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2024, Smith was diagnosed with a type of [[obsessive–compulsive disorder]] (OCD) called religious [[scrupulosity]]. The disorder caused him to miss playing in the final five games of the 2024 NFL season and nearly drove him to retirement. He traveled to Mexico to be treated with [[ibogaine]] and [[5-MeO-DMT]], as the use of these [[psychedelic]] substances is banned in the United States, before returning home and beginning therapy. He reported improvement in his condition after the treatment.<ref name="IndyStar">{{cite web |last=Erickson |first=Joel A. |title=In his own words: Colts RT Braden Smith's desperate, life-threatening fight vs OCD |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2025/04/08/ocd-colts-tackle-braden-smith-religiously-scrupulosity/82738055007/ |date=April 8, 2025 |access-date=April 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Morse |first=Ben |title=On the brink of retirement, this NFL player turned to psychedelics to help with his OCD |website=[[CNN]] |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/06/25/sport/braden-smith-religious-scrupulosity-ocd-colts-nfl-spt |date=June 25, 2025 |access-date=June 27, 2025}}</ref>

Smith is Christian. He is married; he and his wife have a son.<ref name="IndyStar" />

'''Brady Sheldon''' (born February 23, 1993) is an American professional [[gridiron football]] [[linebacker]] who is a [[free agent]]. He was most recently a member of the [[Edmonton Elks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Ferris State Bulldogs#Football|Ferris State]].

==Professional career==
===Oakland Raiders===
Sheldon signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent on July 14, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Add Three Free Agents|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/raiders-add-three-free-agents/a3514fff-ba5b-4c9b-ae5e-182d426ec571|website=Raiders.com|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=December 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122031324/https://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/raiders-add-three-free-agents/a3514fff-ba5b-4c9b-ae5e-182d426ec571|archive-date=November 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived by the Raiders on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|website=Raiders.com|date=September 2, 2017|access-date=December 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209084351/https://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions/f671cc9c-caa3-429f-992e-5629667b4dec|archive-date=December 9, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on November 21, 2017. He was promoted to the active roster on December 22, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Announce Transactions|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions---December-22-2017/7bf8a8e7-7052-423a-b203-f3f6c8041bb3|website=Raiders.com|date=December 22, 2017|access-date=December 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312202247/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Announce-Transactions---December-22-2017/7bf8a8e7-7052-423a-b203-f3f6c8041bb3|archive-date=March 12, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On June 12, 2018, Sheldon was waived by the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign DT Ahtyba Rubin and DT Frostee Rucker|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-dt-ahtyba-rubin-and-dt-frostee-rucker|website=Raiders.com|date=June 12, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===

'''Bradley Bozeman''' (born November 24, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the sixth round of the [[2018 NFL draft]], he also played for the [[Carolina Panthers]] and [[Los Angeles Chargers]].

==College career==
A native of [[Roanoke, Alabama]], Bozeman was a 4-star offensive line recruit. He committed to play college football at [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] in 2013 over offers from  [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]].<ref name=rolltide/><ref>https://rolltide.com/sports/football/roster/bradley-bozeman/3884</ref> 

Bozeman [[redshirted]] as a true freshman in 2013. The following year, as a redshirt freshman, Bozeman played in nine games, starting two (against Arkansas and Texas A&M).<ref name=rolltide/> In 2015, Bozeman played in all 15 games as a reserve [[guard (American football)|guard]] and [[football center|center]].<ref>https://rolltide.com/sports/football/roster/bradley-bozeman/3884</ref>

Bozeman earned a starting spot at center in 2016, serving as the successor for [[Indianapolis Colts]] first-round draft pick [[Ryan Kelly (American football)|Ryan Kelly]]. He started all 15 games in an offense that had 11 100-yard rushing games.<ref name=rolltide/><ref>https://rolltide.com/sports/football/roster/bradley-bozeman/3884</ref> Bozeman was voted team captain by his teammates for the 2017 season.<ref name="rolltide">{{Cite web |title=Bradley Bozeman - Football |url=http://rolltide.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3884 |access-date=June 8, 2019 |website=University of Alabama Athletics |language=en}}</ref> In his senior year, as a starting center, he helped Alabama win the [[2018 College Football Playoff National Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 CFP National Championship |url=https://collegefootballplayoff.com/sports/2018/1/11/game-recap-2018.aspx}}</ref> He was named [[2017 All-SEC football team|Second Team All-SEC]] for his redshirt senior season.<ref>https://rolltide.com/sports/football/roster/bradley-bozeman/3884</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Bozeman was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the sixth round (215th overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=April 28, 2018 |title=Round 6: Ravens Select C Bradley Bozeman at No. 215 |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/round-6-ravens-select-c-bradley-bozeman-at-no-215-20609633 |access-date=May 19, 2018 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He played in 14 games as a rookie, starting one game, against the [[New Orleans Saints]], at [[left guard]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Bozeman 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BozeBr00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=June 8, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In his second season, Bozeman was named starting left guard, and started every game of the 2019 and 2020 seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Bozeman 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BozeBr00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=October 6, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bradley Bozeman 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BozeBr00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2021, he made the shift to being the starting center.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Baltimore Ravens Roster & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/rav/2021_roster.htm |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On March 18, 2022, Bozeman signed a one-year contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt, Darin |date=March 18, 2022 |title=Panthers agree to terms with center Bradley Bozeman |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-agree-to-terms-with-center-bradley-bozeman |website=Panthers.com}}</ref>

On March 13, 2023, Bozeman signed a three-year, $18 million contract extension with the Panthers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers bring back Bradley Bozeman|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-bring-back-bradley-bozeman|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=March 13, 2023}}</ref>

On March 13, 2024, Bozeman was released by the Panthers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers release three players at start of league year|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-release-three-players-at-start-of-league-year|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=March 13, 2024}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On March 18, 2024, Bozeman signed with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Bradley Bozeman|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-bradley-bozeman-2024|website=Chargers.com|date=March 18, 2024}}</ref> He was named the starting center, and started all 17 games.

On March 10, 2025, Bozeman signed a two-year, $6.5 million contract extension with the Chargers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Agree to Extensions with Bozeman and Scott|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/agree-to-extensions-with-bradely-bozeman-and-jk-scott-2025|website=Chargers.com|date=March 10, 2025}}</ref>

During the 2025-26 NFL season Bozeman was graded as the worst center among qualified players.  

On February 23, 2026, Bozeman announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-23 |title=Chargers' Bradley Bozeman: Retires after eight seasons |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chargers-bradley-bozeman-retires-after-eight-seasons/ |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bozeman proposed to Alabama basketball player Nikki Hegstetter in 2018, after the College Football Playoff championship game against Georgia.<ref name="h931">{{cite web | last=Anderson | first=Joel | title=Take a knee: Bama center proposes after win | website=ESPN.com | date=2018-01-09 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/22011046/alabama-crimson-tide-center-bradley-bozeman-proposes-girlfriend-national-title-win?device=featurephone | access-date=2024-10-10}}</ref> They married on March 23, 2019.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}}

During the 2019 NFL season, Bozeman and his wife Nikki lived full-time in an [[Recreational vehicle|RV]] they had bought for offseason travel, but soon decided to live full-time in it. In a 2020 [[ESPN]] story, Bozeman estimated that the move saved them about $1,800 per month in rent. After the season, they traveled the U.S. in a smaller donated RV, combining anti-bullying presentations to student groups with sightseeing side trips until their venture was cut short due to [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The couple initially planned to live in their larger RV for at least two more years, but found a house they felt they could not pass up, and planned to move into it upon their return from their cross-country trip.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hensley |first=Jamison |date=March 14, 2020 |title=Living the RV life with Ravens lineman Bradley Bozeman |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28893198/living-rv-life-ravens-lineman-bradley-bozeman |access-date=March 14, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In 2018, Bozeman and Nikki founded the Bradley & Nikki Bozeman Foundation, which focuses on at-risk children and their families to educate them on the dangers of childhood bullying.<ref name="m100">{{cite web | last=Mink | first=Ryan | title=Why Bradley Bozeman Is Ravens’ Walter Payton Man of the Year | website=Baltimore Ravens | date=2020-12-10 | url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/why-bradley-bozeman-is-ravens-walter-payton-man-of-the-year | access-date=2024-10-10}}</ref> In 2020, the foundation held a number of food drives in partnership with Mount Pleasant Church and Ministries.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-09 |title=The Bradley and Nikki Bozeman Foundation holds food drive |url=https://www.wmar2news.com/news/local-news/the-bradley-and-nikki-bozeman-foundation-holds-food-drive |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=WMAR 2 News Baltimore |language=en}}</ref>

'''Braden Mann''' (born November 24, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]]. During his junior season, he received [[List of unanimous All-Americans in college football|unanimous All-American]] honors and won the [[Ray Guy Award]]. He also broke the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS) records for single-game punting average, single-season punts of 60-plus yards and single-season punting average.

==Early life==
Mann played kicker and punter at [[Cy-Fair High School]] in [[Cypress, Texas]], under the tutelage of head coach Ed Pustejovsky, a former Texas A&M football player. As a junior, Mann scored 7-of-10 [[field goals]] (with a long of 49 yards) and 46-of-48 [[Conversion (gridiron football)|extra points]]. He was named to the 2014 ''[[Houston Chronicle]]'' All-Greater Houston team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Verdejo |first=Angel Jr. |date=December 24, 2014 |title=The Chronicle's 2014 All-Greater Houston football team |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/article/All-Greater-Houston-FootballRODNEY-ANDERSON-5978596.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210015858/https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/article/All-Greater-Houston-FootballRODNEY-ANDERSON-5978596.php |archive-date=December 10, 2018 |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> As a senior, he scored 25-of-25 extra points and recorded a 45-yard punting average on 41 punts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coleman |first=Adam |date=January 16, 2016 |title=Cy-Fair's Mann has a leg up on competition - HoustonChronicle.com |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/highschool/article/Cy-Fair-s-Mann-has-a-leg-up-on-competition-6764461.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209124344/https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/highschool/article/Cy-Fair-s-Mann-has-a-leg-up-on-competition-6764461.php |archive-date=December 9, 2018 |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> Following his senior season, Mann played in the [[Under Armour All-America Game]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cook |first=Kevin |date=October 21, 2015 |title=Cy-Fair kicker Braden Mann selected to All-America Game |work=Chron |url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/champions-klein/sports/article/Cy-Fair-kicker-Braden-Mann-selected-to-9828735.php |url-status=live |access-date=October 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021111431/https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/champions-klein/sports/article/Cy-Fair-kicker-Braden-Mann-selected-to-9828735.php |archive-date=October 21, 2018}}</ref>

Though Mann wanted to play linebacker in high school and college, he was not able to do so due to his size and injuries.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Texas A&M's Braden Mann takes over pressurized gig at 'Punter U' |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Texas-A-M-s-Braden-Mann-takes-over-Punter-U-13144215.php |url-status=live |access-date=October 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021111606/https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Texas-A-M-s-Braden-Mann-takes-over-Punter-U-13144215.php |archive-date=October 21, 2018}}</ref> As a [[college football]] recruit, he was rated nationally as the number two kicker by [[Rivals.com]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Braden Mann, 2016 Kicker |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/braden-mann-8216 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023120008/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/braden-mann-8216 |archive-date=October 23, 2018 |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=Rivals}}</ref> and the number five kicker by [[247Sports.com]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Top Kicker Recruits |url=https://247sports.com/college/mount-st-marys/Season/2016-Football/CompositeRecruitRankings/?Position=K |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=247Sports}}</ref>

==College career==
Mann was primarily the kickoff specialist during his first two years at Texas A&M. During his freshman season, he averaged 63.9 yards on 76 kickoffs, and as a sophomore, he averaged 62.4 yards on 73 kickoffs. He was not the starting punter during his freshman year and only punted the ball twice during the season (two punts for 94 yards, or a 47.0 average). As a sophomore, he did not punt at all and made only one kicking attempt, which came when he missed a 43-yard field goal try in the season-opening 44–45 loss to [[2017 UCLA Bruins football team|UCLA]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ochoa |first=Abigail |date=October 12, 2018 |title=Aggies find unassuming star in junior Braden Mann, one of the best punters in the NCAA |work=The Battalion |url=http://www.thebatt.com/sports/aggies-find-unassuming-star-in-junior-braden-mann-one-of/article_26d02e4a-cddd-11e8-8d96-d3d9c2c15d8d.html |access-date=January 3, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas A&M vs. UCLA – Play-By-Play – September 3, 2017 |url=http://www.espn.com/college-football/playbyplay?gameId=400933838 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181118205842/http://www.espn.com/college-football/playbyplay?gameId=400933838 |archive-date=November 18, 2018 |access-date=January 3, 2019 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Mann was drafted by the [[New York Jets]] in the sixth round with the 191st overall pick in the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mehta |first=Manish |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Jets draft Texas A&M punter Braden Mann in sixth round |work=[[New York Daily News]] |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/jets/ny-braden-mann-punter-texas-am-20200425-dmlz77rkizgsvb66b2knh5ttzi-story.html |access-date=April 26, 2020}}</ref>

During the game against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Mann made a game-saving, open-field tackle on punt returner [[Nsimba Webster]] that helped seal the Jets' 23–20 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Costello |first=Brian |date=December 26, 2020 |title=Jets punter's tackle may have massive Trevor Lawrence implications |url=https://nypost.com/2020/12/26/jets-punters-tackle-may-have-massive-trevor-lawrence-implications/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=New York Post |language=en-US}}</ref> The Jets finished the season 2–14. Mann compiled 3,598 total yards, with a 43.9 punting average. His 3,598 total yards made him the 2020 [[List of National Football League annual punting yards leaders|NFL punting yards leader]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/stats/player-stats/category/punts/2020/REG/all/puntingyards/DESC|title=2020 NFL punts stats – Players|website=[[NFL.com]] }}</ref>

On September 14, 2021, Mann was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Greenberg |first1=Ethan |last2=Allen |first2=Eric |date=September 14, 2021 |title=Jets Sign 4 Players; Place 4 on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-4-players-place-4-on-injured-reserve |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was activated on November 13.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=November 13, 2021 |title=Jets Activate P Braden Mann, OL Conor McDermott; Place OL Chuma Edoga on IR |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-p-braden-mann-ol-conor-mcdermott-place-ol-chuma-edoga-on-ir |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

In Week 2 of the 2022 season, Mann had two punts inside the 20 with a long of 50 yards. He also had a 17-yard completion and had a successful onside kick in a 31–30 win over the Cleveland Browns, earning AFC Special Teams Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=September 21, 2022 |title=Dolphins QB Tua Tagovailoa, Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2022-week-2-tua-tagovailoa-amon-ra-st-brown |access-date=April 6, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On April 13, 2023, Mann was waived by the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Costello |first=Brian |date=April 13, 2023 |title=Jets move on from punter Braden Mann after three inconsistent seasons |url=https://nypost.com/2023/04/13/jets-waive-punter-braden-mann-after-three-seasons/ |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=NYPost.com}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On April 17, 2023, Mann was claimed off waivers by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=April 17, 2023 |title=Steelers sign Muse; claim Mann |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-muse-claim-mann |access-date=August 27, 2023 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> On August 30, Mann was waived by the Steelers.<ref name="u939">{{cite magazine | last=Thompson | first=Stephen | title=Steelers Cut Former Jets Punter | magazine=Sports Illustrated | date=2023-08-30 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/steelers/news/pittsburgh-steelers-cut-former-jets-punter-braden-mann | access-date=2024-10-11}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia Eagles ===
On September 18, 2023, Mann signed with the [[practice squad]] of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=September 18, 2023 |title=Eagles Signing P Braden Mann To Practice Squad |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/eagles-signing-p-braden-mann-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=September 18, 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2023 |title=Eagles sign Braden Mann to the active roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-braden-mann-brandon-smith |access-date=2024-10-11 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> On December 11, Mann faked a punt and threw a 28-yard completion to WR [[Olamide Zaccheaus]] in a 13–33 loss to the [[2023 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]].<ref name="k778">{{cite web | last=Erby | first=Glenn | title=Twitter reacts to Eagles successful fake punt and pass vs. Cowboys | website=Eagles Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2023-12-10 | url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/lists/eagles-cowboys-twitter-reaction-fake-punt-braden-mann-olamide-zaccheaus/ | access-date=2025-02-11}}</ref>

On March 12, 2024, Mann signed a two-year contract extension with the Eagles.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Boyle |first1=Owen |last2=McPherson |first2=Chris |date=March 12, 2024 |title=Eagles agree to terms with Rick Lovato, Braden Mann |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-terms-with-rick-lovato-braden-mann |access-date=2024-10-11 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week following a 24–19 win over the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 13.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McPherson|first=Chris|date=December 4, 2024|title=Braden Mann named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/braden-mann-named-nfc-special-teams-player-of-the-week |access-date=2024-12-04|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Mann won his first Super Bowl when the Eagles defeated the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], 40–22, in [[Super Bowl LIX]]. He punted twice in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIX - Kansas City Chiefs at Philadelphia Eagles - February 9th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202502090phi.htm |access-date=2025-02-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2026, Mann signed a four-year, $14 million contract extension with the Eagles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles, Braden Mann agree to terms on four-year deal|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-braden-mann-agree-to-terms|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=March 13, 2026}}</ref>

'''Bradlee Joseph Ioane Anae''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|n|aɪ}} {{respell|ə|NY}}; born October 17, 1998) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]]/[[defensive lineman]] for the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]].

==Early life==
Anae grew up in [[Laie, Hawaii]] and attended [[Kahuku High & Intermediate School]], where he was a member of the basketball, football, and track teams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olson |first=Max |date=August 6, 2019 |title=Bradlee Anae pets sharks, jumps off cliffs and makes Utah something to fear |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1117957/2019/08/06/bradlee-anae-cliffs-sharks-utah-defense/ |access-date=December 4, 2019 |work=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref> As a senior, he contributed to the school earning a 13-0 record and winning the Division 1 state title. He received All-state and second-team All-USA Hawaii honors. He is of Samoan descent.<ref>{{cite web |last=Etches |first=Melina |title=Bradlee Anae living his dream as NFL player in America |work=Cook Islands News |date=2024-07-06 |url=https://www.cookislandsnews.com/rugby-league/internal/sport/features/weekend/bradlee-anae-living-his-dream-as-nfl-player-in-america/ |access-date=2025-05-12}}</ref>

Rated a three-star recruit, Anae committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Utah]] over offers from Vanderbilt and BYU.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stark |first=Alex |date=February 3, 2016 |title=Signing Day Commit No. 2: DE Bradlee Anae |url=https://www.blocku.com/2016/2/3/10905942/signing-day-commit-no-2-de-bradlee-anae |access-date=December 4, 2019 |website=BlockU.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref> He followed his older sister Adora, who was a volleyball scholar athlete at the school.

==College career==
Anae played in six games for Utah as a true freshman defensive end backup, recording four tackles and two sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Utah football: When it comes to the defensive line, Utes are in the deep end |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2017/08/18/utah-football-when-it-comes-to-the-defensive-line-utes-are-in-the-deep-end/ |work=Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref> He started 9 games at right defensive end and one at defensive tackle for the Utes during his sophomore year, registering 39 total tackles, 3 forced fumbles, with a team-leading 7.0 sacks and tying for the team lead with 10.0 tackles for loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gunther |first=Kyle |date=January 30, 2018 |title=Bradlee Anae is the most important defensive player for the Utes in 2018 |url=https://espn700sports.com/local-sports/bradlee-anae-is-the-most-important-defensive-player-for-the-utes-in-2018/ |access-date=April 5, 2020 |work=[[KALL|ESPN700Sports.com]]}}</ref>

As a junior, he started all 14 games (the last 11 at right defensive end). He led the [[Pac-12 Conference]] with 8.0 sacks and finished third in the conference with 15.5 tackles for loss along with 51 total tackles (fifth on the team), three passes broken up, 2 forced fumbles and was named first-team All-Pac-12.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL teams would have drafted Ute defensive linemen Bradlee Anae |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2019/04/21/nfl-teams-would-have/ |work=Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref> He considered entering the [[2019 NFL draft]], but ultimately decided to return for his senior season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why Utah's Bradlee Anae and Leki Fotu are returning for their senior seasons |url=https://www.deseret.com/2019/4/5/20670145/why-utah-s-bradlee-anae-and-leki-fotu-are-returning-for-their-senior-seasons |access-date=April 5, 2020 |work=Deseret News |date=April 5, 2019}}</ref>

As a senior, he started all 14 games at left defensive end and was part of a stout defensive unit that saw 6 players selected in the [[2020 NFL draft]]. Anae was named preseason first-team All-Pac-12 and to the [[Bednarik Award]] watch list going into his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mauss |first=Jeremy |date=July 26, 2019 |title=Utah's Bradlee Anae Did Not Say That Offensive Quote About BYU |url=https://kslsports.com/413739/utahs-bradlee-anae-did-not-say-that-offensive-quote-about-byu/? |access-date=April 5, 2020 |website=[[KSL (radio network)|KSL.com]]}}</ref> He tied the Utah career sack record with 29.5 after posting 1.5 sacks against Colorado on November 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New co-mayor of Sack Lake City: Bradlee Anae ties Utah sack record in win over Colorado |url=https://www.deseret.com/2019/11/30/20989169/new-co-mayor-of-sack-lake-city-bradlee-anae-ties-utah-sack-record-in-win-over-colorado |access-date=April 5, 2020 |work=Deseret News |date=December 2019}}</ref> Anae broke the career sack record in the [[2019 Alamo Bowl]], the final game of his career, with a half sack against the [[University of Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Genessy |first=Jody |date=December 31, 2019 |title=Bradlee Anae gives Utes one positive to remember about the Alamo Bowl, becomes all-time sacks leader |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2019/12/31/21045153/bradlee-anae-utah-utes-alamo-bowl-sacks-texas-longhorns |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=Deseret News}}</ref> Anae finished his senior season with 14 starts, 41 tackles, 13.0 sacks, 14.0 tackles for loss and a forced fumble, while being named first-team All-Pac-12, consensus All-American selection, received the [[Morris Trophy]] as the best defensive lineman in the Pac-12 and was a finalist for the [[Ted Hendricks Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kragthorpe |first=Kurt |date=December 19, 2019 |title=Utah's Bradlee Anae clinches consensus All-America status and the Utes land their highest-ranked recruit |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2019/12/19/utahs-bradlee-anae/ |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Kostecka |first=Ryan |date=December 11, 2019 |title=Anae wins Morris Trophy for top Pac-12 defensive lineman |url=https://www.si.com/college/utah/football/bradlee-anae-wins-morris-trophy-for-top-pac-12-defensive-lineman |access-date=January 2, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]}}</ref> He also participated in the [[2020 Senior Bowl]], where he had 3 sacks and received defensive MVP honors.

He finished his college career with 38 starts out of 47 games, 30 sacks (school record), 210 sack yards (school record), 41.5 tackles for loss (fourth in school history), 245 tackle for loss yards (school record) and 6 forced fumbles (tied for eighth in school history).

===Dallas Cowboys===
Anae was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fifth round with the 179th overall pick in the [[2020 NFL draft]], after dropping because he didn't test well at the [[NFL Scouting Combine]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gehlken |first=Michael |date=April 25, 2020 |title=The Cowboys drafted Bradlee Anae late, and a disappointing 40-yard dash might be the culprit |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/cowboys/2020/04/25/the-cowboys-drafted-bradlee-anae-late-and-a-disappointing-40-yard-dash-might-be-the-culprit/ |access-date=April 26, 2020}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in the first six games with minimum playing opportunities. After [[defensive end]] [[Randy Gregory]] returned from his suspension, Anae was declared inactive in nine of the last 10 contests. It was later reported in the media, that the team's [[defensive end]] depth and his struggles against the run were the reasons for his lack of playing time. He played mainly on [[special teams]] and had one defensive tackle.

On September 24, 2021, he was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list. On October 6, he was activated from the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list. On November 2, Anae was waived after committing a defensive offsides penalty on fourth-and-5 in the second quarter against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], that kept a drive alive. On November 4, he was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys roster move: Dallas waives defensive end Bradlee Anae after playing 11 games with team|url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2021/11/2/22760037/cowboys-roster-move-dallas-waives-defensive-end-bradlee-anae-after-playing-11-games-with-team|work=Blogging the Boys|publisher=SB Nation|date=November 2, 2021}}</ref> He appeared in 4 games as a backup defensive end, making 2 defensive tackles.

===New York Jets (first stint)===
On January 19, 2022, Anae signed a reserve/future contract with the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign DL Bradlee Anae to Reserve/Future Contract|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-dl-bradlee-anae-to-reserve-future-contract|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=January 19, 2022}}</ref> He was waived on August 30, and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Final Cuts: Jets Move 27 Players to Trim Roster to NFL's 53-Man Limit|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-53-man-roster-2022-season|last1=Lange|first1=Randy|last2=Greenberg|first2=Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign 13 Players to Practice Squad|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-practice-squad-2022-season|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> On January 7, 2023, he was promoted to the active roster to provide depth for the season finale against the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place 5 on Injured Reserve, Sign 5 to Active Roster for Season Finale vs. Dolphins|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-5-on-injured-reserve-sign-5-to-active-roster-for-season-finale-vs-dol|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=January 7, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2023|archive-date=January 10, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230110024045/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-5-on-injured-reserve-sign-5-to-active-roster-for-season-finale-vs-dol|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2023, he returned to the team to compete for a roster position. He was placed on injured reserve on May 25, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign WR Jerome Kapp|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-wr-jerome-kapp|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=May 25, 2023}}</ref> He became an unrestricted free agent and was not re-signed at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=D-Line Reset, Jets' Powerful Line Plans to Keep Up the Pressure in '24 |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-defensive-line-2023-reset-quinnen-williams-jermaine-johnson-bryce-huff|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=January 23, 2024}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On May 13, 2024, Anae signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falcons sign TE Ross Dwelley plus 3 rookie minicamp tryout players |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/ross-dwelley-bradlee-anae-dane-cruikshank-dylan-drummond-sign |access-date=2024-05-13 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> He was waived on August 25.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons begin 53-man roster cutdown, release 13 players|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/transaction-13-players-released-donavan-mutin-lukas-denis-bradlee-anae|author=Waack, Terrin|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=August 25, 2024}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Stallions (first stint) ===
On November 18, 2024, Anae signed with the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Larnsen |first1=James |title=Stallions Sign Bradlee Anae & Stantley Thomas-Oliver |url=https://pfnewsroom.com/news/stallions-sign-bradlee-anae-stantley-thomas-oliver/ |access-date=18 November 2024 |work=Pro Football Newsroom |date=November 18, 2024 }}</ref>

===New York Jets (second stint)===
On December 18, 2024, the [[New York Jets]] signed Anae to their practice squad. The Jets did not sign Anae to a reserve/future contract at the end of the [[2024 NFL season]], leaving him as a free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=S Jalen Mills Placed on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jalen-mills-placed-on-injured-reserve-12-18-2024|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 18, 2024}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Stallions (second stint) ===
On January 16, 2025, Anae was re-signed by the Stallions.

===San Francisco 49ers===
On August 4, 2025, Anae signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-announce-roster-moves-x1591|website=49ers.com|date=August 4, 2025|access-date=August 5, 2025}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 13, and was released shortly after.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign WR Turner; Place DL Anae on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-wr-turner-place-dl-anae-on-injured-reserve|website=49ers.com|date=August 13, 2025|access-date=August 14, 2025}}</ref>

=== BC Lions ===
On September 9, 2025, Anae signed as a defensive lineman with the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baker |first=Matt |date=2025-09-08 |title=Lions Sign DL Bradlee Anae & OL Brandon Yates |url=https://www.bclions.com/2025/09/08/lions-sign-dl-bradlee-anae-ol-brandon-yates-to-practice-roster/ |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=BC Lions |language=en}}</ref> On September 18, 2025, Anae was placed on the Lions' 1-game injured list. ==Personal life==
Anae's father, [[Brad Anae]], played college football at [[BYU Cougars football|BYU]] and was an honorable mention All-American in 1980 and a third-team All-America selection in 1981 and played three seasons in the [[United States Football League]].
