'''Brady Joe McDonnell''' (born July 24, 1977) is an American [[auto racing]] driver and former [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] who played for the [[New York Giants]] and [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[University of Colorado Boulder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McDoBr20.htm |title=Brady McDonnell Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |access-date=2020-01-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bradymcdonnell/2504505/profile |title=Brady McDonnell, TE |work=Nfl.com |access-date=2020-01-19}}</ref>

McDonnell started all four years at [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]] and was a team captain in his senior year. After going unselected in the [[2001 NFL draft]], he was picked up by the Giants but missed the season due to a knee injury he suffered in training camp.<ref name="Football still on mind">{{cite news|last=Holland|first=Jim|url=https://rapidcityjournal.com/article_299b2a85-76cc-5dd0-be42-001675768cf8.html|title=Football still on mind of driver, NFL veteran|newspaper=[[Rapid City Journal]]|date=August 12, 2009|access-date=March 6, 2025}}</ref> He signed with the Bills in 2002 and was converted to tight end.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/concord-monitor-bills-sign-tight-end-mcd/167391403/|title=Bills sign tight end McDonnell|newspaper=[[Concord Monitor]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 4, 2002|access-date=March 6, 2025}}</ref> Officially, he was with the Bills through 2004 but noted "only two of them were actually playing," having spent his final season on the [[injured reserve list]].<ref name="Football still on mind" />

After retiring from football, McDonnell returned to [[Rapid City, South Dakota]], to work for a medical supply company. He later became a [[dirt track racing]] driver alongside his brothers Jay and Travis.<ref name="Football still on mind" /> Brady and Travis also compete in [[off-road racing]] like their father Steve; McDonnell has raced events like the [[Mint 400]] with Steve's vintage 1987 Ford, which he and Jay restored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://unlimitedoffroadracing.com/drivers/brady-mcdonnell/|title=Brady McDonnell|work=Unlimited Off-Road Racing|access-date=March 7, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250307022751/https://unlimitedoffroadracing.com/drivers/brady-mcdonnell/|archive-date=March 7, 2025}}</ref> The McDonnells also operate a farm near [[Wall, South Dakota]].<ref name="Football still on mind" />

'''Bradley Sylve''' (born January 29, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], and was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an undrafted free agent in 2017.

== College career ==
Sylve spent 2011–2015 at Alabama primarily in the reserve, logging 40 tackles (9 on special teams) and 7 pass breakups.<ref name=":0" /> He started 3 games in 2013, one game in 2014, and was one of the Alabama's four Special Teams Players of the Year.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2016/03/alabama_nfl_draft_hopeful_brad.html|title=Tide draft hopeful on injury: 'I just put my head down and started crying'|last=Zenitz|first=Mark|date=March 17, 2016|website=AL.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-11}}</ref> With the Crimson Tide, Sylve won 2 [[BCS National Championship Game]]s, in 2011 and 2012.<ref name=":2" />

The day before Alabama's Pro Day in 2016, he suffered a torn Achilles tendon.<ref name=":1" />

== Professional career ==

=== Buffalo Bills ===
On April 7, 2017, Sylve was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Robert |date=April 7, 2017 |title=Bills sign speedy former Alabama CB Bradley Sylve |url=https://billswire.usatoday.com/2017/04/07/bills-sign-speedy-former-alabama-cb-bradley-sylve/ |access-date=2020-02-10 |website=Bills Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en}}</ref> He was waived on September 1.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://billswire.usatoday.com/2017/09/01/bills-roster-cut-down-tracker/|title=All of the players released by the Bills in roster cut down|last=Silagyi|first=Kyle|last2=Saeli|first2=Victoria|date=September 1, 2017|website=Bills Wire|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Saints ===
On September 20, 2017, Sylve was signed to the [[New Orleans Saints]]' practice squad.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2017/09/bradley_sylve_returning_to_an.html|title=Bradley Sylve returning to an NFL roster|last=Inabinett|first=Mark|date=September 20, 2017|website=AL.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref> On October 10, he was cut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_5e3f2c45-860b-5927-a03c-adb9d9304095.html|title=Saints waive linebacker, shuffle practice squad by adding Shayne Skov, Woodrow Hamilton|last=Erickson|first=Joel|date=October 10, 2017|website=NOLA.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref> On January 5, 2018, Sylve was signed to a reserve/futures contract with the Saints.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2018/01/bradley_sylve_gets_another_nfl.html|title=Bradley Sylve gets another NFL opportunity|last=Inabinett|first=Mark|date=January 5, 2018|website=AL.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref> He was waived on May 14, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/c8492992c2034b739247e26001d9c193|title=Saints add 4 players, waive 4 others after rookie camp|date=May 14, 2018|website=AP NEWS|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Iron ===
Sylve was signed to the [[Birmingham Iron]] in 2019 and competed in 8 games before the [[Alliance of American Football]] folded on April 2, 2019. He recorded 30 tackles and two interceptions, picking off [[Mike Bercovici]] of the [[San Diego Fleet]] & [[Matt Simms (American football)|Matt Simms]] of the [[Atlanta Legends]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2019/03/birmingham-iron-snaps-2-game-losing-skid-as-nick-novak-makes-field-goal-on-final-play.html|title=Birmingham Iron wins on FG as time expires|last=Dudley|first=Evan|date=March 18, 2019|website=AL.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2019/03/nick-novaks-3-fgs-trent-richardsons-td-clinches-playoff-berth-for-birmingham-iron.html|title=Iron clinches playoff berth with win|last=Dudley|first=Evan|date=March 31, 2019|website=AL.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-10}}</ref>

=== DC Defenders ===
Sylve was drafted by the [[DC Defenders]] in the 5th round in phase 4 of the [[2020 XFL draft]]. In his first career game with the Defenders, Sylve picked off [[Brandon Silvers]] and took it back, marking the first defensive touchdown in the XFL. The Defenders would defeat the [[Seattle Dragons]] 31–19.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/teams/washington-dc/defenders-articles/three-stars-defenders-vs-dragons|title=Three Stars: Defenders vs. Dragons|date=February 8, 2020|website=XFL.com|language=en|access-date=2020-02-09}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Wildcats ===
On February 14, 2020, Sylve was traded to the [[Los Angeles Wildcats (XFL)|Los Angeles Wildcats]] in exchange for [[Anthony Johnson (defensive lineman)|Anthony Johnson]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://xflnewsroom.com/news/anthony-johnson-traded-to-dc-defenders/|title=Anthony Johnson Traded to DC Defenders|last=Rachuk|first=Stephan|date=February 14, 2020|website=XFL Newsroom|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-14}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Stars===
Sylve was selected in the 11th round of the [[2022 USFL draft]] by the [[Philadelphia Stars (2022)|Philadelphia Stars]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Inabinett |first1=Mark |title=Bradley Sylve trying another spring football league |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2022/02/bradley-sylve-trying-another-spring-football-league.html |access-date=March 5, 2022 |work=[[Al.com]] |date=February 22, 2022}}</ref> After suffering an ankle injury before the start of the regular season,<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Week 1 Game Status Update: |number=1515148804772843527 |date=April 15, 2022 |access-date=April 16, 2022}}</ref> he was transferred to the team's practice squad on April 16, 2022.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Roster Updates: Transferred to practice squad: |number=1515218725787639811 |date=April 16, 2022 |access-date=April 16, 2022}}</ref> He remained on the inactive roster on April 22, 2022,<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Transferred to inactive roster |number=1517403351574409217 |date=April 22, 2022 |access-date=April 23, 2022}}</ref> with the injury.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Game Status Report |number=1517420525017989120 |date=April 22, 2022 |access-date=April 23, 2022}}</ref> He was transferred to the active roster on May 5.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Roster Updates |number=1522129729679024129 |date=May 5, 2022 |access-date=May 5, 2022}}</ref> He was transferred back to the inactive roster on May 14.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Roster Updates |number=1525587027365965824 |date=May 14, 2022 |access-date=May 16, 2022}}</ref> On February 23, 2023, Sylve was released by the Stars.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Released |number= 1628956453506813954 |date=February 23, 2023 |access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref>

'''Brady Christensen''' (born September 27, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive guard]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|BYU Cougars]] and was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Christensen grew up in [[Bountiful, Utah]], and attended [[Bountiful High School]]. Christensen was rated a two-star recruit and originally committed to play [[college football]] at the [[US Air Force Academy]] before changing his commitment to BYU. After graduating from Bountiful and prior to attending BYU, he served a 2-year mission for [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] in [[Hamilton, New Zealand]], from 2015 to 2016.<ref name=mainstay>{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/byu-cougars/2018/10/09/byu-freshman-left-tackle/|title=BYU freshman left tackle Brady Christensen doesn't have a flashy resume, but the late bloomer has emerged as a mainstay on the Cougars' offensive line|first=Jay|last=Drew|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=October 9, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
Christensen redshirted his true freshman season at BYU after returning from his mission. He became the Cougars' starting left tackle going into his redshirt freshman season and started every game for them over the next two seasons.<ref name=mainstay/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Drew |first=Jay |date=May 6, 2020 |title=BYU football: Redshirt junior Brady Christensen has a big decision to make after the 2020 college football season |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/5/6/21247003/byu-football-returned-missionary-brady-christensen-eric-mateos-james-empey-kalani-sitake-lds-mormon |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=[[Deseret News]]}}</ref> As a redshirt junior, he was named a consensus first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/byu/Article/Brady-Christensen-All-America-Team-157772305/|title=Brady Christensen: From Two-Star to All-America|first=Jeff|last=Hansen|website=[[247Sports]]|date=December 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://kslsports.com/448176/brady-christensen-byu-football-penei-sewell/?|title=BYU's Brady Christensen Putting Together Season That Compares To Penei Sewell|first=Mitch|last=Harper|website=[[KSL (radio network)|KSL.com]]|date=December 10, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2021/1/8/22220947/byu-football-brady-christensen-zach-wilson-consensus-all-american-nfl-draft-ty-detmer|title=BYU offensive lineman Brady Christensen becomes Cougars' first consensus All-American since 2009|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=January 8, 2021|access-date=January 9, 2021}}</ref> Following the end of the season, he announced that he would forgo his remaining collegiate eligibility to enter the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/byu/news/brady-christensen-declares-for-the-nfl-draft|title=Brady Christensen Declares for the NFL Draft|first=Casey|last=Lundquist|website=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=December 30, 2020|access-date=January 9, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==

Christensen was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the third round (70th overall) of the 2021 NFL draft.<ref>{{cite news |author=Bryan, Will |title=Panthers draft offensive tackle Brady Christensen in third round |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-draft-offensive-tackle-brady-christensen-in-third-round |website=Panthers.com |date=April 30, 2021 |access-date=May 8, 2021}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract with Carolina on June 24, 2021, worth $5.16 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers Sign Brady Christensen|url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/06/panthers-sign-brady-christensen|work=Pro Football Rumors|date=June 24, 2021}}</ref> He was named a backup tackle as a rookie, but started six games due to injuries.

In 2022, Christensen was named the Panthers starting left guard, starting all 17 games. In the season finale against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he suffered a broken left ankle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Panthers G Brady Christensen sustained broken ankle in Week 18|url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2023/01/09/panthers-g-brady-christensen-broken-ankle-austin-corbett-week-18/|access-date=January 2, 2024|website=pantherswire.usatoday.com|language=en}}</ref>

Christensen returned to his starting role in 2023, but suffered a biceps injury in Week 1 and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 13, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers place Brady Christensen on injured reserve|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-place-brady-christensen-on-injured-reserve|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=September 13, 2023}}</ref>

On March 12, 2025, Christensen re-signed with the Panthers on a one-year, $2.8 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Panthers agree to terms with Brady Christensen |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-agree-to-terms-with-brady-christensen-offensive-line |access-date=2025-03-13 |website=Panthers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He made eight appearances (four starts) for Carolina during the regular season. In Week 8 against the [[2025 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]], Christensen suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|torn Achilles tendon]], causing him to be placed on season-ending injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Panthers place OL Brady Christensen on season-ending IR, sign QB to active roster|url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/panthers/2025/10/30/panthers-brady-christensen-injured-reserve-mike-white/86948821007/|access-date=November 2, 2025|website=pantherswire.usatoday.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Brandin Echols''' (born October 16, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Northwest Mississippi Community College]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky]] and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the sixth round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=MacGregor |date=May 1, 2021 |title=2021 NFL Draft Results: Jets Select Brandin Echols With 200th Overall Pick |url=https://www.ganggreennation.com/2021/5/1/22414657/2021-nfl-draft-results-jets-select-brandin-echols-with-200th-overall-pick |access-date=May 19, 2023 |website=Gang Green Nation |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Echols played [[college football]] at [[Northwest Mississippi Rangers football|Northwest Mississippi]] in 2017 and 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nwccrangers.com/sports/football/roster/brandin-echols/2013|title=Brandin Echols - Football|website=Northwest Mississippi Community College Athletics}}</ref> He began his college career as a [[wide receiver]] and switched to defensive back as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2018/12/19/nsd-2019-brandin-echols/|title=NSD 2019 – Brandin Echols|date=December 19, 2018|via=ukathletics.com}}</ref> In 2018, he was named second-team NJCAA All-American.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nwccrangers.com/news/2021/5/1/football-echols-selected-by-new-york-jets-in-2021-nfl-draft.aspx|title=Jets Select Brandin Echols in Sixth Round of NFL Draft|date=May 1, 2021|website=Northwest Mississippi Community College Athletics}}</ref>

Echols was ranked as a three{{endash}}star recruit by [[247Sports.com]] coming out of [[Community colleges in the United States|junior college]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Brandin-Echols-46052708/junior-college-213297/|title=Brandin Echols Recruiting Profile|website=247Sports.com}}</ref> He committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky]] on September 23, 2018,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/brandin-echols-46052708/|title=Brandin Echols 247|website=247Sports.com}}</ref> playing for Kentucky in 2019 and 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/roster/brandin-echols/|title=Brandin Echols|date=December 18, 2018}}</ref> In the [[2021 Gator Bowl (January)|2021 Gator Bowl]], Echols recorded his first interception for Kentucky.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wymt.com/2021/05/01/brandin-echols-selected-by-new-york-jets-in-sixth-round-of-nfl-draft/|title=Brandin Echols Selected by New York Jets in Sixth Round of NFL Draft|first=Camille|last=Gear|date=May 1, 2021|website=www.wymt.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Echols was drafted by the [[New York Jets]] with the 200th pick in the sixth round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Grab Third Cornerback on Day 3, Select Brandin Echols|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/brandon-echols-nfl-draft-cornerback-kentucky|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=May 1, 2021}}</ref> On May 7, 2021, Echols officially signed with the Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=May 7, 2021 |title=NFL Draft Pick Signings: 5/7/21 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/05/nfl-draft-pick-signings-5721#ref=home |access-date=March 3, 2025 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

Echols was named a starting cornerback to begin his rookie season in 2021. He started the first nine games before suffering a thigh injury in Week 10. On November 16, 2021, he was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign TE Kenny Yeboah, CB Rachad Wildgoose to Active Roster|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-te-kenny-yeboah-cb-rachad-wildgoose-to-active-roster|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=November 16, 2021}}</ref> He was activated on December 11.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place WR Elijah Moore on IR, Activate CB Brandin Echols Off IR|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-wr-elijah-moore-on-ir-activate-cb-brandin-echols-off-ir|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 11, 2021}}</ref>

In 2022, Echols played in 13 games for the Jets, tallying 8 total tackles. His season ended after he was placed on injured reserve on January 7, 2023.<ref name="x712">{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Jets put Duane Brown and Lamarcus Joyner on IR; don't call up Chris Streveler | website=NBC Sports | date=January 7, 2023 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/jets-put-duane-brown-and-lamarcus-joyner-on-ir-dont-call-up-chris-streveler | access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

On May 25, 2023, Echols was suspended one game by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The suspension stemmed from a 2022 high-speed car crash Echols was involved in.<ref name="f570">{{cite web | last=Crane | first=Andrew | title=Jets’ Brandin Echols’ one-game suspension may stem from 2022 crash | website=New York Post | date=May 25, 2023 | url=https://nypost.com/2023/05/25/jets-brandin-echols-suspended-one-game-for-mystery-reason/ | access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On March 13, 2025, Echols signed a two-year contract with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/echols-signed-to-two-year-contract|title= Echols signed to two-year contract |work=Pittsburgh Steelers|date=March 13, 2025|first=Teresa|last=Varley}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On April 22, 2022, Echols was involved in a two-car crash in [[Florham Park, New Jersey]] that resulted in the partial paralyzation of the other driver. Echols had been traveling 84 mph in a 50 mph zone before making contact with the other vehicle.<ref name="i890">{{cite web | last=Comstock | first=Lori | title=NY Jets football player charged in NJ crash enrolls in PTI program | website=Daily Record | date=March 10, 2023 | url=https://www.dailyrecord.com/story/news/crime/2023/03/10/ny-jets-football-player-charged-in-nj-crash-enrolls-in-pti-program/69989414007/ | access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> In January 2023, Echols was charged with fourth-degree assault by auto, and was summoned for [[reckless driving]], speeding, failure to wear a seat belt, an unsafe lane change, and improper passing.<ref name="q456">{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=NFL suspends Jets CB Brandin Echols for one game | website=NBC Sports | date=May 25, 2023 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/nfl-suspends-jets-cb-brandin-echols-for-one-game | access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> On March 10, he was accepted into a [[diversion program|diversionary program]] to avoid the charges.<ref name="b191">{{cite web | last=Riccette | first=Billy | title=Jets CB Brandin Echols suspended one game by league | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=May 25, 2023 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/jets-cb-brandin-echols-suspended-221759526.html | access-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

'''Bradley Dee White''' (August 18, 1958 – July 16, 2022) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] for six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], and [[Minnesota Vikings]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]].

==Early life and education==
White was born on August 18, 1958, in [[Rexburg, Idaho]].<ref name="auto9">{{Cite web |title=Brad White Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WhitBr20.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |language=en}}</ref> He was the oldest of four children.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=dany |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Bradley Dee White: August 18 1958 – July 16 2022 (age 63), death notice, USA |url=https://usobit.com/obituaries-2022/bradley-dee-white-august-18-1958-july-16-2022-age-63/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220729193611/https://usobit.com/obituaries-2022/bradley-dee-white-august-18-1958-july-16-2022-age-63/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=July 29, 2022 |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=United States Obituary Notice |language=english}}</ref> Growing up, White worked on the family [[potato farm]] in [[Idaho Falls, Idaho|Idaho Falls]].<ref name="auto" /><ref name="auto12">{{Cite news |last=Selman |first=Jim |date=August 5, 1981 |title=White Won't Drop Bucs' Hot Potato |page=31, [https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106638417/the-tampa-tribune/ 36] |work=[[The Tampa Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106638282/the-tampa-tribune/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> He started playing [[American football|football]] while in fourth grade and was coached by his father for several years.<ref name="auto" /> He attended [[Skyline High School (Idaho)|Skyline High School]] in Idaho Falls, where he was a top football player and state champion [[Scholastic wrestling|wrestler]].<ref name="auto" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Brad White Stats and Bio |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerw/whit03000.html |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=Pro Football Archives}}</ref> White earned all-state honors in both sports and also was the state champion in [[discus throw]] and [[shotput]].<ref name="auto" /> ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' later named him one of the "Top 50 Greatest Sports Figures from Idaho".<ref name="auto" /> He is an inductee into the Idaho High School Football Hall of Fame.<ref name="auto" />

White committed to the [[University of Tennessee]], arriving on August 16, 1976, after driving 2,800 miles.<ref name="auto8">{{Cite news |last=Riggs |first=Ted |date=October 17, 1978 |title=Brad White's a Full-Fledged Vol After 2 Years |page=19 |work=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106614484/the-knoxville-news-sentinel/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Football practice started on August 18, which was his 18th birthday.<ref name="auto8" /> Things "almost immediately headed downhill," and he became "an athlete in waiting," seeing no varsity action in his first two years.<ref name="auto8" /> White, suffering from depression and homesickness, nearly quit the team and headed home.<ref name="auto8" />

In 1976, White appeared in two games on the [[junior varsity]] football team, against [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky]] and [[Lees–McRae College#Athletics|Lees–McRae]].<ref name="auto8" /> He redshirted for the 1977 season.<ref name="auto8" /> In 1978, he made the varsity team and became one of their top defensive performers, posting 45 tackles in the first four games.<ref name="auto8" /> He made his varsity debut on September 16 against the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]], starting before an attendance of over 82,500.<ref name="auto8" /> "In 1976 and 1977, I played before about 2,500 people. The largest single audience for a JV game was, I guess, 1,500. You can imagine how it felt when I started against UCLA, my first varsity appearance, before more than 82,500," he said.<ref name="auto8" />

In the 1979 season, White led Tennessee in "big plays" ([[Quarterback sacks|sacks]], {{abbr|TFLs|tackles-for-loss}}, [[fumble]] recoveries, forced fumbles) and made a team-leading seven sacks.<ref name="auto11">{{Cite news |last=Bailes |first=Frank |date=November 27, 1980 |title=What's Cooking? Vol Brad White Knows |page=52 |work=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106617379/the-knoxville-news-sentinel/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> In the 1980 season, White's [[Senior (education)|senior]] year, he tied for first on the team in "big plays", having recorded five sacks, five tackles-for-loss and two forced fumbles.<ref name="auto12"/>

After his senior year, White was selected to play in the 1981 [[Japan Bowl]] and the [[East–West Shrine Bowl]].<ref name="auto" /> White finished his college career with 19 sacks, 245 tackles, 24 tackles-for-loss, four forced fumbles and two fumbles recovered in three seasons at the varsity level.<ref name="auto" />

==Professional career==
White was selected in the 12th round (310th overall) of the [[1981 NFL draft]] by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1981 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1981/draft.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Selman |first=Jim |date=April 30, 1981 |title=Offensive Tackle, Quarterback Top Bucs' Late Picks |pages=19, 6C |work=[[The Tampa Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106638006/the-tampa-tribune/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Despite being a 12th round pick, he impressed in training camp and made the final roster as backup [[nose tackle]], becoming one of only six rookies to make the team.<ref name="auto12"/><ref name="auto10">{{Cite news |last=Ahillen |first=Steve |date=September 20, 1981 |title=Brad White Doing All Right in Tampa |page=63 |work=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106638575/the-knoxville-news-sentinel/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name="auto5">{{Cite news |last=Wood |first=Tom |date=December 10, 1981 |title=Ex-Vol Lineman Brad White Paying Dues At Tampa Bay With Super Bowl Thoughts |page=95 |work=[[The Tennessean]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106639298/the-tennessean/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> At first, they had him play exclusively on the [[special teams]].<ref name="auto10" /> Against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on October 25, White blocked a 54-yard [[field goal]], which was the first time this was accomplished in team history.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Selman |first=Jim |date=October 26, 1981 |title=Bucs Play Giveaway |page=45, [https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106639086/the-tampa-tribune/ 50] |work=[[The Tampa Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106639008/the-tampa-tribune/ |quote=And the Bucs even foiled a 54-yard field goal by [[Tony Franklin (kicker)|Franklin]] in the third quarter when it was 7–7. Leaper Brad White got a hand on the ball. The Bucs have had only one outright blocked kick in their history. |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> "On field goal attempts, I'm what they call the 'jumper,' the guy who's supposed to block the kick," White said.<ref name="auto5" /> The Buccaneers eventually made the playoffs, but lost 0–38 to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the Divisional Round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1981 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/tam/1981.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys – January 2nd, 1982 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/198201020dal.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> White played every regular season game in the season and also appeared in their one playoff game, recording 22 tackles on the year.<ref name="auto9"/><ref name="auto6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bucpower.com/brad-white.html|website=bucpower.com|title=Brad White}}</ref>

In a strike-shortened [[1982 NFL season|1982 season]], White played in all nine regular season games and made three tackles.<ref name="auto6"/><ref name="auto7">{{Cite web |title=1982 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/tam/1982.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He helped the Buccaneers compile a 5–4 record and make it to the playoffs, where they lost to the Dallas Cowboys for the second consecutive year.<ref name="auto7" /> In the following season, White appeared in all 16 games, but did not start any, as Tampa Bay finished 2–14.<ref name="auto6"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=1983 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/tam/1983.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He recorded a total of 20 tackles on the season.<ref name="auto6"/>

Despite impressing in the {{NFL Year|1984}} preseason, and coach [[John McKay (American football)|John McKay]] declaring White to be the team's best backup nose tackle and [[defensive end]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Selman |first=Jim |date=August 7, 1984 |title=Clouds of concern shift over Bucs |page=113 |work=[[The Tampa Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106643131/the-tampa-tribune/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> White was released at the final roster cuts in August.<ref name="auto4">{{Cite news |last=Selman |first=Jim |date=August 28, 1984 |title=Capece waived by Bucs |page=100 |work=[[The Tampa Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106642808/the-tampa-tribune/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> His release was described as "the biggest surprise of all" by ''[[The Tampa Tribune]]''.<ref name="auto4" /> McKay said that the play of new signings [[Brison Manor]] and [[Byron Braggs]] contributed to his release.<ref name="auto4" /> "It came as a complete surprise," White said.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite news |last=Gates |first=Nick |date=August 18, 1985 |title=New life |page=33 |work=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106644022/the-knoxville-news-sentinel/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

On August 31, White was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106643211/the-des-moines-register/|newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 1, 1984|page=19|title=Colts sign Brad White}} {{Open access}}</ref> He played as second-string nose tackle for most of the season, behind [[Leo Wisniewski]].<ref name="auto3" /> White mostly appeared on special teams, but became a starter for the final two games of the year after Wisniewski was injured.<ref name="auto3" /> They were the first two starts of his career.<ref name="auto9"/> White finished the season with 15 games played, two as a starter, and 39 tackles, including 13 solo stops.<ref name="auto3" /> He also made two sacks for a loss of 16 yards and pressured the quarterback into throwing the ball away nine times, which was fourth-highest on the team.<ref name="auto3" />

After Wisniewski announced his plans to sit out the [[1985 NFL season|1985 season]], White was named the Colts' starting nose tackle.<ref name="auto3" /> White had his best year as a professional in 1985, starting 15 out of 16 games and making 97 tackles, leading the team's defensive line as the Colts finished 5–11.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news |last=Rietmann |first=Tom |date=August 11, 1986 |title=Colts cut four as team prepares for Bears |page=13 |work=[[The Indianapolis Colts]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106644654/the-indianapolis-news/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1985 Indianapolis Colts Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/clt/1985.htm |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He also made one sack.<ref name="auto9"/> White was released in August {{NFL Year|1986}} after losing a training camp battle to [[Willie Broughton]].<ref name="auto2" />

In {{NFL Year|1987}}, White was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as a [[replacement player]] during the [[1987 NFL strike|NFLPA strike]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sansevere |first=Robert |date=October 9, 1987 |title=Mularkey rejoins striking Vikings after misunderstanding |page=79 |work=[[Star Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106644976/star-tribune/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> He appeared in one game, starting in a 7–27 loss to the [[Chicago Bears]] before being released.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WhitBr20/gamelog/1987/|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Brad White 1987 Game Log}}</ref> It was the final game of his NFL career.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |last=Calhoun |first=Caleb |date=June 23, 2020 |title=Tennessee football's 10 DTs with best NFL careers |url=https://allfortennessee.com/2020/06/23/tennessee-football-defensive-tackles-nfl/3/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=All for Tennessee|publisher=FanSided |language=en-US}}</ref>

White played six NFL seasons and finished his career with 73 games played, 18 as a starter, and three sacks.<ref name="auto1" /> He also unofficially made at least 181 tackles.<ref name="auto6"/><ref name="auto3" /><ref name="auto2" />

==Later life and death==
White later worked for ''Anderson Press'' and TNT Fireworks.<ref name="auto"/> He resided the last 31 years of his life in [[Florence, Alabama]].<ref name="auto"/> With his wife, Cathy, White had two children.<ref name="auto"/>

White died on July 16, 2022, at the age of 63.<ref name="auto"/>

'''Bralen Trice''' (born February 26, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]]. The Falcons drafted him in round 3 of the 2024 NFL draft at the 74th pick.

==Early life==
Trice attended [[Sandra Day O'Connor High School (Arizona)|Sandra Day O'Connor High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nemec |first=Andrew |date=September 12, 2018 |title=Oregon Ducks DE/OLB target sets decision date |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2018/09/bralen_trice_3-star_deolb_has.html |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=OregonLive.com |language=en}}</ref> During his high school career he had 16.5 sacks. He committed to the [[University of Washington]] to play college football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |date=October 6, 2018 |title=O'Connor DE Bralen Trice commits to Washington Huskies |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/10/06/sdos-trice-gives-washington-commitment-play-football/1549671002/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jude |first=Adam |date=October 6, 2018 |title=Huskies get commitment from 3-star defensive end Bralen Trice |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-football/huskies-get-commitment-from-3-star-defensive-end-bralen-trice/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Trice redshirted his first year at Washington in 2019 and opted out of the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kirschman |first=Lauren |date=May 1, 2021 |title=UW linebacker Bralen Trice caps impressive practice month with strong spring game |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/college/university-of-washington/article250984069.html |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=The News Tribune}}</ref> He returned in 2021 to play in all 12 games and made two starts. He finished the year with 14 tackles, two sacks and a [[touchdown]] via a fumble return.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vorel |first=Mike |date=May 4, 2022 |title=UW fans already know about ‘ZTF,’ but is Bralen Trice the hardest Husky to block? |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/may/04/uw-fans-already-know-about-ztf-but-is-bralen-trice/ |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=The Spokesman-Review}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Raley |first=Dan |date=May 27, 2022 |title=When Bralen Trice Got His Big Chance, He didn't Fumble It |url=https://www.si.com/college/washington/football/when-bralen-trice-got-his-big-chance-he-didnt-fumble-it |access-date=June 8, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> Trice was named the defensive MVP of the [[2022 Alamo Bowl]].<ref>{{cite tweet |user=LarsHanson |number=1608707008131403778 |title=Bralen Trice named 2022 Alamo Bowl defensive MVP |date=December 30, 2022 |accessdate=December 30, 2022}}</ref>

'''Braeden Edward Daniels''' ({{respell|BRAY|dən}}; born August 22, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] and was selected by the [[Washington Commanders]] in the fourth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Daniels was born on August 22, 2000, in [[Carrollton, Texas]].<ref name="TheBeast">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2023 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410190932/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 10, 2023 |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 10, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=175 }}</ref> He attended [[Hebron High School (Texas)|Hebron High School]], where he played football, [[javelin throw]], [[discus throw]], and [[shot put]], earning all-district honors for the latter.<ref name="TheBeast"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/4/25/23694422/braeden-daniels-2023-nfl-draft|title=Who is NFL draft prospect Braeden Daniels?|first=Joe|last=Coles|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=April 25, 2023}}</ref> Rated a three-star recruit, Daniels initially committed to play [[college football]] at [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]] before switching his commitment to [[Utah Utes football|Utah]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Worthy |first=Lynn |date=January 14, 2018 |title=Three recruits from Texas commit to Utes football program on the same day |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2018/01/14/three-recruits-from-texas-commit-to-utes-football-program-on-the-same-day/ |access-date=April 25, 2023 |website=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Daniels played in two games during his true freshman season at Utah before redshirting the year. He became the Utes' starting left guard going into his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kragthorpe |first=Kurt |date=August 2, 2019 |title=Retooling Utah's offensive line is a big issue, but Jim Harding will 'get it done,' Kyle Whittingham says |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2019/08/02/retooling-utahs-offensive/ |access-date=April 25, 2023 |website=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]}}</ref> He moved to right tackle two games into his redshirt junior season and was named second team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Call |first=Jeff |date=December 7, 2021 |title=Utah football: Which Utes collected Pac-12 accolades? |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2021/12/7/22822829/utah-football-who-earned-all-pac-12-honors-kyle-whittingham-devin-lloyd-cam-rising-junior-tafuna |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=[[Deseret News]]}}</ref> Daniels was named first team All-Pac-12 as a redshirt senior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/nfl-scouting-combine-utah-ol-braeden-daniels-trying-for-a-high-4s-40-he-says|title=NFL Scouting Combine: Utah OL Braeden Daniels trying for a "high 4’s" 40 he says|first=Bo|last=Marchiote|website=[[SI.com]]|date=February 25, 2023|access-date=April 26, 2023}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===

On August 27, 2024, Daniels was waived by the Commanders as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Selby |first1=Zach |title=Commanders release 34 players; place 3 on IR, 1 on PUP list |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-release-34-players-place-3-on-ir-1-on-pup-list |website=Commanders.com |access-date=28 August 2024}}</ref>

On August 29, 2024, Daniels signed with the [[practice squad]] of the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-08-29-2024|work=HoustonTexans.com|title=Houston Texans Transactions (08-29-2024)|date=August 29, 2024|accessdate=August 29, 2024}}</ref> He was released on September 17.<ref>{{cite web |title=Houston Texans Transactions (09-17-2024) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-09-17-2024 |website=houstontexans.com |access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On September 26, 2024, Daniels was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]' practice squad and released five days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Tony Jefferson to Active Roster|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-tony-jefferson-to-active-roster-2024|website=Chargers.com|date=September 26, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Sandoval |first1=Ricardo |title=Chargers Officially Release Safety to Make Room for Derwin James |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/chargers/los-angeles-chargers-latest-news/chargers-officially-release-safety-to-make-room-for-derwin-james |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=2 October 2024}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On December 12, 2024, Daniels signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Updates: Zack Martin has surgery, OL signed |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/updates-december-2024 |website=dallascowboys.com |access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On January 1, 2025, Daniels was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] off the Cowboys' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-1-1-25|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=January 1, 2025}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Daniels was waived by the Dolphins as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-08272025-2 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=29 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-08262025 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref> He was released on December 2.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins make practice squad roster moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-practice-squad-roster-moves-x6738 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=3 December 2025}}</ref> 

On January 9, 2026, Daniels signed a reserve/futures contract with the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dolphins sign four players to futures contracts |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-four-players-to-futures-contracts |website=MiamiDolphins.com |access-date=10 January 2026}}</ref> On May 21, he was waived by Miami.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dolphins make roster moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-x3726 |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Brady Russell''' (born August 31, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado Buffaloes]] and was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in {{NFL Year|2023}}.

==Early life==
Russell was born on August 31, 1998, at [[Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton|Camp Pendleton]] in [[California]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://cubuffs.com/sports/football/roster/brady-russell/15825|publisher=[[Colorado Buffaloes]]|title=Brady Russell}}</ref> Several of his family members were also involved in athletics: his father, Randy, and uncle, Marc Booth, both played [[American football|football]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]]; his uncle, [[Matt Russell|Matt]], played for the [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado Buffaloes]] and is an executive with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]; his brother, Cody, played for the [[Northern Colorado Bears football|Northern Colorado Bears]] and another brother, Tyler, ran [[Track and field|track]] at [[Navy Midshipmen|Navy]].<ref name="auto1"/>

Russell attended [[Fossil Ridge High School (Colorado)|Fossil Ridge High School]] in [[Fort Collins, Colorado]], initially being a track athlete before switching to football and playing [[defensive end]] as well as some [[tight end]].<ref name="auto4">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/bradyrussell|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NFL Draft Profile: Brady Russell, Tight End, Colorado Buffaloes|date=November 16, 2022}}</ref> He was the team's [[most valuable player]] as both a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] and [[Senior (education)|senior]], twice earning first-team All-Front Range League honors on defense, as well as one second-team selection on offense.<ref name="auto1"/> He was a two-star recruit and opted to [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] at [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|Football Bowl Subdivision]] Colorado rather than accept a [[Athletic scholarship|scholarship]] offer from [[NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision|Football Championship Subdivision]] Northern Colorado.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/football/tcu-vs-colorado-players-to-watch|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=TCU Football vs Colorado: Opponent's Players to Watch|author=Cross, Nathan|date=September 1, 2022}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-collins-coloradoan/126092951/|newspaper=[[Fort Collins Coloradoan]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 30, 2018|page=D1, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-collins-coloradoan/126093215/ D4]|author=Lytle, Kevin|title=Russell's Gamble Pays Off}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true [[freshman]] at Colorado in 2017, Russell spent time learning how to play [[outside linebacker]] and tight end, quickly being made the latter while spending the season on the [[scout team]].<ref name="auto"/> He was named Colorado's 2017 Offensive Scout Player of the Year.<ref name="auto"/> He impressed in [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]] in 2018 and was given a scholarship prior to the regular season, despite it taking most walk-ons at minimum three years to earn it, if ever.<ref name="auto"/> Russell was placed second on the depth chart to begin the 2018 season.<ref name="auto"/> He totaled five [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 41 yards on the year.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.buffzone.com/2019/12/25/brady-russell-becoming-reliable-weapon-for-colorado-buffaloes-football/|website=BuffZone.com|title=Brady Russell becoming reliable weapon for CU Buffs|author=Howell, Brian|date=December 25, 2019}}</ref>

In 2019, Russell made 23 catches for 221 yards with two [[touchdown]]s, exceeding the amount of catches made by Colorado tight ends in the prior three years (18).<ref name="auto3"/> The following year, he was named team [[Captain (sports)|captain]], but suffered an injury in the second game that sidelined him for the season.<ref name="auto4"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.greeleytribune.com/2021/08/07/brady-russell-playing-key-role-for-cu-buffs/|newspaper=[[Greeley Tribune]]|title=Brady Russell playing key role for CU Buffs |date=August 7, 2021|author=Howell, Brian|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He had his best season in 2021, recording a team-leading 25 receptions for 307 yards while being a nominee for the [[Burlsworth Trophy]], given to the best player who started his career as a walk-on.<ref name="auto4"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/colorado/Article/Colorado-football-Buffaloes-tight-end-Brady-Russell-ready-to-roll-under-new-offensive-scheme-191092626/|website=[[247Sports]]|title=Veteran Colorado tight end Brady Russell ready to roll under new offensive scheme|date=August 7, 2022|author=Searfoss, Jimmy}}</ref> Russell returned for a final year in 2022 and posted 20 catches for 153 ===Philadelphia Eagles===
After going unselected in the [[2023 NFL draft]], Russell was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref name="auto2"/> He was waived on August 29, 2023 and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-2023|author1=Spadaro, Dave|author2=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles announce practice squad|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-practice-squad-2023|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
Russell was signed off the Eagles' practice squad to the 53-man roster of the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on September 20, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-te-brady-russell|author=Boyle, John|date=September 20, 2023|title=Seahawks Sign TE Brady Russell |publisher=[[Seattle Seahawks]]}}</ref> He played in 15 games for Seattle, logging 7 tackles while playing 2% of the team's offensive snaps. Russell made 11 appearances for the Seahawks in 2024, playing mostly on special teams. On January 2, 2025, Russell was placed on injured reserve with a foot injury, ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levine |first=Ben |date=January 2, 2025 |title=Minor NFL Transactions: 1/2/25 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2025/01/minor-nfl-transactions-1-2-25 |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

On April 9, 2025, Russell signed his exclusive rights free agent contract with the Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boyle |first1=John |date=April 9, 2025 |title=Seahawks Sign Exclusive Rights Free Agent Brady Russell |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-exclusive-rights-free-agent-brady-russell |access-date=10 April 2025 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> During the 2025 off-season, Russell changed positions from tight end to fullback under new offensive coordinator [[Klint Kubiak]], who planned to use the position in a greater capacity than previous offensive coordinator [[Ryan Grubb]], who did not employ an official  fullback during his time with the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Van Til |first=Cameron |date=April 23, 2025 |title=Switching positions: Seattle Seahawks TE moving to fullback |url=https://sports.mynorthwest.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/seattle-seahawks-brady-russell-move-tight-end-fullback/1808195 |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Seattle Sports |language=en}}</ref>  Russell made the Seahawks' 53-man roster as the Seahawks' backup fullback behind [[Robbie Ouzts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 26, 2025 |title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves, Establish Initial 2025 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-make-roster-moves-establish-initial-2025-53-man-roster |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Seahawks.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Russell played in Super Bowl LX, a 29–13 victory over the New England Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Strella |first=Charlie |date=February 9, 2026 |title=Former Colorado tight end wins Super Bowl LX with Seattle Seahawks |url=https://coloradobuffaloeswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/buffaloes/football/2026/02/09/brady-russell-super-bowl-lx-seahawks-colorado-football/88590607007/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Buffaloes Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

On March 12, 2026, Russell re-signed with the team on a two-year, $4.8 million contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/seahawks-free-agency-signings-russell-707567d79c5d69e2565cbfeb6cade34c|work=APNews.com|title=Seahawks agree to a 2-year contract with fullback and special teams captain Brady Russell|first=Andrew|last=Destin|date=March 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/2026-free-agency-seahawks-re-sign-fb-special-teams-standout-brady-russell|title=Seahawks Re-Sign FB & Special Teams Standout Brady Russell|date=March 12, 2026|first=John|last=Boyle|work=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], winning three consecutive [[Big Ten Football Championship Game#Results|Big Ten Conference titles]] and a [[2024 College Football Playoff National Championship|national championship]] in 2023. ==Early life== McGregor was born on July 12, 2001, in Port Huron, Michigan.{{citation needed|date=April 2024}} He attended [[Port Huron Northern High School]], and was a three-time All-State and All-Conference selection as a football player.{{cite web|title=Braiden McGregor|publisher=University of Michigan|accessdate=September 10, 2023|url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/roster/braiden-mcgregor/24384}} As a junior, McGregror recorded 99 tackles, 13 tackles for loss, eight sacks, two forced fumbles and two interceptions. As a senior, he played in the first seven games of the season before injuring his knee and missing the remainder of the season. He registered 32 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and two sacks. He set a school record with 227 career tackles. McGregor was ranked as the #1 high school football player in the state of Michigan in [[2020 college football recruiting class|2020]], and rated as the #32 overall ranked player in the country in ESPN’s Top 300.{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/playerrankings/_/view/rn300/sort/rank/class/2020|title=Recruiting Database: 2020 ESPN 300|website=ESPN}} He received scholarship offers from 36 schools, including [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]], and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]].{{cite news|title=Port Huron Northern's Braiden McGregor commits to Michigan football|author=Joseph Hayes|newspaper=Port Huron Times Herald|date=May 24, 2019|access-date=September 10, 2023|url=https://www.thetimesherald.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/05/24/mcgregor-headed-university-michigan/1230650001/}}{{cite news|title=Michigan football got 4-star DE Braiden McGregor, but how good can he be?|author=Steven Lorenz|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=May 29, 2019|access-date=September 10, 2023|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2019/05/28/michigan-football-recruiting-braiden-mcgregor/1257645001/}} On May 24, 2019, McGregor committed to the [[University of Michigan]].{{cite news|title=For Braiden McGregor, four-star DE, 'It was always Michigan'|author=Matt Schoch|newspaper=The Detroit News|date=May 24, 2019|access-date=September 10, 2023|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2019/05/24/its-michigan-for-braiden-mcgregor-four-star-de-port-huron-northern/1219172001/}} ==College career== [[File:Braiden McGregor.jpg |thumb|right|McGregor with Michigan following the 2023 season opening game]] McGregor enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] in 2020. After tearing his MCL, PCL, and meniscus in his right knee during his senior year in high school, McGregor did not play while rehabilitating the knee during his freshman year.{{cite news|title=A Fully Healthy Braiden McGregor Is Ready To Shine In 2023|publisher=SI.com|date=August 14, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023|author=Trent Knoop|url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/football/michigan-football-braiden-mcgregor-ready-to-shine-in-2023}}{{cite news|title=Michigan's Braiden McGregor Primed For Breakout Season|publisher=SI.com|author=Christopher Breiler|date=July 11, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023|url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/football/michigan-wolverines-football-braiden-mcgregor-jim-harbaugh-big-ten-national-championship-college-playoff}} In 2021, as a sophomore, he appeared in nine games as a backup defensive end and special teams member and recorded five tackles. As a junior in 2022, he appeared in all 14 games and started three games.{{cite news|title=Michigan DE Braiden McGregor has new role, ambitious goal for 2022|newspaper=[[Mlive.com]]|author=Aaron McMann|date=May 15, 2022|access-date=September 10, 2023|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2022/05/michigan-de-braiden-mcgregor-has-new-role-ambitious-goal-for-2021.html}}{{cite news|title=Former PHN star Braiden McGregor relishes increased role as Michigan football chases national title|author=Brenden Welper|newspaper=Port Huron Times Herald|date=December 22, 2022|access-date=September 10, 2023|url=https://www.thetimesherald.com/story/sports/2022/12/22/former-port-huron-northern-braiden-mcgregor-michigan-football/69723028007/}} On September 17, 2022, McGregor started in his first game against [[UConn Huskies football|UConn]]. McGregor totaled 17 tackles, five tackles for a loss and 2.5 sacks. '''Braden Fiske''' (born January 18, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Western Michigan Broncos football|Western Michigan Broncos]] and [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]].

==Early life ==
Braden Fiske was born on January 18, 2000, and grew up in [[Michigan City, Indiana]].

== College career ==
Fiske attended [[Michigan City High School]] in [[Michigan City, Indiana]]. He committed to [[Western Michigan University]] to play college football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waddle |first=Brian |date=2022-01-05 |title=Quite a ride for Western Michigan's Braden Fiske |url=https://www.nwitimes.com/sports/football/college/quite-a-ride-for-western-michigans-braden-fiske/article_19482b7a-395d-5d04-b10c-22d25d781b43.html |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=NWI Times |language=en}}</ref>

Fiske played at Western Michigan from 2019 to 2022. While there he started 30 of 45 games and had 148 tackles and 13.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nothaft |first=Patrick |date=2022-12-27 |title=WMU football loses 6th offseason transfer to Power 5 team |url=https://www.mlive.com/broncos/2022/12/wmu-football-loses-6th-offseason-transfer-to-power-5-team.html |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=mlive.com |language=en}}</ref> As a junior, Fiske was named second team All-MAC after making 58 tackles (12 for loss) with 6.0 sacks, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. After the 2022 season, he entered the transfer portal and transferred to [[Florida State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kassim |first=Ehsan |date=December 26, 2022 |title=Florida State football: Western Michigan DL transfer Braden Fiske commits to Seminoles |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/football/2022/12/26/fsu-football-dl-transferbraden-fiskecommits-to-seminoles/69757246007/ |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=Tallahassee Democrat |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Jim |date=2022-12-27 |title=Fiske to Florida State: Michigan City alum, Western Michigan graduate transfer to play final college football season with Seminoles |url=https://www.lpheralddispatch.com/sports/fiske-to-florida-state-michigan-city-alum-western-michigan-graduate-transfer-to-play-final-college/article_737f0e94-b5b8-54ef-9047-c3a9f4e9ee05.html |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=LPHeraldDispatch.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Murschel |first=Matt |date=2023-02-01 |title=FSU bolsters 2023 recruiting class with another solid group of transfers |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2023/02/01/fsu-bolsters-2023-recruiting-class-with-another-solid-group-of-transfers/ |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref> Fiske earned third team AP All-American and second team All-ACC honors as a senior, recording 43 tackles, including 9.0 for loss with 6.0 sacks, and five quarterback hurries for the Seminoles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Jim |date=2022-12-27 |title=2023 Team Roster - Braden Fiske |url=https://seminoles.com/sports/football/roster/braden-fiske/5438 |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=Seminoles.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Bradyn Swinson''' (born July 4, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]] and [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon Ducks]]. Swinson was selected by the Patriots in the fifth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Swinson attended [[Chapel Hill High School (Douglasville, Georgia)|Chapel Hill High School]] in [[Douglasville, Georgia]]. He was rated as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon Ducks]] over Arizona State, Florida State, Missouri and North Carolina.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nemec |first1=Andrew |title=Bradyn Swinson, Georgia 3-star DE, commits to Oregon Ducks over Florida State, Arizona State, others |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2019/09/bradyn-swinson-georgia-3-star-de-commits-to-oregon-ducks-over-florida-state-arizona-state-others.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=21 September 2019 |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
=== Oregon ===
As a freshman in 2020 Swinson played in seven games where he made three tackles.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Rustik |first1=John |title=Bradyn Swinson Recounts Recovery From Injury |url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/football/swinson-opens-up-on-injury-vs-ohio-state |work=Oregon Ducks on SI |publisher=SI.com |date=21 October 2021 |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref> In 2021, he notched 24 tackles with four being for a loss, three sacks, and two pass deflections.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crepea |first1=James |title=Did Georgia overlook Bradyn Swinson? 'Yes,' says the Oregon Ducks edge rusher, who wants his homecoming to be a memorable performance |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/09/did-georgia-overlook-bradyn-swinson-yes-says-the-oregon-ducks-edge-rusher-who-wants-his-homecoming-to-be-a-memorable-performance.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=2 September 2022 |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref> During week 2 of the 2021 season, Swinson made the start against [[2021 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State]] and had five tackles, a sack, and a pass deflection in the upset win, earning [[Pac-12 Conference]] defensive lineman of the week honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crepea |first1=James |title=Oregon Ducks edge rusher Bradyn Swinson doubtful to play against Arizona |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2021/09/oregon-ducks-edge-rusher-bradyn-swinson-doubtful-to-play-against-arizona.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=20 September 2021 |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he totaled eight tackles, with one and a half being for a loss.<ref name="portal">{{cite web |last1=Crepea |first1=James |title=Oregon Ducks edge rusher Bradyn Swinson to enter transfer portal, per source |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/12/oregon-ducks-edge-rusher-bradyn-swinson-to-enter-transfer-portal-per-source.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=December 2022 |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref> After the season, Swinson entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref name=portal/>

=== LSU ===
Swinson transferred to play for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crepea |first1=James |title=Former Oregon Ducks edge rusher Bradyn Swinson commits to transfer to LSU |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/12/former-oregon-ducks-edge-rusher-bradyn-swinson-commits-to-transfer-to-lsu.html |website=OregonLive.com |date=21 December 2022 |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref> In his first season with LSU he notched 35 tackles with six and a half being for a loss, two sacks, five pass deflections, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bradyn Swinson 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bradyn-swinson-1.html/gamelog/2023/ |website=Sports Reference |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref>
